Random conformation changes can be used to sample a distribution. The 1953 work of Metropolis, both Rosenbluths and both Tellers provided a classic method for sampling interacting systems according to equilibrium weights. In a fixed-length chain ensemble, every sample retains the same segment count. Allowing length to change requires a separately defined statistical model. Local rotations or exchanges must produce the correct weights and connect the relevant state regions. Satisfying an acceptance-probability rule alone does not ensure that the available moves can reach every necessary conformation. Connectivity of the sampling process and its equilibrium weighting are related but distinct requirements.

Lattice self-avoiding chains make the distinction concrete. If each step always attempts one of four directions equally and any collision restarts the whole chain, successful fixed-length direction sequences have equal original weights. Choosing instead only among currently available directions gives history-dependent branching counts and can introduce growth bias requiring correction. In either method, a sampling step is not normally one second of molecular motion. It is first a way to explore a probability distribution. Only physically calibrated kinetic rules justify interpreting the sequence as real-time evolution, an important distinction when comparing an equilibrium conformation calculation with a measured relaxation curve.

## The microcanonical ensemble for an isolated system

If a system exchanges neither energy nor particles with its surroundings and has a fixed container with time-independent interactions, total energy can serve as a constraint. A statistical description then concentrates on accessible states near that energy, defining a microcanonical ensemble. Measurements have finite energy resolution, so it is useful to consider a thin energy shell rather than count a single exact continuous energy value as though it were a discrete state. The shell should be narrow enough to preserve the macroscopic conditions of interest while containing the microscopic states needed for the chosen statistical description.

Microcanonical weights in an energy shellEq. 6

![Microcanonical weights in an energy shell](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/39d8ba9466cd8137ed479307.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pi | Probability of microstate i within the energy shell | 1 |
| Ω(E,ΔE) | Equal-weight state count in the defined energy shell | 1 |
| E | Lower energy boundary of the shell | J |
| ΔE | Positive shell energy width | J |
| S | Microcanonical entropy | J K⁻¹ |
| kB | Boltzmann constant, 1.380649×10⁻²³ | J K⁻¹ |
| ln | Natural logarithm | 1 |

Reading the relationshipCount and normalize equally weighted states within the prescribed energy shell; their logarithmic count gives entropy.

A worked exampleFor eight equally weighted discrete states, each probability is 1/8 and S=kB ln8≈2.871×10⁻²³ J K⁻¹.

ConditionsIsolated equilibrium at fixed volume and particle number. Applies inside E≤Ei<E+ΔE, with zero probability outside; continuum systems need consistent phase measure and state counting.

Equal weighting applies to allowed microstates defined with a consistent phase-space measure. It does not imply uniformity in every projected coordinate. An oscillator moves slowly near its turning points and spends more time there, making its position distribution nonuniform. Geometry and speed connect the energy curve to its projection onto the position axis. Reading equal energy-state weighting as equal probability for all positions would lose that connection. An energy shell or the corresponding induced energy-surface measure preserves the relationship between counting and dynamics. Even a simple oscillator therefore illustrates why the measure used to define a probability matters.

Macroscopic thermodynamic quantities can be obtained from the constrained state set. As energy, volume or particle number changes, the number of accessible states changes and so does entropy. Energy allocation between systems brought into contact is related to how their combined state count grows. Temperature is consequently not just a renamed kinetic-energy value; it is also connected to the energy dependence of the state count. Simple classical systems obeying equipartition relate mean kinetic energy directly to temperature. Frozen quantum degrees of freedom, interactions and constraints require the appropriate statistical treatment rather than unconditional application of that simple relation.

For an ideal frictionless spring, specifying total energy without specifying oscillation phase permits an ensemble distributed around one energy orbit. This differs from specifying energy, position and momentum completely for one state. The ensemble reflects a distribution over states; the fully specified state follows a definite deterministic trajectory in the model. Such distributions and their entropies can be discussed even for one particle. Small particle number changes fluctuation magnitudes and possible thermodynamic approximations, but does not make probability or statistical mechanics meaningless. It instead makes the definition of states and the measurement protocol especially visible.

Polymer experiments commonly exchange heat with their surroundings, so perfect isolation is often an idealization. The microcanonical viewpoint remains useful because the specimen together with a sufficiently large environment can be treated as a larger isolated system. The specimen's own equilibrium weights can then be derived from the number of environment states compatible with each specimen energy. The exponential probabilities in the next ensemble are thus connected to a physical counting argument rather than chosen arbitrarily. Defining the boundary between specimen and environment makes different ensembles expressions of the same statistical logic under different conditions of exchange.

## Why a heat bath produces Boltzmann weights

Place a specimen in contact with a large heat bath, allowing energy exchange while keeping specimen volume and particle number fixed. Specimen energy fluctuates, but the bath is large enough that its temperature changes negligibly in those exchanges. This defines a canonical ensemble. Treating specimen plus bath as isolated, any energy gained by the specimen is lost by the bath. The bath has different numbers of states at different energies, changing the relative probability of specimen states. Expanding the bath entropy near its initial energy produces the exponential Boltzmann weight. Thermal equilibrium thus determines a particular distribution through counting of the larger combined system.

Canonical Boltzmann weightsEq. 7

![Canonical Boltzmann weights](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/71ee666700d9456c659e7489.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| β | Inverse thermal energy | J⁻¹ |
| kB | Boltzmann constant | J K⁻¹ |
| T | Absolute heat-bath temperature | K |
| Z | Partition function summing microstate weights | 1 |
| i | Index of a complete microstate | 1 |
| Ei | Microstate energy | J |
| e | Natural-exponential base | 1 |
| Σi | Sum over all allowed states | 1 |
| pi | Normalized state probability | 1 |

Reading the relationshipThe change in bath state count with exchanged energy produces exponential weights. Dividing by their sum normalizes the probabilities.

A worked exampleOne zero-energy state and three states at energy 2kBT give Z=1+3e⁻²≈1.4060 and total upper-level probability 3e⁻²/Z≈0.2888.

ConditionsEquilibrium at fixed T,V,N with a weakly coupled large bath. The discrete form counts microstates; degeneracy requires individual counting or a multiplicity factor.

An exponential requires a dimensionless argument, so energy is divided by Boltzmann's constant times absolute temperature. Boltzmann's constant is 1.380649 times ten to the minus twenty-three joules per kelvin; at three hundred kelvin the thermal-energy scale is about 4.14 times ten to the minus twenty-one joules. The partition function adds weights of all microstates to normalize their probabilities. It is generally not the unweighted number of states. Only special circumstances, such as equal appropriately zero-referenced energies for all included states, reduce it directly to simple counting. Keeping this distinction clear prevents an energy-dependent normalization from being interpreted as a bare multiplicity.

If several microstates share an energy, their probabilities must be added to obtain the probability of that energy level. Suppose the lower level has one state and a higher level has three, separated by two thermal-energy units. Each higher state has weight the exponential of minus two relative to the lower state. Adding all three gives a total higher-level probability of about 0.289. Although each higher-energy state is individually less probable, its three realizations make a substantial combined contribution. This distinction between a microstate and an energy-level population is especially important for molecules with many conformations or symmetry-related arrangements.

From probabilities to energy, entropy and free energyEq. 8

![From probabilities to energy, entropy and free energy](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/39da3ed95b5cb6206a4b6f80.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U | Mean internal energy | J |
| F | Helmholtz free energy | J |
| S | Statistical entropy | J K⁻¹ |
| pi,Ei | State probability and energy | pi: 1; Ei: J |
| i,Σi | Microstate index and summation | 1 |
| kB | Boltzmann constant | J K⁻¹ |
| T | Absolute temperature | K |
| Z | Canonical partition function | 1 |
| ln | Natural logarithm, with zero-probability terms contributing zero by continuity | 1 |

Reading the relationshipInternal energy averages state energies. Substituting logarithms of Boltzmann probabilities into entropy gives F=U−TS and the relation between F and Z.

A worked exampleFor two equally probable zero-energy states, Z=2,U=0,S=kB ln2. At T=300 K, F≈−2.871×10⁻²¹ J, consistent with F=U−TS.

ConditionsCanonical equilibrium with fixed T,V,N and consistent energy reference and state counting. Absolute continuum entropy requires the corresponding physical phase-space measure.

The partition function also links probabilities to thermodynamics. Its natural logarithm gives free energy, internal energy is probability weighted, and entropy averages logarithms of probabilities. A more spread-out distribution generally involves more accessible information, but thermodynamic comparisons require consistent state definitions and constraints. The entropy expression vanishes for a single certain state and reduces to Boltzmann counting for equally likely states. A zero-probability term contributes zero through its continuous limit. These relations explain how a statistical model can predict both populations and thermodynamic quantities without treating them as disconnected measurements requiring unrelated assumptions.

Constructing a partition function from continuous classical phase space also requires a physical counting scale and consistent treatment of identical-particle indistinguishability. Standard expressions contain phase-space units set by Planck's constant and corrections for permutations of identical particles. These factors matter for absolute free energies, entropies and chemical potentials. Arbitrarily dividing a continuous distribution into bins and calling its binned entropy an absolute thermodynamic entropy would mix resolution changes into a physical result. The discrete examples here enumerate their states explicitly, making normalization and entropy directly checkable. A continuum model needs the corresponding measure specified with equal care.

## Particle exchange brings chemical potential into probability

Some systems exchange matter as well as heat. An adsorption site can bind or release a molecule from solution, particle number in a small solution region fluctuates through diffusion, and a polymer gel can absorb or release solvent. Equilibrium with large thermal and particle reservoirs is often described by a grand canonical ensemble at fixed temperature, volume and chemical potential. Particle number is no longer identical in every state. It fluctuates among allowed values, so a state must specify both how many particles are present and their internal microscopic arrangement. This extends the ensemble description without changing the basic requirement to normalize probabilities over all allowed possibilities.

Chemical potential measures the marginal change of an appropriate free energy when particles are added under specified thermodynamic conditions. Per-particle chemical potential has units of joules; a molar chemical potential has joules per mole, and the conventions are related by Avogadro's constant. It is not the kinetic energy currently carried by one particle, nor is it determined by concentration alone. Temperature, interactions and the reference convention also enter. During equilibrium exchange, the reservoir's chemical potential determines the statistical tendency to add or remove particles from the system, making it the appropriate control variable for the exchange process.

Grand canonical weights with particle exchangeEq. 9

![Grand canonical weights with particle exchange](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/789a5923e22e8a1c897d7114.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ξ | Grand partition function over particle numbers and internal states | 1 |
| N | Fluctuating system particle number | 1 |
| i | Microstate index at fixed N | 1 |
| ΣN,Σi | Sum over allowed particle numbers and internal states | 1 |
| β | 1/(kBT), inverse thermal energy | J⁻¹ |
| EiN | Energy of microstate i with N particles | J |
| μ | Chemical potential per particle | J |
| PiN | Joint probability of that particle number and state | 1 |
| e | Natural-exponential base | 1 |

Reading the relationshipThe reservoir contribution of supplying particles enters with sample energy, and normalization covers both particle count and configuration.

A worked exampleIf only an empty state N=0,E=0 and an occupied state N=1,E=μ are allowed, both weights are one, Ξ=2 and each probability is 0.5.

ConditionsEquilibrium with large thermal and particle reservoirs at fixed T,V,μ; identical-particle counting must be consistent across N.

Energy minus chemical potential times particle number combines the sample's energy cost with the reservoir contribution of supplying those particles. The grand partition function sums over particle numbers and their internal states. For one site that can be empty or occupied, choose zero empty-state energy and occupied-state energy ε. Their weight ratio is the exponential of minus the difference between ε and chemical potential divided by thermal energy. Raising chemical potential or lowering the occupied-state energy both increase occupancy. The same energy difference controls these two changes in the simplest model, providing a direct bridge between reservoir conditions and a measurable bound fraction.

Occupancy of one empty-or-filled siteEq. 10

![Occupancy of one empty-or-filled site](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/220214c7cfd8b4a3a6250bc3.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pocc | Probability that one particle occupies the site | 1 |
| ε | Occupied-state energy relative to the empty state | J |
| μ | Reservoir chemical potential per particle | J |
| kB | Boltzmann constant | J K⁻¹ |
| T | Absolute temperature | K |
| e | Natural-exponential base | 1 |

Reading the relationshipNormalize the empty weight one and occupied weight exp[−(ε−μ)/(kBT)] to obtain occupancy.

A worked exampleFor ε−μ=2kBT, Pocc=1/(1+e²)≈0.1192. For ε=μ, Pocc=0.5.

ConditionsOne particle at most, one empty and one occupied realization, no neighbor interactions. This can describe a classical independent adsorption site.

If occupied-state energy equals chemical potential, empty and occupied states each have probability one half. If the occupied energy exceeds chemical potential by two thermal-energy units, occupancy is about 0.119. This assumes one realization of each state and no interactions with neighboring sites. Multiple binding arrangements or cooperative and repulsive interactions change the state count and energies accordingly. The simple site model therefore explains a basic trend while identifying the physical additions needed for more complex adsorption or binding. A measured occupancy curve can then be used to test those additions rather than treating every deviation as a change in one unexplained fitting parameter.

Ensembles are not competing categories of material. They describe the same physical system under different exchange constraints. For suitable macroscopic short-range systems in a thermodynamic limit, many local or mean properties can agree across ensembles. Energy and particle-number fluctuations can still differ substantially in finite systems. Measuring a small specimen with fixed particle number and a region that freely exchanges particles asks different questions. Ensemble choice should therefore follow what the experiment permits to be exchanged and which average or fluctuation it needs to predict. This keeps the statistical boundary conditions connected to the actual physical preparation and measurement.

## The same equilibrium can have very different waiting times

Equilibrium probabilities describe how states are populated in the long run but do not determine transition speed. Suppose a molecule has conformations A and B, with B higher in energy. Thermal equilibrium balances probability flux from A to B against flux from B to A, linking the ratio of transition rates to the energy difference. Multiplying both rates by the same small factor lengthens waiting times without changing their ratio or the final populations. Energy differences and crossing barriers therefore play different roles: one controls relative equilibrium occupation, while the other can strongly control how rapidly that occupation is established.

Balanced probability flux for two equilibrium statesEq. 11

![Balanced probability flux for two equilibrium states](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/3efaac888735ede182d778c9.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PAeq,PBeq | Equilibrium probabilities of states A and B | 1 |
| kAB,kBA | Transition rates from A to B and B to A | s⁻¹ |
| ΔE | EB−EA, the state energy difference | J |
| kB | Boltzmann constant | J K⁻¹ |
| T | Absolute temperature | K |
| e | Natural-exponential base | 1 |

Reading the relationshipDirectional probability flux equals occupation times escape rate. At equilibrium the fluxes balance and agree with Boltzmann populations under equal state multiplicities.

A worked exampleFor ΔE=kBT, PBeq/PAeq=e⁻¹≈0.3679 and PBeq≈0.2689. Rates kAB=0.04979 and kBA=0.13534 s⁻¹ have the same ratio.

ConditionsOne realization per state, thermal equilibrium and continuous-time Markov jumps. Additional driving or multiplicities require modifications.

[Figure: Two-state energies and a transition-energy barrier](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp02/en/#en-s8)

Figure 3 · Energy is vertical and a schematic conformation coordinate horizontal. The difference between A and B minima sets equal-multiplicity equilibrium populations, while transition energy E‡ relative to each starting state affects escape. Horizontal spacing is not a molecular-distance measurement.

The interaction uses an explicit two-state jump model. Divide the energy difference by thermal energy to define δ, and introduce a nonnegative barrier parameter B that slows both directions. The base attempt rate is one per second. Directional rates have different exponential factors but retain the required equilibrium ratio. Waiting times for jumps follow exponential distributions, expressing a fixed instantaneous escape tendency while the system remains in a state. A jump is not guaranteed at regularly spaced times. After entering the other state, the appropriate escape rate determines the next waiting time. The model has a physical time unit because those kinetic rates have been specified.

Example rates with an adjustable barrierEq. 12

![Example rates with an adjustable barrier](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/1d8d6a16103303ca45a3707f.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| δ | Dimensionless energy difference | 1 |
| EA,EB | Energies of the two states | J |
| kB | Boltzmann constant | J K⁻¹ |
| T | Absolute temperature | K |
| kAB,kBA | Directional transition rates | s⁻¹ |
| k₀ | Common attempt rate, set to 1 in the interaction | s⁻¹ |
| B | Barrier above the higher-energy state divided by kBT; distinct from state label B | 1 |
| max | Take the larger of the two inputs | 1 |
| e | Natural-exponential base | 1 |

Reading the relationshipSet transition energy to the higher state energy plus BkBT. Subtracting each starting-state energy gives activation factors and guarantees rate ratio e⁻δ.

A worked exampleFor δ=1,B=2,k₀=1 s⁻¹, kAB=e⁻³≈0.049787 s⁻¹ and kBA=e⁻²≈0.135335 s⁻¹. Increasing B by one divides both rates by e without changing equilibrium populations.

ConditionsIllustrative thermally activated Markov model with B≥0 and constant attempt rate; individual molecular kinetics can require different prefactors and mechanisms.

If every independent specimen starts in A, the ensemble probability of B begins at zero and approaches its equilibrium value. The sum of the directional rates sets its relaxation time. One specimen, however, can only be in A or B and produces an irregular step-like record of jumps. Divide its total residence time in B by the observation duration to obtain its time-averaged occupancy. That quantity generally does not equal the ensemble probability exactly at an arbitrary finite instant. The latter compares many specimens at one time; the former accumulates occupation along one history. Their differences are visible even with exact knowledge of the model's rates.

Relaxation of a two-state ensembleEq. 13

![Relaxation of a two-state ensemble](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/1c15e0924f9216bd1b67d27e.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| p* | Equilibrium probability of B | 1 |
| kAB,kBA | Positive directional transition rates | s⁻¹ |
| τ | Relaxation time of B probability | s |
| PB(t) | Ensemble probability of B at time t | 1 |
| p₀ | Initial B probability, zero for all A and one for all B | 1 |
| t | Time since preparation | s |
| e | Natural-exponential base | 1 |

Reading the relationshipProbability changes by A-to-B inflow minus B-to-A outflow, producing a linear equation whose solution approaches equilibrium exponentially.

A worked exampleFor δ=0,B=2,k₀=1 s⁻¹, p*=0.5 and τ=e²/2≈3.6945 s. Starting all in A gives PB(τ)=0.5(1−e⁻¹)≈0.3161.

ConditionsTwo-state continuous-time dynamics with constant rates and a specified initial ensemble. A single trajectory’s cumulative time average differs from PB(t).

[Figure: Single jump record and probability averages](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp02/en/#en-s8)

k₀=1 s⁻¹. Above is one random history. Below, green is ensemble probability, orange its cumulative B residence fraction, and grey dashed the equilibrium probability. The full record is 200 s; the vertical line marks the cumulative observation window. No autoplay.

Energy gap changes equilibrium populations; a common barrier changes recovery speed. Compare fast and slow jumps at fixed gap to distinguish finite-time occupation, instantaneous ensemble probability and long-term equilibrium.

Keep the energy difference at zero and increase the barrier. Equilibrium B probability remains one half, but at a high barrier a two-hundred-second record may contain no jumps. Changing the prepared state from A to B can then give very different observed occupancies. Generating another random realization shows variation between repeated experiments. Lowering the barrier permits more exchanges, improving long-time sampling of equilibrium. Both model rates remain positive, so each state remains accessible in the long-time limit. The finite-observation discrepancy comes from a record short relative to relaxation, rather than a permanent disconnection between state regions.

Preparation at equilibrium differs from beginning in a specified state. To generate an equilibrium ensemble, initial states should themselves be drawn from equilibrium probabilities. The interaction deliberately starts all specimens in one selected state to display relaxation. Protein switching, adsorption–desorption and local chain-relaxation records likewise require energy difference, barriers, preparation and record length to be considered together. Fitting final occupancy alone cannot determine transition speed. Combining populations with waiting-time observations gives information that neither measurement supplies by itself, and helps separate a changed thermodynamic preference from a changed kinetic obstacle to reaching it.

## Entropy, coarse graining and finite specimens

Probability entropy depends on a distribution rather than being an ordinary function of one instantaneous mechanical coordinate. A single particle can have a distribution over positions or energy states and therefore a statistical entropy; many particles are not a prerequisite for defining it. With a specified model and counting convention, entropy is a state quantity determined by the distribution. It differs from the particular process used to reach an equilibrium state, although a process can change both state and distribution. Independence from path does not mean that entropy cannot change when temperature, volume or energy changes.

For two independent subsystems, joint probabilities are products of their separate probabilities. The logarithm turns those products into sums, making their entropies additive. Correlated subsystems have additional information in their joint distribution, so adding marginal entropies without examining the correlation does not give the full entropy. Macroscopic short-range systems usually have good extensivity when boundary effects are relatively small: increasing material amount approximately scales entropy proportionally. Length itself does not scale with material amount for every geometry and is not universally an extensive thermodynamic variable. Temperature and pressure are familiar intensive quantities, distinguished by their behavior under system scaling rather than by informal descriptions of size.

Coarse graining merges unresolved details into larger state cells or fewer variables. It may use spatial boxes, finite measurement times or replacement of many atoms by effective chain segments. The coarse distribution retains information at selected scales while losing details inside cells or among eliminated variables. Under Hamiltonian evolution, a fine distribution can stretch into increasingly thin structures that fixed-resolution observations no longer resolve. Fine and coarse entropies can consequently evolve differently. Thermodynamic irreversibility also involves initial conditions, environment and observational scale. A single word such as disorder cannot replace this physical account of what information is retained and how the system evolves.

[Figure: Fine and coarse displays of the same regional probabilities](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp02/en/#en-s9)

Figure 4 · Dark and light fine cells above have different probability densities. Below, each group of four becomes one coarse cell with the same total probability but unresolved internal differences. The diagram changes resolution rather than representing a physical time step.

Larger coarse cells are not automatically better. Very small cells may have too little data and mostly remain empty, while overly large cells merge interfaces, binding states or slow structures relevant to the question. Resolution should preserve the target phenomenon and account for memory in the retained dynamics. If eliminated degrees of freedom relax slowly, a memoryless evolution law may be inadequate, requiring additional variables or memory terms. The value of coarse graining lies in retaining the predictive relations needed for a problem, with calibration against experiments or a more detailed model. Resolution and dynamical assumptions must therefore be chosen together.

The thermodynamic limit usually increases particle number and volume together while holding density and other intensive conditions fixed. It helps define sharp transitions and stable macroscopic relations, but finite-system statistics remain meaningful. Averages over a small number of independent objects tend to fluctuate more, and correlations change the effective number of independent samples. In single-molecule and nanoscale measurements, distributions, variances, correlation times and preparation conditions often give a more complete description than one mean. Improving precision requires more effectively independent information, not merely a faster sampling rate along the same strongly correlated record.

Phase space specifies what a state contains. An ensemble assigns weights under defined exchange constraints. Dynamics determines how an observation explores those possibilities. Together they explain stable macroscopic properties with continuing microscopic fluctuations, as well as historical differences retained when waiting is too short. Keeping state definitions, normalization, model conditions and time scales explicit makes statistical mechanics applicable to real polymer shapes, thermal behavior and motion. An average then becomes part of a physical explanation connected to preparation and measurement, rather than a formal number whose relevance is assumed from its mathematical appearance.

---

# 一条链能占多大空间：理想链的构象统计

Source: https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/
Language: zh-CN

沿链量出的长度、两端之间的距离和整条链的空间尺寸，为什么是不同的量？从随机步子出发，逐步理解回转半径、库恩长度、概率分布和熵弹性，再比较柔性链、半刚性链与环状和支化结构。

## 一根很长的链，为什么能装进很小的地方

把一根细绳放在桌上，沿绳子量得到的长度不会改变，但两个端点之间的直线距离可以很短，也可以很长。高分子链也有这样的区别：组成链的单元很多，并不意味着分子在溶液里始终伸成一根长杆。链上许多位置能够转动，热运动不断改变它的弯曲方式，于是同一条链在不同时刻呈现不同的空间形状。这些在不改变连接关系的情况下得到的形状叫作构象。理解构象，是理解溶液中的分子尺寸、橡胶的回复力，以及柔性连接臂怎样影响生物分子相遇机会的起点。

例如，把两个能够结合的生物分子用一条柔性链连起来，连接臂的作用并不只是防止它们分开。链的长度和柔顺程度决定它们通常能相隔多远、靠近时有多少种安排，以及把两端拉开需要多大力。相同分子量的线性链、环状链和支化链，也可能占据不同大小的空间，影响它们在孔道中移动和在溶液中相互接近。要比较这些情况，需要能反映大量构象的尺寸指标，而不是选择一张看起来最典型的分子图。

[库恩在1934年关于链状分子形状的研究](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01451681)把统计思路带进了这个问题：分子形状可以从许多局部转动的共同结果来理解。把一条链画成接连迈出的步子，便能用随机行走分析整体尺寸。这里的随机不是没有物理规律，而是每次具体运动都受热扰动影响，我们改为计算哪些结果更常出现。大量单链照片虽然不同，它们组成的尺寸分布和平均值仍然可以稳定，并与实验相联系。

[Figure: diagram](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/#zh-s1)

图 1 · 库恩统计链思路的原创图解：区分沿链长度与端到端距离，并把一条链理解为许多构象的集合。 下方三条开链具有相同的段数与段长，端点以橙色标出。

本章从理想链开始。理想链保留连接关系和必要的局部几何，但在指定尺度上忽略远距离链段之间的排斥或吸引对构象统计的改变。这是一个便于建立基准的模型，并不是说化学键消失，也不是说真实链段能够毫无代价地穿过彼此。真实溶剂中，排除体积、电荷、特殊结合和拥挤都可能使结果偏离这个基准。先把理想情况算清楚，便能判断一条链变大或变小时，到底是哪一类相互作用改变了它。

## 先把方向、长度和平均分开

把链的起点放在坐标原点，沿链走过第一段、第二段，直到最后一段。每段位移既有长度，也有方向，因此用矢量表示。矢量可以理解为一支箭头：在三维空间中，它需要分别记录沿三个互相垂直方向走了多少。把这些小箭头首尾相接，最后得到从起点直接指向终点的大箭头，称为末端距矢量。它的大小才是两个端点之间的直线距离。沿着全部小箭头走过的总路程则是轮廓长度，两者回答不同的问题。

直线距离与沿链长度式 1

![直线距离与沿链长度](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/55107d014d9ae1be28d52333.svg)

| 符号 | 含义 | 单位 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R (vector) | 末端距矢量 | nm |
| b_{i} (vector) | 第i个链段的位移矢量，长度均为b | nm |
| R | 末端距矢量的大小 | nm |
| N, i | 链段总数与编号 | 1 |
| b, L | 单段长度与轮廓长度 | nm |
| Σ, \| \| | 依次相加；取矢量大小 | — |

怎样理解位移矢量首尾相接后相加，得到起点到终点的净位移。轮廓长度把各段的正长度相加。

算一个例子两段各1 nm，一段向右、一段向上：轮廓长度2 nm，末端距为√(1²+1²)=1.414 nm。

使用条件本式轮廓长度采用N个等长模型段；不等长时应逐段相加。

现在想象拍摄许多没有外力、没有优先方向的链。某次终点偏右，另一次可能偏左，方向相反的位移在平均时相互抵消，所以平均末端距矢量为零。这不意味着所有链都缩成一个点。就像一群人均匀站在广场中心的四周，平均位置可以位于中心，而每个人仍离中心有一定距离。要描述尺寸，可以先对距离平方，再平均，最后开平方。这样所有构象都以非负数贡献尺寸，而且平方展开后能够把不同链段之间的相关性分开。

尖括号表示对构象集合取平均：每个构象按它在给定条件下出现的机会加权。若我们抽取的样本符合这些概率，就可以用许多样本的算术平均来近似。先平均再平方，与先平方再平均是两种运算，结果一般不同。对于三个末端距大小分别为1、2、3纳米的样本，平均距离为2纳米，而均方根距离约为2.16纳米；较大的值经过平方后获得了更大的权重。纳米是一米的十亿分之一，适合描述分子尺度。

自由连接链的平均尺寸式 2

![自由连接链的平均尺寸](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/e8bd557bb6efbcba18bffd16.svg)

| 符号 | 含义 | 单位 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R (vector), R | 末端距矢量及其大小 | nm |
| b_{i} (vector), b_{i}, b | 第i段位移矢量、其长度及共同长度 | nm |
| N, i, j | 段数及两个段的编号 | 1 |
| 〈 〉 | 按构象概率取平均 | — |
| Σ_{i}, Σ_{i}<j | 所有段求和；每一对不同段只计一次 | — |
| · | 点积，描述方向投影关系 | — |
| R_{rms} | 均方根末端距 | nm |
| √, 0 (vector) | 平方根；零矢量 | — |

怎样理解平方展开产生自身项和交叉项。独立且各向同性的方向使不同段交叉项平均为零，自身项各为b²。

算一个例子N=100、b=1 nm时，〈R²〉=100 nm²，均方根末端距10 nm，轮廓长度100 nm；N增至400时，两者分别20和400 nm。

使用条件无外力、独立等长步子、各向同性；单张构象的交叉项一般不为零。

对自由连接链，每一段长度相同，方向独立且在空间中均匀分布。平方展开时，每一段与自身的点积贡献一份长度平方；不同段之间的点积有正有负，平均后抵消。点积衡量两个箭头在彼此方向上的投影关系，同向为正，反向为负，垂直时为零。于是均方末端距与段数成正比，均方根尺寸只与段数的平方根成正比。将段数增加到四倍，轮廓长度增加四倍，典型端到端距离却只增加两倍，这就是长链能够明显卷曲的基本统计原因。

## 从两端走向整条链：回转半径

末端距只看两个端点。它能抓住线性链的一项重要尺寸，却无法描述全部质量怎样分布。一个闭合的环没有相互分离的首尾，即使环占据很大的空间，把同一处当作起点和终点仍会得到零末端距。支化分子又有许多末端，任意挑选一对会让结果依赖选择。回转半径解决的是另一件事：以整条分子的质心为参照，计算所有部分距离质心有多远。质心是按质量加权的平均位置，好比一块物体能够平衡在支点上的中心。

如果每个模型珠子的质量相同，质心就是所有珠子坐标的平均。先计算每个珠子到质心的距离平方，再对珠子求平均，得到一个构象的回转半径平方；随后还可以对不同构象求平均。这两个平均层次应当分清：前一个描述一张照片中的质量分布，后一个描述许多照片的统计结果。回转半径适合线性链、环和支化链，也广泛用于解释静态散射测量。它不是必须画出的一圈分子外边界，链的一些部分可以在这个半径之外。

整条链的质量分布式 3

![整条链的质量分布](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/0cc5dff8fc24ea7e868b8008.svg)

| 符号 | 含义 | 单位 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| r_{i}, r_{j} (vector) | 第i或j个珠子的空间位置 | nm |
| r_{cm} (vector) | 质心位置 | nm |
| R_{g}² | 一个构象的回转半径平方 | nm² |
| N, N+1 | 链段数与等质量珠子数 | 1 |
| b | 自由连接段长 | nm |
| i, j, Σ | 珠子编号与对所列编号求和 | — |
| 〈 〉, \| \| | 构象平均；矢量大小 | — |
| ≃ | 长链近似 | — |

怎样理解质心定义使两两距离展开中的交叉项抵消，得到等价配对公式。自由连接链两珠子间均方距离等于连接段数乘b²，求和得到最后一行。

算一个例子N=100、b=1 nm时，〈R_g²〉=100×102/(6×101)=16.8317 nm²，其平方根约4.103 nm；长链近似给4.082 nm。

使用条件前三行适用于等质量珠子的一般构象；最后一行仅用于自由连接线性链，末项需N足够大。

[Figure: diagram](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/#zh-s3)

图 2 · 等质量珠子的质心与距离分布。回转半径统计所有珠子，不是只测末端，也不规定一条硬边界。

公式还给出了一个等价算法：把所有珠子两两之间的距离平方相加，再除以规定的计数因子。双重求和把有顺序的两种配对都数进去，因此分母有一个2。这个关系很有用，因为理想链上两个位置之间的均方距离，可以从连接它们的链段数直接得到。对于很多段的理想线性链，均方回转半径约为均方末端距的六分之一；这里比较的是平方，半径本身的比例要再开平方。有限段数时，则应使用保留端点计数的精确表达。

不同实验中的“半径”也要按定义理解。动态光散射分析散射信号随时间的涨落，通常先得到平移扩散信息，再换算为与该扩散速度对应的水动力学半径。这个半径描述分子拖动溶剂时的等效阻力，回转半径描述质量或散射对比的空间分布。柔软线团内部可以有溶剂穿行，所以两个数不必相同，也不能只因都叫半径就直接替换。比较尺寸时，先看测量对应哪一种物理量，往往比先比较数值大小更重要。

## 局部化学怎样改变整条链的尺寸

真实化学键不像任意转向的球形铰链。以常见的四面体成键几何为例，相邻键的夹角受到限制；绕单键转动也可能受到侧基拥挤和电子作用的影响。自由旋转链先保留固定键角，再假定绕键的转动方向没有偏好。这样相邻步子的方向相关，隔得越远，方向记忆通常越弱。为了避免角度定义混淆，下面的夹角取沿链向前走的相邻两个位移矢量之间的角，而不是在中心原子处向外画出的两根化学键夹角；这两个角互为补角。

固定键角留下方向记忆式 4

![固定键角留下方向记忆](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/03ce248881ab2a06df2a8855.svg)

| 符号 | 含义 | 单位 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| α | 相邻向前位移矢量的夹角 | 弧度（无量纲） |
| q, cos | 相邻方向余弦及余弦函数 | 1 |
| l_{i}, l_{i}+s (vector) | 相隔s根键的位移矢量 | nm |
| l | 固定键长 | nm |
| N, i, s | 键数、编号与间隔键数 | 1 |
| R | 端到端距离 | nm |
| 〈 〉, ·, Σ | 构象平均、点积与逐项求和 | — |

怎样理解自由方位旋转使每隔一步的方向记忆乘q；相隔s步的配对有N−s对。把这些相关项加入自身项得到有限链结果，再取长链极限。

算一个例子q=1/3时，长链因子(1+q)/(1−q)=2。平方尺寸为自由连接基准的两倍，均方根尺寸为其√2倍。

使用条件固定键长与角度、均匀自由方位旋转；长链极限要求相关长度远小于链长，|q|<1。

当向前的相邻位移有正相关时，一小段链较倾向于保持大致方向，因此同样数量、同样长度的键，整体均方末端距会比自由连接链更大。以向前夹角的余弦为三分之一作示例，长链的尺寸平方是自由连接基准的两倍，尺寸本身则乘以根号二。这个结果来自对所有不同间隔的方向相关求和。它只保留固定角度的影响，尚未加入真实分子中各类内旋转偏好，因此不宜直接当成任何一种实际聚合物的完整尺寸预测。

进一步描述内旋转时，可以把一个键附近的常见状态分为反式和两种旁式。反式与旁式描述的是相邻骨架片段绕键转动后的相对方向，而不是把化学连接顺序改变。各状态的能量不同，因此出现概率不同；同一种能量可能对应不止一种状态，这种状态数也要计入。用玻尔兹曼权重把能量转换成概率，便能看到温度如何改变局部选择。指数函数在这里的作用是使高能状态受到抑制，同时保留热运动让它们偶尔出现的可能。

化学中常把许多分子的能量合在一起报告，因此这里需要说明“摩尔”。一摩尔表示6.02214076×10²³个所指定的对象，这个每摩尔的数目是阿伏伽德罗常数N_A；对象可以是分子，也可以是模型中正在比较的内旋转单元。每摩尔3千焦的能量差，是这么多个相同单元的能量差之和，分到一个单元约为4.98×10⁻²¹焦耳。焦耳是能量单位，1千焦等于1000焦耳。热运动的每个单元能量尺度由玻尔兹曼常数k_B与绝对温度T相乘给出，其中k_B为1.380649×10⁻²³ J/K；把它乘以N_A，就得到按每摩尔计量的气体常数R，约为8.314 J/(mol·K)。绝对温度用开尔文K表示，把摄氏温度数值加273.15即可换算，所以300 K约为26.85 ℃。在相同计量基础上，能量差除以RT比较的是该状态代价与热运动尺度，两者的单位抵消；这样才适合放进指数函数，而不是直接把带单位的能量当作指数。

三个内旋转状态的概率式 5

![三个内旋转状态的概率](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/bbb4500257bc156fe46ce929.svg)

| 符号 | 含义 | 单位 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Δε | 每种旁式相对反式的摩尔能量差 | kJ mol⁻¹ |
| R | 气体常数0.008314 | kJ mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| T | 绝对温度 | K |
| w | 一种旁式相对于反式的权重 | 1 |
| p_{t}, p_{g}+, p_{g}− | 反式及两种旁式各自的概率 | 1 |
| exp | 自然指数函数 | 1 |

怎样理解把反式能量作为零点，其权重为1；两种等能旁式各有权重w，总权重为1+2w。各自除以总权重使概率之和为1。

算一个例子Δε=3 kJ/mol、T=300 K时，w约0.300，反式概率约0.625，两种旁式各约0.188。Δε为0时三种状态各占1/3。

使用条件三种离散状态、两旁式等能、局部状态独立；相邻耦合需要引入组合权重。

三态例子如果把每个位置独立处理，已经比完全自由旋转更接近化学直觉，但相邻旋转还可能相互影响。前一个旁式会改变后一个位置的拥挤程度，使某些组合更难出现。旋转异构态模型正是把这类离散状态与相邻状态之间的权重联系起来。对于蛋白质骨架、带大侧基的合成链或某些多糖，还要采用适合其键角和化学结构的局部描述。柔顺性由这些微观选择共同产生，因此“键可以转动”不等于“所有转动都同样容易”。

## 库恩长度：把化学细节换成有效步长

如果关心整条长链占据多大空间，逐个追踪每一根化学键可能过于繁琐。可以把局部的许多键合成一个较粗的有效单元，让化学细节主要通过有效步长体现。粗粒化就像把一条曲折的小路换成地图上较少的转折点：保留研究所需的大尺度距离关系，减少暂时不需要的局部细节。但有效单元不是随意截取的一小段，也不要求它的每一种微观构象都像一根刚棒。它是在明确匹配条件下定义的统计描述。

一种常用定义同时匹配轮廓长度和长链的均方末端距。把原链换成有效自由连接链后，库恩长度就是这条等效链的步长，等效步数则由轮廓长度除以它得到。两项匹配一起决定有效参数，因此不能只凭“每三四个单体算一段”给所有材料套同一个值。轮廓长度也要明确采用怎样的骨架路径或连续链定义；原子级锯齿路径与平滑后的中心线之间，可能需要几何转换。参数与定义配套，比较不同分子才有意义。

匹配轮廓与均方尺寸式 6

![匹配轮廓与均方尺寸](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/543c4d1982e3cb02a4a1ce81.svg)

| 符号 | 含义 | 单位 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| b_{K} | 库恩长度 | nm |
| N_{K} | 等效库恩段数，可以为非整数 | 1 |
| L | 采用明确路径定义的轮廓长度 | nm |
| 〈R²〉₀ | 无扰链的均方末端距；下标0表示无扰统计 | nm² |

怎样理解等效自由连接链同时满足L=N_Kb_K和均方尺寸N_Kb_K²，联立后确定两个参数。

算一个例子L=200 nm、〈R²〉₀=400 nm²时，b_K=2 nm，N_K=100，均方根末端距20 nm。

使用条件长链、局部相关已粗粒化且远程作用不改变无扰统计；轮廓定义随参数一起保留。

[Figure: diagram](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/#zh-s5)

图 3 · 粗粒化示意与库恩匹配条件。连接少数点说明降低分辨率的想法，具体库恩步长仍由轮廓和均方尺寸共同确定。

保持轮廓长度相同，较大的库恩长度对应较少、较长的有效步子，链在整体上较伸展。保持库恩长度相同而增加轮廓长度，则增加了有效步数，链的尺寸按平方根规律长大。这两种改变都能使线团变大，但物理原因不同：前者改变局部刚性，后者增加链的长度。若一条链只有很少几个有效单元，很多长链近似就不够准确；这时应回到有限链或半刚性链模型，保留仍然重要的方向相关。

把许多独立步子再合成一组，这组的均方位移等于组内各步均方位移之和。组数减少，组的典型尺寸相应增大，整条链的总体均方末端距保持不变。这种统计自相似性是理想链大尺度描述的基础：换一个观察分辨率，仍然看见同一种平方根标度。它不是说每一小段的精确形状都和整条链相同，也不是说化学键尺度和整条链尺度之间没有区别。它适用于已经越过局部相关长度、又尚未受到其他大尺度约束主导的范围。

## 为什么末端距形成一条概率曲线

平均尺寸把许多构象压缩成一个数，但做连接、捕获或拉伸实验时，我们还想知道某段距离出现得多不多。许多独立小位移相加后，每个坐标方向的总位移趋近钟形的高斯分布，这是中心极限定理在链模型中的体现。它要求有足够多的有效步子，并且单步变化没有被少数极端贡献主导。三维中的末端距矢量由三个坐标分量组成，分布密度可以写成只依赖距离平方的形式，因为各方向在无外力时等价。

概率密度不是某个精确点的概率。把密度乘以一个很小的空间体积，才近似得到终点落入该体积的机会；把整个空间中的贡献相加，总概率为一。如果每根步子长度固定，单步终点只能在球面上，数学上可以用狄拉克δ分布表达这一约束。δ分布是积分中的集中权重，不应解释成某个点具有“无限概率”。本章直接从许多步子的平滑分布入手，避免让这种记号遮住最重要的空间计数。

矢量密度与距离密度式 7

![矢量密度与距离密度](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/7baa3f327bdb1ae705acd3ff.svg)

| 符号 | 含义 | 单位 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q | 均方末端距 | nm² |
| N, b | 独立段数与段长 | N：1；b：nm |
| R (vector), R | 末端距矢量及其大小，R非负 | nm |
| p(R (vector)) | 单位空间体积的末端位置概率密度 | nm⁻³ |
| w(R) | 单位距离区间的径向概率密度 | nm⁻¹ |
| R_{mode}, R_{rms} | 最可能距离与均方根距离 | nm |
| π, exp, √ | 圆周率、自然指数与平方根 | — |

怎样理解三个坐标分量的高斯分布相乘给出矢量密度。把半径R薄球壳内的所有方向相加，乘球面面积4πR²得到径向密度。

算一个例子N=100、b=1 nm时，Q=100 nm²，径向峰位约8.165 nm，均方根距离10 nm；矢量密度仍在原点最大。

使用条件足够多独立有效段的三维长链近似，典型卷曲距离范围；固定段链的真实末端距不超过轮廓长度。

矢量密度在原点最高，而只按距离大小统计的曲线却在非零距离达到最高。原因是半径越大的薄球壳包含越多不同方向的位置。想象在城市地图上统计住户：中心一小块区域可以很密，但离中心稍远的一整圈面积很大，其中总人数可能更多。径向概率密度把所有方向的机会合并，因此要乘上球壳面积因子。这个区别还能解释为什么平均矢量为零、最常见距离不为零、均方根距离又是另一个数；它们分别使用了不同的统计规则。

三维自由连接链的构象样本。每次计算2000条链，采用相同随机序列以便比较；曲线是长链近似，数值同时给出有限自由连接链的回转尺寸。

交互中每条链都在三维生成，图上的单条链只是其二维投影，距离计算仍使用全部三个坐标。改变段数时，比较轮廓长度、均方根末端距和回转半径如何变化；再保持段数不变，改变步长，所有空间距离会按相同比例缩放。直方图统计许多独立构象，平滑曲线是长链高斯近似。有限样本会有起伏，较短链的尾部也会偏离近似。这些差别恰好说明一张照片、有限样本平均和理论极限是三个层次，不能把其中一个当成另一个。

高斯近似还有一个明确的几何边界：固定长度的真实步子全部排直时，端到端距离最多等于轮廓长度，而高斯曲线在任意远处都有很小的尾巴。在典型卷曲范围，这个差别对长链很小；接近拉直时，它却决定了模型能否正确描述力。使用概率曲线时，应当让所考察的距离范围与近似的推导范围一致。下面讨论弹性时，这条看似细小的区别会变得十分重要。

## 没有拉长化学键，也会产生回复力

轻轻拉开柔性链的两端，最先改变的通常是许多局部段的方向，而不必明显拉长每一根化学键。没有拉力时，链可以采用大量不同的卷曲安排；两端被固定在较远位置后，满足条件的安排减少。熵衡量这种可用微观安排的多少，安排减少使自由能提高，于是链对固定端表现出向回拉的平均作用。这个回复力来自构象统计，称为熵弹性。橡胶网络中许多连接在一起的链段，就能把这种单链趋势传递为宏观回复力。

从高斯矢量概率密度可以求出固定末端位置的自由能代价。自然对数把乘法权重转成可以相加的自由能，再对位移求变化率，就得到维持该位移所需的平均外力。这里固定的是末端在空间中的位置，不是只固定距离大小而允许端点在整个球壳上自由移动，因此应使用矢量密度。若误把径向曲线直接代入，便会把球壳位置的计数混入不同的约束问题，产生额外的项。约束条件决定应该使用哪一种概率。

单链受力很小，通常用皮牛顿pN表示：1 pN等于10⁻¹² N。力与沿力方向的位移相乘具有能量的单位，因此1 pN·nm等于10⁻²¹ J。这样可以把分子距离和分子力放在同一组便于阅读的单位中：300 K时的热能尺度k_BT约为4.142 pN·nm。下面的自由能差正使用这种能量单位，对纳米表示的位移求变化率后，单位便成为皮牛顿，得到维持端点位置所需的力。

固定末端位置的熵弹性式 8

![固定末端位置的熵弹性](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/c25a81a4ee410a72b2811b98.svg)

| 符号 | 含义 | 单位 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ΔF | 相对于端点位于原点的自由能差 | pN nm |
| k_{B} | 玻尔兹曼常数0.01380649 pN·nm/K | pN nm K⁻¹ |
| T | 绝对温度 | K |
| R (vector), R, 0 (vector) | 末端距矢量、其大小与零矢量 | nm |
| p | 末端矢量位置的概率密度 | nm⁻³ |
| N, b | 有效段数与段长 | N：1；b：nm |
| ln | 自然对数；密度比是无量纲 | 1 |
| f_{hold} | 保持该末端位移所需的平均外力大小 | pN |
| dΔF/dR | 自由能对距离的变化率 | pN |

怎样理解固定端点时可用构象权重下降，−k_BT乘其对数给出自由能代价。对位移求导得到外力；链的回复力方向相反。

算一个例子T=300 K、N=100、b=1 nm、R=5 nm时，k_BT=4.142 pN·nm，弹簧常数0.1243 pN/nm，保持力约0.621 pN。

使用条件平衡高斯链、固定矢量端点、伸长远小于轮廓长度；Nb²在比较中按指定条件使用。

[Figure: diagram](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/#zh-s7)

图 4 · Rouse珠簧思想的示意：粗粒化连接承载子链的熵弹性。两行仅对照构象自由度，不是实测力—位移曲线。

这个关系类似普通弹簧：在适用范围内，拉开得越多，维持它所需的力越大。但弹簧常数来自温度与链的统计尺寸。其他参数不变时，温度提高会放大熵变化的自由能代价；链更长则有更多可调整的构象，同样的端点位移通常需要较小的力。真实材料升温时，库恩长度、相互作用和网络结构也可能变化，因此实验中的温度效应应把这些因素一起考虑。单链公式提供的是明确参数下的比较，而不是所有橡胶材料的统一温度规律。

当链被拉到接近轮廓长度时，可用方向越来越少，有限伸长变得关键，线性高斯弹簧便需要被更合适的关系替代。更强的拉力还可能改变键长、打开局部折叠或破坏结合，这些过程分别有自己的能量和时间尺度。单分子拉伸实验之所以有价值，正是因为力与位移曲线能够把不同阶段分开：先调整构象，再限制弯曲，随后可能进入分子内部结构变化。看清曲线转折对应什么，才能把测得的“硬”解释成具体机制。

## 从柔性线团到半刚性细杆

一根短竹条看起来近似直杆，一根很长的同类细条却可以明显弯曲。高分子的柔软或刚硬也取决于观察长度。持久长度用来描述方向记忆沿链衰减的尺度：从某一点沿着链走，局部切线方向与起点方向的相关性逐渐减小；走过一个持久长度后，简单蠕虫链模型中的相关性降至原来的约37%。这里测量的是沿链走过的弧长，而不是两点之间的空间直线距离。持久长度越大，局部方向能够维持得越远。

[Kratky与Porod在1949年的研究](https://doi.org/10.1002/recl.19490681203)把链的局部刚性与溶液散射行为联系起来。蠕虫链把骨架描述为连续且能够弯曲的细线，适合研究从局部杆状到整体线团的过渡。轮廓长度远短于持久长度时，链几乎没有空间积累大幅弯曲；远长于持久长度时，不同远处的方向逐渐失去相关，整体又接近随机线团。一个模型由此包含了两种看似不同的形态，而不需要给同一材料贴上永远柔软或永远刚硬的标签。

连续弯曲链的方向相关与尺寸式 9

![连续弯曲链的方向相关与尺寸](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/eee2bf7a02ebc3fb618e681a.svg)

| 符号 | 含义 | 单位 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| t(s), t(0) (vector) | 弧长位置s与0的单位切线矢量 | 1 |
| s, L | 沿链弧长间隔与总轮廓长度 | nm |
| ℓ_p | 持久长度 | nm |
| R | 端到端距离 | nm |
| b_{K} | 长链等效库恩长度 | nm |
| 〈 〉, ·, exp | 构象平均、点积与自然指数函数 | — |
| ≫, ≃ | 远大于；相应极限的近似 | — |

怎样理解链的总位移由沿轮廓的切线累加得到；把两处切线的指数相关对整条链积分，得到均方末端距。长链时端部修正相对较小。

算一个例子L=100 nm、ℓ_p=10 nm时，〈R²〉≈1800.009 nm²，均方根约42.43 nm；长链首项2000 nm²尚高约11.1%，说明此处保留有限长度修正有用。

使用条件三维、无外力、均匀不可伸长蠕虫链；局部弯曲刚性恒定，忽略远程相互作用。

[Figure: diagram](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/#zh-s8)

图 5 · Kratky–Porod连续链中的方向相关示意。棕色曲线采用更大的持久长度，因此方向记忆沿轮廓衰减得更慢。

在长链极限下，这个模型的库恩长度为持久长度的两倍。这个二倍关系来自连续蠕虫链的方向相关积分以及轮廓长度的匹配，使用其他离散角度模型或有限短链时，应先说明具体定义，再讨论换算。特征比则用实际无扰链的均方末端距除以相同化学键数和键长下的自由连接基准，提供另一种衡量局部结构影响的办法。它比较的是选定化学骨架的统计结果，所以单体数、骨架键数和有效库恩段数仍需分开记录。

双链DNA提供了很直观的生物例子：在短距离上双螺旋有明显弯曲刚性，在足够长的尺度上却仍能形成线团。[Marko与Siggia在1995年分析DNA拉伸](https://doi.org/10.1021/ma00130a008)时，用蠕虫链统计解释力与伸长之间的关系，并讨论了电荷作用和更强拉力带来的改变。盐条件会影响带电链段之间的作用，局部结构也可能随条件变化，因此持久长度应与测量环境一起使用。对蛋白质细丝、多糖或核酸，选择模型的关键同样是链长与局部方向记忆尺度的比较。

## 环、星形与支化：连接方式也在决定尺寸

总链段数相同，连接方式不同，分子的平均尺寸仍会改变。线性链的两端自由，闭环要求首尾相接，这个全局约束改变了链上不同位置之间的距离统计；星形分子则把多条臂连接到同一个中心。这里的拓扑结构指谁与谁连接，不是某一时刻在纸上画出的轮廓。把一条链弯成星形外观并不会产生真正的分支，必须有相应连接点。天然分子中，糖原具有支化连接，纤维素的基本链则是线性的，二者不应只因都属于多糖就归成同一种结构。

[Zimm与Stockmayer在1949年研究了含支链和环的链分子尺寸](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1747157)。对理想链，两点间的统计距离可以结合分子连接结构计算，再汇总成回转半径。没有环的支化树中，任意两点之间只有一条沿链路径，因此可以把路径上的独立段贡献相加；出现闭环后，不同路径受到闭合约束，便不能简单当成互不相关的自由行走。这种把连接图与空间统计分开处理的思路，是理解复杂分子构筑的重要工具。

相同总链长下的拓扑比较式 10

![相同总链长下的拓扑比较](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/cd2b03d9b296d0ac16ca1df3.svg)

| 符号 | 含义 | 单位 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R_{g}² | 回转半径平方 | nm² |
| 〈 〉 | 构象平均 | — |
| N, b | 全部结构的总统计段数与共同段长 | N：1；b：nm |
| lin, ring, star, architecture | 线性链、环、等臂星形和所比较结构的下标 | — |
| g | 均方回转半径之比，称为收缩因子 | 1 |
| f | 等臂星形的臂数 | 1 |

怎样理解回转半径来自所有点对的均方距离。环闭合约束和分支路径改变这些距离；在总段数相同条件下与线性链比较得到g。

算一个例子N=120、b=1 nm时，线性链平方回转半径约20 nm²，环约10 nm²。四臂星形g=10/16=0.625，平方回转半径约12.5 nm²。

使用条件理想高斯长链、相同总段数与段长，星形各臂等长；不含排除体积、结或穿套约束。

[Figure: diagram](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/#zh-s9)

图 6 · Zimm–Stockmayer拓扑尺寸比较：示意线性、环和等臂星形连接，数值采用理想长链且总统计段数相同。

收缩因子比较的是非线性结构与相同总段数、相同统计步长的线性链的均方回转半径。理想长环的这个比值为二分之一，因此半径比约为0.707，而不是半径减半。等臂星形中，臂数增多时，每条臂变短，平均质量分布更靠近中心。若各臂长度不相等，总量相同也不能只用臂数决定尺寸；长臂会把一部分质量带到更远处。梳形链还需要给出主链长度、侧链长度与接枝位置，才能从连接图得到有意义的比较。

真实高支化分子可能因侧链拥挤而明显伸展，环也可能受到结、穿套和其他链的约束。这些作用会改变理想模型的预测。即便在理想模型中，一张单链照片也通常不是完美球形：沿不同主方向的展开程度可以不同。回转张量把各方向的质量分布及其相关性记录在一个表中，转到主轴后，三个非负主值之和就是回转半径平方。若先对所有随机朝向平均，空间看起来可以各向同性；若先找每条链自己的长轴再比较，形状的不对称仍然保留。

即便是同一条线性链，不同位置的活动空间也不相同。在线性高斯长链中，端点到质心的均方距离通常比链中点更大，因为中点两侧都连着长链，端点只有一侧受到连接限制。例如整条链的均方末端距为100平方纳米时，连续链模型给出端点到质心的均方距离约33.3平方纳米，中点约8.33平方纳米。平方量相差四倍，对应的均方根距离相差两倍。这是许多构象的统计比较，并不要求每张照片里端点都比中点更远，也没有说端点一定在一层固定的球壳上。

## 把单链统计接到材料与实验

理想链的几种模型像同一张地图上的不同分辨率。自由连接链适合建立独立步子的基准，自由旋转和旋转异构态模型保留更多局部化学，库恩链将这些影响压缩为有效步长，高斯链进一步描述大量步子的总体分布，蠕虫链则保留连续弯曲刚性。它们在适当大尺度上可能给出相同的平均尺寸，却不一定在短距离、强拉伸或动力学上等价。选择模型时，先明确要预测的是整体大小、局部弯曲、端点靠近概率还是力学响应，再决定需要保留哪些细节。

[Rouse在1953年提出的珠簧描述](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1699180)把较长子链替换成具有熵弹性的连接，并把与溶剂有关的阻力放在粗粒化珠子上。珠子不是必须对应一个真实单体，弹簧也不是链内存在的小金属弹簧；它们分别承载保留下来的摩擦和构象自由能。这样，单链的统计尺寸可以进一步接到形变后的恢复过程。加入时间后，还需要说明热扰动、摩擦以及流体或其他链带来的耦合，静态平均本身并没有给出全部运动规律。

以柔性连接臂为例，设计时可以先估计它的有效段数与典型尺寸，再比较两个结合部位之间需要跨越的距离。如果距离远大于典型尺寸，符合要求的构象较少，连接会受到明显熵代价；如果距离较近，还要考虑端基的朝向、局部位阻和真正发生结合的化学条件。对环化反应也是如此，两端接近只是其中一个要求，合适取向和反应时间同样重要。统计模型告诉我们空间机会怎样变化，再由具体化学决定这些机会有多少转化为反应。

一次清楚的尺寸比较，应同时写明链的连接结构、总长度或分子量、统计段定义、溶剂与温度，以及测量的是哪一种半径。若结果随浓度变化，要考虑链间相互作用；若随盐变化，要考虑电荷与局部结构；若拉伸响应偏离线性，要检查有限伸长和内部转变。这样，理想链不只是一组平方根公式，而是一套逐层提问的方法：先确定几何量，再确定概率规则，最后检查现实中哪些相互作用使基准发生改变。

实际比较时，可以让同一份样品接受几种互补测量。静态散射观察空间分布，扩散测量观察分子与溶剂一起移动时的阻力，端点标记观察特定位置之间的距离。一个模型若能同时解释这些量，比只匹配其中一个平均值更容易辨认其物理含义。若平均尺寸相同而分布宽度、形状或拉伸响应不同，也说明仍有结构信息没有被一个尺寸参数概括。先选择所需的观测，再判断最简单的充分模型，能够让计算保持清楚，同时保留实验真正关心的细节。

---

# How Much Space Does a Chain Occupy? Ideal-Chain Statistics

Source: https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/en/
Language: en

Contour length, end-to-end distance and overall molecular size measure different things. Random steps lead to the radius of gyration, Kuhn length, probability distributions and entropic elasticity, followed by semiflexible chains, rings and branches.

## How a long chain fits into a small region

Place a piece of string on a table. Its length measured along the string stays the same, while the straight-line distance between its ends can vary enormously. A polymer has the same distinction: a large number of connected units does not mean that the molecule remains stretched into a long rod in solution. Many positions along its backbone can rotate, and thermal motion continually changes the pattern of bending. Shapes obtained without changing the molecular connectivity are called conformations. Understanding them is a starting point for explaining molecular dimensions in solution, the restoring force of rubber and the role of flexible linkers between biological molecules.

A flexible linker does more than prevent two binding partners from separating completely. Its length and flexibility determine their typical separation, the number of arrangements that bring them close, and the force needed to hold them apart. Likewise, linear, cyclic and branched molecules with the same molecular mass can occupy different amounts of space. Their dimensions affect movement through pores and encounters in solution. Comparing such cases requires measures that represent many conformations, rather than a single molecular drawing chosen because it appears typical.

[Kuhn's 1934 study of thread-like molecules](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01451681) helped establish a statistical approach to molecular shape. Many local rotations collectively determine the overall dimensions, and a chain can be represented as a sequence of steps in a random walk. Randomness here does not mean an absence of physical rules. Thermal fluctuations make individual outcomes variable, so we calculate which outcomes occur more frequently. Individual molecular snapshots differ, yet their size distribution and average dimensions can be reproducible and experimentally meaningful.

[Figure: diagram](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/en/#en-s1)

Figure 1 · Original illustration of the statistical-chain idea: contour and end-to-end distances differ, and a chain occupies an ensemble of conformations. The three open chains below have equal segment counts and segment lengths; orange dots mark their ends.

We begin with an ideal chain. This model retains connectivity and the necessary local geometry while neglecting the influence of long-range attraction or repulsion between chain segments on the statistics at the scale of interest. Chemical bonds remain present. The model provides a baseline against which excluded volume, charge, specific binding and crowding can be recognized. Real segments do not freely pass through one another, and real solutions can depart from ideal statistics. Establishing the baseline first makes an increase or decrease in size easier to connect to a particular physical cause.

## Separating direction, length and averaging

Fix the beginning of a chain at the coordinate origin and follow the first segment, then the second, until reaching the last. Each displacement has both magnitude and direction, so it is represented by a vector. A vector is an arrow whose three components record displacement along mutually perpendicular spatial directions. Adding the small arrows head to tail gives the arrow directly connecting the starting point to the endpoint: the end-to-end vector. Its magnitude is the straight-line distance between the ends. The total distance traveled along all the segments is the contour length, which answers a different geometric question.

Straight-line distance and contour lengthEq. 1

![Straight-line distance and contour length](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/55107d014d9ae1be28d52333.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R (vector) | End-to-end vector | nm |
| b_{i} (vector) | Displacement vector of segment i, each of magnitude b | nm |
| R | Magnitude of the end-to-end vector | nm |
| N, i | Total segment count and segment index | 1 |
| b, L | Segment length and contour length | nm |
| Σ, \| \| | Summation; vector magnitude | — |

Reading the relationshipHead-to-tail vector addition gives net displacement. Contour length adds the positive lengths of all segments.

A worked exampleTwo 1 nm segments, one rightward and one upward, have contour length 2 nm and end-to-end distance √(1²+1²)=1.414 nm.

ConditionsThe contour expression assumes N equal-length model segments; unequal lengths must be added individually.

Now imagine many chains with no imposed force or preferred direction. An endpoint lying to the right in one configuration can be balanced by one lying to the left in another, so the mean end-to-end vector is zero. The chains have not collapsed into points. People arranged around the center of a square have an average position at the center while each remains some distance away. To characterize size, we can square the end-to-end distance, average the squared values and then take the square root. Squaring makes every contribution nonnegative and also allows correlations between segments to be separated mathematically.

Angle brackets denote a conformational average, with configurations weighted by their probabilities under the chosen conditions. Samples drawn according to these probabilities can approximate the average by ordinary arithmetic. Averaging before squaring differs from squaring before averaging. For three distances of 1, 2 and 3 nanometers, the mean distance is 2 nanometers, while the root-mean-square distance is about 2.16 nanometers because squaring gives greater weight to the larger values. A nanometer is one billionth of a meter, a convenient unit for molecular dimensions.

Mean dimensions of a freely jointed chainEq. 2

![Mean dimensions of a freely jointed chain](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/e8bd557bb6efbcba18bffd16.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R (vector), R | End-to-end vector and its magnitude | nm |
| b_{i} (vector), b_{i}, b | Segment-i vector, its magnitude and common segment length | nm |
| N, i, j | Segment count and indices of two segments | 1 |
| 〈 〉 | Average weighted by conformational probabilities | — |
| Σ_{i}, Σ_{i}<j | Sum over segments; sum over each distinct pair once | — |
| · | Dot product measuring directional alignment | — |
| R_{rms} | Root-mean-square end-to-end distance | nm |
| √, 0 (vector) | Square root; zero vector | — |

Reading the relationshipExpanding the square gives self-terms and cross-terms. Independent isotropic directions make the mean cross-terms zero, leaving b² per segment.

A worked exampleFor N=100 and b=1 nm, 〈R²〉=100 nm², the rms distance is 10 nm and the contour is 100 nm. At N=400 these lengths become 20 and 400 nm.

ConditionsNo imposed force, independent equal steps and isotropic directions. Cross-terms are generally nonzero in an individual configuration.

In a freely jointed chain, every segment has the same length, and its direction is independent and uniformly distributed in space. Expanding the squared total displacement gives self-terms and cross-terms. Each segment's dot product with itself contributes its squared length. Cross-terms between different segments have positive and negative values that cancel in the average. The dot product measures directional alignment: it is positive for parallel arrows, negative for opposite arrows and zero for perpendicular ones. The mean-square end-to-end distance therefore grows in proportion to segment number, while its square root grows only as the square root of that number. Four times as many segments give four times the contour length but only twice the typical end-to-end distance.

## Beyond the two ends: radius of gyration

The end-to-end distance examines only two points. It captures an important dimension of a linear chain but does not describe how all the mass is distributed. A closed ring has coincident starting and ending points even while occupying a substantial region of space. A branched molecule has many ends, so selecting a particular pair introduces an arbitrary choice. The radius of gyration instead measures the distribution of all parts around the center of mass. This center is a mass-weighted mean position, analogous to the balance point of an object supported against gravity.

For equal-mass model beads, the center of mass is simply the average of their coordinates. Averaging the squared distances of the beads from this center gives the squared radius of gyration for one configuration. A second average can then be taken over configurations. The first operation describes the mass distribution in one snapshot; the second describes a collection of snapshots. This measure works for linear, cyclic and branched chains and is widely used in interpreting static scattering. It does not define a hard molecular boundary, and parts of the chain can lie outside the corresponding radius.

Mass distribution of the entire chainEq. 3

![Mass distribution of the entire chain](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/0cc5dff8fc24ea7e868b8008.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| r_{i}, r_{j} (vector) | Position of bead i or j | nm |
| r_{cm} (vector) | Center-of-mass position | nm |
| R_{g}² | Squared radius of gyration of one configuration | nm² |
| N, N+1 | Number of segments and equal-mass beads | 1 |
| b | Freely jointed segment length | nm |
| i, j, Σ | Bead indices and summation over those indices | — |
| 〈 〉, \| \| | Conformational average; vector magnitude | — |
| ≃ | Long-chain approximation | — |

Reading the relationshipExpanding pairwise squared distances and using the center definition gives the pair identity. In a freely jointed chain, each pair has mean-square separation equal to its contour segment count times b²; summing gives the last line.

A worked exampleFor N=100 and b=1 nm, 〈R_g²〉=100×102/(6×101)=16.8317 nm², whose square root is about 4.103 nm. The long-chain approximation gives 4.082 nm.

ConditionsThe first three lines apply to any equal-mass bead configuration. The final line applies to a freely jointed linear chain, with the approximation requiring large N.

[Figure: diagram](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/en/#en-s3)

Figure 2 · Center and distance distribution for equal-mass beads. Gyration includes every bead and is neither an endpoint-only distance nor a hard boundary.

An equivalent calculation sums squared distances between all pairs of beads. The double sum counts each distinct pair in both orders, which explains the factor of two in the denominator. This identity is useful because the mean-square separation of two points on an ideal chain follows from the number of independent segments connecting them. For a long ideal linear chain, the mean-square radius of gyration is approximately one sixth of the mean-square end-to-end distance. These are squared sizes; the ratio of radii requires taking a square root. A finite chain uses the more precise expression that retains the endpoint counting.

Experimental quantities called radii must also be distinguished by definition. Dynamic light scattering analyzes time-dependent fluctuations of scattered light, usually yielding translational diffusion information that can be converted into a hydrodynamic radius. This is an equivalent size associated with resistance to motion through the solvent. The radius of gyration describes the spatial distribution of mass or scattering contrast. Solvent can move through a flexible coil, so the two measures need not agree. Before comparing numerical values, identify the physical quantity that the measurement actually reports.

## How local chemistry changes overall dimensions

A chemical backbone is not a sequence of joints that can point freely in every direction. Common tetrahedral bonding geometries constrain the angle between neighboring bonds. Rotation about a bond can also be affected by side-group crowding and electronic interactions. The freely rotating chain retains a fixed bond angle while allowing unrestricted azimuthal rotation. Neighboring displacement directions are then correlated, with directional memory usually weakening along the chain. In the following convention, the angle is measured between successive forward-pointing displacement vectors. It is supplementary to the angle between two bonds drawn outward from their common atom, so distinguishing the conventions prevents a sign error.

Directional memory from a fixed bond angleEq. 4

![Directional memory from a fixed bond angle](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/03ce248881ab2a06df2a8855.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| α | Angle between successive forward displacement vectors | radians (dimensionless) |
| q, cos | Adjacent-direction cosine and cosine function | 1 |
| l_{i}, l_{i}+s (vector) | Bond displacement vectors separated by s steps | nm |
| l | Fixed bond length | nm |
| N, i, s | Bond count, index and separation in steps | 1 |
| R | End-to-end distance | nm |
| 〈 〉, ·, Σ | Conformational average, dot product and summation | — |

Reading the relationshipFree azimuthal rotation multiplies directional memory by q per step. There are N−s pairs at separation s. Adding these correlations gives the finite-chain result and its long-chain limit.

A worked exampleFor q=1/3, the long-chain factor is (1+q)/(1−q)=2. The squared size doubles and the rms size increases by √2.

ConditionsFixed lengths and angles with uniform free azimuthal rotation; the asymptotic expression requires a chain much longer than its correlation scale and |q|<1.

A positive correlation between successive forward displacements makes a short portion of the chain more likely to continue in a similar direction. The same number of bonds of the same length then gives a larger mean-square end-to-end distance than the freely jointed baseline. For a forward-angle cosine of one third, the long-chain squared size is twice the freely jointed result; the size itself increases by the square root of two. The result sums directional correlations over every separation along the chain. It accounts for fixed-angle geometry, while actual torsional preferences introduce further changes.

A more detailed local model can distinguish a trans state and two gauche states around a rotatable bond. These describe relative orientations of neighboring backbone portions without changing chemical connectivity. Different energies give different probabilities, and the number of states at each energy matters as well. Boltzmann weights convert the energies into relative statistical weights. The exponential suppresses higher-energy states while preserving their finite probability under thermal motion. This makes it possible to examine how temperature changes the local choices available to the backbone.

Chemistry often reports the combined energy of many molecules, so the mole needs a definition here. One mole contains 6.02214076×10²³ specified entities; this count per mole is the Avogadro constant N_A. The entities may be molecules or the torsional units being compared in a model. An energy difference of 3 kilojoules per mole is the sum for that many equivalent units, corresponding to about 4.98×10⁻²¹ joules per unit. The joule is an energy unit, and one kilojoule equals 1000 joules. The thermal energy scale per unit is the Boltzmann constant k_B multiplied by absolute temperature T, with k_B=1.380649×10⁻²³ J/K. Multiplication by N_A gives the molar gas constant R, approximately 8.314 J/(mol·K). Absolute temperature is measured in kelvin, K; adding 273.15 to a Celsius temperature gives its kelvin value, so 300 K is approximately 26.85 °C. Dividing the molar energy difference by RT compares the state cost with the thermal scale on the same counting basis. Their units cancel, giving the dimensionless argument required by the exponential instead of placing an energy with units directly in its exponent.

Probabilities of three torsional statesEq. 5

![Probabilities of three torsional states](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/bbb4500257bc156fe46ce929.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Δε | Molar energy difference of each gauche state relative to trans | kJ mol⁻¹ |
| R | Gas constant, 0.008314 | kJ mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| T | Absolute temperature | K |
| w | Weight of one gauche state relative to trans | 1 |
| p_{t}, p_{g}+, p_{g}− | Probabilities of trans and each of the two gauche states | 1 |
| exp | Natural exponential function | 1 |

Reading the relationshipTaking trans as zero energy gives weight 1. Two equivalent gauche states each contribute w, so normalization by 1+2w makes the probabilities sum to one.

A worked exampleFor Δε=3 kJ/mol and T=300 K, w≈0.300, the trans probability is about 0.625 and each gauche probability is about 0.188. At Δε=0 all three states have probability 1/3.

ConditionsThree discrete states, equivalent gauche energies and independent local choices; neighboring coupling requires joint-state weights.

Treating every torsion independently already adds chemical information, but neighboring torsions can influence each other. A preceding gauche state may change crowding around the next bond, making a particular pair of states unfavorable. Rotational-isomeric-state models connect discrete local choices through such conditional weights. Protein backbones, polymers with bulky side groups and different polysaccharides require local descriptions appropriate to their chemistry and geometry. Flexibility emerges from these microscopic options together. The presence of a rotatable bond therefore does not imply that every rotation is equally easy or statistically independent.

## Kuhn length: replacing chemical detail with effective steps

Following every chemical bond can be unnecessarily elaborate when the question concerns the overall dimensions of a long chain. Coarse-graining replaces local groups of bonds with effective units so that chemical details enter through fewer statistical parameters. A map can similarly replace a winding road with a smaller set of turning points while preserving the distances relevant to a particular journey. The effective unit is not an arbitrary short fragment, and every microscopic configuration of that fragment need not resemble a rigid rod. It is defined by the properties that the coarse model is required to match.

A common construction matches both contour length and the long-chain mean-square end-to-end distance. The Kuhn length is the segment length of the equivalent freely jointed chain; its effective segment count is the contour length divided by that value. Both matching conditions are needed. A fixed rule such as grouping every few monomers cannot be transferred unchanged between different materials. The contour definition must also be specified: an atom-by-atom zigzag and a smoothed backbone centerline can require a geometric conversion. Comparing parameters is meaningful when the associated definitions are consistent.

Matching contour length and mean-square sizeEq. 6

![Matching contour length and mean-square size](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/543c4d1982e3cb02a4a1ce81.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| b_{K} | Kuhn length | nm |
| N_{K} | Effective Kuhn-segment count, which may be noninteger | 1 |
| L | Contour length under a specified backbone-path convention | nm |
| 〈R²〉₀ | Unperturbed mean-square end-to-end distance; subscript 0 denotes unperturbed statistics | nm² |

Reading the relationshipThe equivalent freely jointed chain matches both contour length N_Kb_K and mean-square size N_Kb_K², determining the two parameters.

A worked exampleFor L=200 nm and 〈R²〉₀=400 nm², b_K=2 nm, N_K=100 and the rms end-to-end distance is 20 nm.

ConditionsA long chain with local correlations coarse-grained and unperturbed statistics at the relevant scale; retain the contour convention with the parameter.

[Figure: diagram](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/en/#en-s5)

Figure 3 · Coarse-graining concept and Kuhn matching conditions. Connecting fewer points illustrates reduced resolution; Kuhn length is determined by contour and mean-square-size matching.

At fixed contour length, a larger Kuhn length corresponds to fewer, longer effective steps and a more extended overall coil. At fixed Kuhn length, increasing the contour length adds steps and increases the typical size according to the square-root law. Both changes enlarge the coil, but for different reasons: one changes local stiffness, while the other adds chain length. When only a few effective segments fit within the chain, long-chain approximations become less accurate. A finite-chain or semiflexible description then retains directional correlations that still matter for the requested observable.

Grouping several independent steps produces a group whose mean-square displacement is the sum of the individual contributions. Fewer groups with larger typical displacements preserve the full chain's mean-square end-to-end distance. This statistical self-similarity underlies ideal-chain descriptions across scales. It does not mean that every short section has exactly the same shape as the entire chain, or that chemical and whole-molecule scales are interchangeable. The useful range begins beyond the local correlation scale and ends where larger-scale interactions or constraints change the statistics. Keeping this range explicit explains why a coarse model can be accurate for one question and insufficient for another.

## Why end-to-end distances form a probability curve

An average size compresses many configurations into one number. Binding, capture and stretching problems often require more: how frequently does a particular separation occur? Adding many independent small displacements makes the total displacement in each coordinate approach a bell-shaped Gaussian distribution. This is a consequence of the central limit theorem when there are enough effective steps and no few extreme contributions dominate. The three-dimensional end-to-end vector combines three coordinate components. With no preferred direction, its probability density depends only on the squared distance from the origin.

A probability density is not the probability of one exact point. Multiplying it by a small volume approximately gives the probability of finding the endpoint in that volume, and integrating over all space gives one. For a single fixed-length step, the endpoint is confined to a sphere. A Dirac delta distribution can represent this constraint mathematically, but it is a concentrated weight under an integral, not an infinite probability assigned to a point. Starting directly from the smooth distribution of many steps keeps the spatial counting clear without requiring that more specialized notation.

Vector density and radial densityEq. 7

![Vector density and radial density](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/7baa3f327bdb1ae705acd3ff.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q | Mean-square end-to-end distance | nm² |
| N, b | Independent segment count and segment length | N: 1; b: nm |
| R (vector), R | End-to-end vector and its nonnegative magnitude | nm |
| p(R (vector)) | Endpoint probability density per spatial volume | nm⁻³ |
| w(R) | Radial probability density per distance interval | nm⁻¹ |
| R_{mode}, R_{rms} | Most probable distance and root-mean-square distance | nm |
| π, exp, √ | Pi, natural exponential and square root | — |

Reading the relationshipMultiplying the three coordinate Gaussian densities gives vector density. Summing directions in a thin shell multiplies by spherical area 4πR² to give radial density.

A worked exampleFor N=100 and b=1 nm, Q=100 nm², the radial peak is near 8.165 nm and the rms distance is 10 nm, while vector density remains maximal at the origin.

ConditionsThree-dimensional long-chain approximation with many independent effective segments, appropriate to typical coiled distances; an actual fixed-segment chain cannot extend beyond its contour.

The vector density is largest at the origin, yet the distribution of distance alone peaks at a nonzero value. A thin spherical shell at a larger radius contains more positions in different directions. A city provides an analogy: its central district can have a high population density while a broad surrounding annulus contains more residents in total. The radial probability density adds contributions from all directions and therefore includes the shell-area factor. This also explains why a zero mean vector, a nonzero most probable distance and a different root-mean-square distance can all describe the same ensemble.

Conformational samples of three-dimensional freely jointed chains. Each calculation uses 2000 chains and the same random sequence for comparison. The curve is a long-chain approximation; numerical feedback also gives the finite-chain gyration result.

Every chain in the interaction is generated in three dimensions. The displayed individual chain is a two-dimensional projection, while all distances are calculated using three coordinates. Vary segment number and compare contour length, root-mean-square end-to-end distance and radius of gyration. Then hold the segment count fixed and change segment length: all spatial distances scale by the same factor. The histogram represents many independent configurations, and the smooth curve is the long-chain Gaussian approximation. Finite sampling produces fluctuations, while shorter chains can differ systematically in the tails. A single snapshot, a finite-sample average and a theoretical limiting result are distinct levels of description.

The Gaussian approximation has a clear geometric boundary. A chain of fixed-length segments reaches its greatest end-to-end distance when every segment aligns, giving the contour length. A Gaussian distribution nevertheless has a very small tail at arbitrarily large distances. For a long chain near its usual coiled size, this discrepancy is small. Near full extension it becomes decisive. A probability model should therefore be applied within the range that supports its derivation. The same distinction determines whether its predicted force remains useful when the chain is strongly stretched.

## A restoring force without stretching chemical bonds

Gently separating the ends of a flexible chain initially changes segment orientations, often without substantially stretching individual chemical bonds. An unconstrained chain can adopt many coiled arrangements. Holding its ends far apart leaves fewer compatible arrangements. Entropy measures the availability of microscopic configurations, and reducing that availability raises the free energy under the relevant conditions. The chain consequently exerts a mean restoring force on its anchors. This contribution is called entropic elasticity. In a rubber network, many connected chain segments transmit such tendencies into a macroscopic restoring force.

The Gaussian vector density gives the free-energy cost of fixing an endpoint at a specified position. A natural logarithm converts statistical weights into an additive free-energy contribution. Differentiating with respect to displacement gives the mean external force needed to maintain that position. The constraint concerns the endpoint's position in space, rather than only its distance while it remains free to move over a spherical shell. Using the radial density instead would introduce shell-position counting into a different constrained problem. Identifying the constraint first determines which probability belongs in the calculation.

The force on one chain is small and is commonly expressed in piconewtons, pN: one piconewton equals 10⁻¹² N. Force multiplied by displacement along its direction has units of energy, so 1 pN·nm equals 10⁻²¹ J. These units keep molecular forces and distances within convenient numerical ranges. At 300 K, the thermal scale k_BT is about 4.142 pN·nm. The free-energy difference below uses this energy unit; taking its rate of change with displacement in nanometers leaves piconewtons, giving the force required to hold the endpoint in place.

Entropic elasticity at fixed endpoint positionEq. 8

![Entropic elasticity at fixed endpoint position](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/c25a81a4ee410a72b2811b98.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ΔF | Free-energy difference relative to an endpoint at the origin | pN nm |
| k_{B} | Boltzmann constant, 0.01380649 pN·nm/K | pN nm K⁻¹ |
| T | Absolute temperature | K |
| R (vector), R, 0 (vector) | End-to-end vector, magnitude and zero vector | nm |
| p | Probability density of endpoint-vector position | nm⁻³ |
| N, b | Effective segment count and length | N: 1; b: nm |
| ln | Natural logarithm; its density-ratio argument is dimensionless | 1 |
| f_{hold} | Magnitude of the mean external holding force | pN |
| dΔF/dR | Rate of free-energy change with distance | pN |

Reading the relationshipFixing the endpoint reduces configuration weight; −k_BT times its logarithm gives the free-energy cost. Its displacement derivative gives holding force; chain restoring force points oppositely.

A worked exampleAt T=300 K, N=100, b=1 nm and R=5 nm, k_BT=4.142 pN·nm, the spring constant is 0.1243 pN/nm and the holding force is about 0.621 pN.

ConditionsAn equilibrium Gaussian chain with fixed vector endpoint and extension well below contour length; Nb² is defined under the specified conditions.

[Figure: diagram](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/en/#en-s7)

Figure 4 · Illustration of the Rouse bead–spring idea: a coarse connection carries subchain entropic elasticity. The rows compare conformational freedom rather than measured force–extension data.

Within its range of validity, the relation resembles an ordinary spring: greater displacement requires greater holding force. Its spring constant, however, comes from temperature and the chain's statistical dimensions. Holding other parameters fixed, raising temperature increases the free-energy cost of losing configurational entropy. A longer chain offers more rearrangement options and generally requires less force for the same endpoint displacement. Actual materials can also change Kuhn length, interactions or network structure when heated, so these contributions should accompany the entropic comparison when interpreting temperature-dependent experiments.

Near the contour length, the remaining orientation choices become scarce and finite extensibility becomes essential. A linear Gaussian spring must then give way to a more suitable description. Stronger forces may stretch bonds, unfold a local structure or rupture an association, each with its own energetic and kinetic behavior. Single-molecule force–extension measurements are useful because they can distinguish successive regimes: conformational adjustment, suppression of bending and changes within the molecular structure. Connecting a curve's change in slope to the relevant process gives a physical meaning to a measured increase in stiffness.

## From flexible coils to semiflexible rods

A short thin strip can appear almost straight, while a much longer strip of the same material bends appreciably. Whether a polymer appears flexible also depends on observation length. Persistence length describes how directional memory decays along the contour. Starting from one point and following the chain, the local tangent gradually loses correlation with its initial direction. In the simple wormlike-chain model, the correlation falls to about 37% after one persistence length. The separation is contour distance traveled along the chain, rather than straight-line spatial distance. Larger persistence length means that local orientation persists farther.

[Kratky and Porod's 1949 work](https://doi.org/10.1002/recl.19490681203) connected local chain stiffness to scattering from molecules in solution. The wormlike chain represents the backbone as a continuous bendable line and describes the transition from locally rod-like behavior to an overall coil. A contour much shorter than the persistence length offers little opportunity to accumulate large bends. A much longer contour contains widely separated portions whose directions have largely decorrelated. One model thus includes both appearances without assigning a material a permanently rigid or permanently flexible identity.

Directional correlation and size of a bendable contourEq. 9

![Directional correlation and size of a bendable contour](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/eee2bf7a02ebc3fb618e681a.svg)

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| t(s), t(0) (vector) | Unit tangent vectors at contour positions s and 0 | 1 |
| s, L | Contour separation and total contour length | nm |
| ℓ_p | Persistence length | nm |
| R | End-to-end distance | nm |
| b_{K} | Long-chain equivalent Kuhn length | nm |
| 〈 〉, ·, exp | Conformational average, dot product and natural exponential | — |
| ≫, ≃ | Much greater than; approximation in that limit | — |

Reading the relationshipTotal displacement accumulates tangent vectors along the contour. Integrating their exponential pair correlation gives the mean-square end-to-end distance; the end correction becomes relatively small for long chains.

A worked exampleFor L=100 nm and ℓ_p=10 nm, 〈R²〉≈1800.009 nm² and the rms distance is about 42.43 nm. The leading long-chain value 2000 nm² is still about 11.1% higher, showing the value of the finite-length correction.

ConditionsA three-dimensional, unforced, homogeneous inextensible wormlike chain with constant local bending stiffness and no long-range interactions.

[Figure: diagram](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/biomaterials-courses/cp03/en/#en-s8)

Figure 5 · Tangent correlation in the Kratky–Porod continuum model. The brown curve has a larger persistence length and retains directional memory farther along the contour.

In the long-chain limit of this continuous model, the Kuhn length is twice the persistence length. The factor follows from integrating tangent correlations and matching the contour length. For other discrete-angle models or short chains, the definitions and conversion should be checked explicitly.
