# Connecting Symbolic Mathematics to Numerical Computation

Source: https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p24/en/
Language: en

Derive force and stiffness from elastic energy with SymPy, then use exact algebra to understand numerical error.

## Begin with an elastic element in your hand

Opening a clip, compressing a spring, or stretching a flexible connector gives a familiar sensation: resistance changes as the object moves. Suppose an expression describes the energy stored in that element. Can it also tell us the force required to hold a displacement, and how much extra force a small additional movement will require? These are questions about energy, force, and stiffness. They provide a connected way to learn symbolic computation: derive relationships while retaining letters, then supply parameters and displacement values to obtain corresponding curves.

We will use a deliberately simple elastic energy model throughout. Loading is slow, work supplied by the applied force is stored in the element, and unloading follows the same relation in reverse. This describes reversible elastic response. A measured loop, a dependence on loading speed, or permanent deformation calls for additional variables describing dissipation or internal state. Understanding this small model makes the connection between a physical assumption and a formula's purpose concrete.

SymPy stores and transforms the expressions, NumPy evaluates arrays of displacement values, and Matplotlib displays the physical quantities. We will also estimate force by subtracting two nearby energy values and dividing by their separation. Comparing that estimate with a symbolic derivative reveals why making a numerical step extremely small can eventually make a calculation worse.

## Put energy, displacement, and units together

Think of stored energy as mechanical work gradually deposited in an element. A larger displacement generally stores more, while each equal increment of displacement can require a different amount of work. A quadratic term describes a simple elastic energy. Adding a quartic term allows resistance to rise more rapidly at larger displacements. Two coefficients control their contributions. These are chosen inputs to a teaching model; the plotted values are evaluations of that model.

$$
U(x)=\frac{kx^2}{2}+\frac{\alpha x^4}{4},\qquad k>0,\quad \alpha\geq0
$$

| Symbol | Meaning and units |
| --- | --- |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/9469b6261e047457191334c2.svg) | Elastic energy at displacement x, mJ; U(0) = 0. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/fcc5df999e3b49fae1685ee0.svg) | Displacement from the undeformed position, mm; its sign indicates direction. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/8dc6f7e80ecaac9fa07890ce.svg) | Quadratic energy coefficient and tangent stiffness at the origin, N/mm. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/7995b2daef1650484d2fa651.svg) | Quartic energy coefficient, N/mm³. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/96d66c13fb959b10fd625f8f.svg) | Dimensionless denominator constants; superscripts 2 and 4 denote second and fourth powers. |

For k = 2 N/mm, α = 0.5 N/mm³, and x = 1 mm, U = 2 × 1² / 2 + 0.5 × 1⁴ / 4 = 1.125 N·mm = 1.125 mJ. Both terms have energy units. Setting α to zero retains quadratic energy; positive α adds a contribution that grows faster at larger displacement.

Powers apply to units as well as numerical values. Squared displacement has units of square millimeters. Multiplying by newtons per millimeter produces newton millimeters. The quartic coefficient needs units of newtons per cubic millimeter so that its contribution has the same energy units. Checking that addition combines like quantities can reveal an incorrect exponent or coefficient. Throughout this example, displacement is entered in millimeters and energy is reported in millijoules: one newton millimeter equals one millijoule.

With a quadratic coefficient of 2 N/mm and a quartic coefficient of 0.5 N/mm³, a displacement of 1 mm stores 1 mJ in the quadratic contribution and 0.125 mJ in the quartic contribution. At 2 mm, these become 4 mJ and 2 mJ, giving 6 mJ altogether. Doubling displacement multiplies the quadratic contribution by four and the quartic contribution by sixteen. These numbers already explain why the higher power becomes more prominent farther from the origin.

The energy at zero displacement is chosen as zero. Adding the same constant everywhere changes this reference but leaves energy differences and forces unchanged. Changing displacement units is different: converting from millimeters to meters requires converting both coefficients as well. Relabeling the horizontal axis alone would change the physical interpretation of every calculated point.

Symmetry can be checked before inserting numbers. Both energy terms contain even powers, so equal displacements in opposite directions store equal energy. Holding forces consequently have equal magnitudes and opposite signs, while tangent stiffness is the same on both sides. This is a concrete assumption encoded by the formula. An element with different tensile and compressive responses requires an energy model that captures that distinction.

## Why the slope of energy gives force

Consider a short loading interval over which the applied force is nearly constant. Work is force multiplied by displacement increment. Dividing the increase in energy by that increment therefore gives the average force over the interval. On an energy graph, this ratio is the slope of a line joining two points. As the points approach one another, the average approaches the force at a particular position and the line approaches a tangent. A derivative describes this local rate of change.

$$
F(x)=\frac{\mathrm dU}{\mathrm dx}=kx+\alpha x^3,\qquad K(x)=\frac{\mathrm dF}{\mathrm dx}=k+3\alpha x^2
$$

| Symbol | Meaning and units |
| --- | --- |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/d7f42ff2aa801298d0b0e10a.svg) | Applied force holding a displacement during slow loading, N; the restoring force is −F. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/c18cc14db4443d05e8ca8d27.svg) | Tangent stiffness at the current position, N/mm. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/d2936881a9db32d00d3ef560.svg) | U is stored energy, mJ; x is displacement, mm. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/c716d1023aa9003462dc1854.svg) | k is the quadratic coefficient, N/mm; α the quartic coefficient, N/mm³. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/d7307287aa169cbb98be8758.svg) | Derivative with respect to displacement: local change per unit displacement. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/6cb44f25e489afb06ec62d2e.svg) | Dimensionless coefficient obtained by differentiating x³ to give 3x². |

For a power, bring the exponent forward and reduce it by one: x² becomes 2x and x⁴ becomes 4x³, canceling the energy denominators. With k = 2, α = 0.5, and x = 1 in the defined units, F = 2 + 0.5 = 2.5 N and K = 2 + 3 × 0.5 = 3.5 N/mm. The first derivative connects energy slope to force, and the next connects force slope to stiffness.

Positive force here means the external force needed to hold a positive displacement. The element's restoring force points in the opposite direction, toward lower energy, and has the opposite sign. Identifying which object exerts the force resolves the apparent sign difference between familiar energy formulas. Differentiating once more gives tangent stiffness: the local rate at which required force rises with displacement.

At 1 mm, holding force is 2.5 N and tangent stiffness is 3.5 N/mm. An additional displacement of 0.01 mm therefore increases force by approximately 0.035 N. The complete expression gives 0.0351505 N, differing by about 0.0001505 N. The local slope is useful for small increments. Over a longer interval, stiffness changes along the path, so evaluate the full force at both endpoints and subtract.

![Energy, applied force, and tangent stiffness from one model. Colors compare α = 0, 0.5, and 2 N/mm³, with k = 2 N/mm throughout. Blue markers track three corresponding values at x = 1 mm. Curves are model evaluations.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/22fa82ae00c17ce447225822.svg?v=22fa82ae00c1)

Figure 1Energy, applied force, and tangent stiffness from one model. Colors compare α = 0, 0.5, and 2 N/mm³, with k = 2 N/mm throughout. Blue markers track three corresponding values at x = 1 mm. Curves are model evaluations.

The three panels use identical parameters to show energy, applied force, and stiffness. With the quartic term set to zero, the gray force curve is linear and stiffness is constant. The blue and orange models retain the quartic term, so stiffness increases with displacement. A high energy value and a steep energy slope have different meanings and units. Reading the axis labels and the derivative linking each pair of panels keeps those meanings distinct.

## Keep the letters meaningful and the fractions exact

The statement `x = sp.Symbol('x', real=True)` creates a symbol representing a real number; it does not yet choose a displacement. The coefficient `k` is positive and `alpha` is nonnegative. Including zero lets us compare models with and without the quartic contribution. These assumptions guide algebraic operations. For example, the square root of a squared real displacement is its absolute value. At −2 mm the result is 2 mm, which explains why retaining the absolute value matters.

The program constructs coefficients with `sp.Rational(1, 2)` and `sp.Rational(1, 4)`. Both fractions happen to have exact binary floating-point representations, but rational objects keep the derivation in exact arithmetic. The benefit becomes especially visible with one third. Ordinary division between Python integers is evaluated before its result enters a symbolic expression. A Rational object instead retains a numerator and denominator. Conversion to a decimal can wait until a numerical result is needed.

Substituting values returns a new expression while preserving the general one. This resembles keeping both an unfilled calculation sheet and a version containing one element's parameters. Supplying the two coefficients leaves displacement as a free symbol; supplying displacement as well produces a definite energy. Inspecting `free_symbols` helps locate a parameter that has not yet been assigned. The separation also makes it easy to evaluate the same general model for several parameter sets.

These symbolic objects carry algebraic relationships, while this example manages units through explicit definitions and consistent numerical conventions. Naming a symbol displacement does not automatically attach millimeters to it. When extending the model, list the input and output units, then check each added term and derivative. A successful program execution then corresponds to an understandable physical calculation.

## How a formula becomes something a computer can transform

A picture of a formula can be displayed, but taking its derivative requires an operational representation. In their 2017 paper describing SymPy, Meurer and colleagues explained expression trees: operations form nodes, symbols and constants form leaves, and algebraic transformations consume and construct these structures. Implementing the system as a Python library connects symbolic work to the surrounding scientific ecosystem. The authors' openly available paper sources explain the architecture behind this connection.

![Original model illustration: thirteen nodes read recursively from the actual SymPy expression show how sums, products, powers, and rational numbers form energy. The expression and its derivative appear below. The 2017 paper discusses this architecture; the spring model is constructed for this chapter.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/ce6234471836d23e588a0d28.svg?v=ce6234471836)

Figure 2Original model illustration: thirteen nodes read recursively from the actual SymPy expression show how sums, products, powers, and rational numbers form energy. The expression and its derivative appear below. The 2017 paper discusses this architecture; the spring model is constructed for this chapter.

The top Add node combines two terms. Each Mul branch multiplies a rational coefficient, a parameter, and a displacement power. A Pow node connects the displacement to its exponent. The illustration is generated from the actual energy expression, so each branch corresponds to its `func` and `args` structure. Symbols and fractions have no further children in this algebraic representation. Following a branch from top to bottom provides a practical reading of how the formula is stored.

This also explains a distinction between mathematical equality and matching structure. A polynomial written as a product can have a different tree from its expanded sum. Python assignment gives an object a name; `sp.Eq` constructs an equation; `==` compares the structure of SymPy expressions. To check the polynomial identities used here, expand or simplify the difference and see whether it becomes zero. Substituting several numerical values is also useful for finding mistakes in a proposed identity.

For the spring, the same stored expression produces both force and stiffness, and integrating force reconstructs energy. Changing the energy model therefore regenerates related quantities from a common mathematical definition. This organization helps keep coefficients and powers consistent across calculations. The tree illustration exposes the representation that makes those operations possible.

## Turn a derived expression into a numerical curve

Letters are useful during a derivation, while plotting needs numerical values. The call `lambdify((x, k, alpha), U, modules='numpy')` constructs a callable numerical function. The ordered tuple specifies the argument order. Passing a displacement array and the two coefficients returns the corresponding energy values. Force and stiffness are converted in the same way. This is a deliberate transition from a completed symbolic expression to array-based evaluation.

The displacement array contains 401 equally spaced positions from 0 to 2 mm, separated by 0.005 mm. The exported model table keeps displacement, energy, force, and stiffness in the same row. At 1 mm, a reader can inspect 1.125 mJ, 2.5 N, and 3.5 N/mm together. Increasing the number of plotted points gives a finer display of the same model; it does not add a new physical parameter or create extra measurements.

The model can also answer an inverse question: which displacement requires a force of 3 N? The program subtracts 3 from the force expression and passes the result to `nsolve`, starting at 1 mm. The solution is approximately 1.134728 mm. Substituting it back checks the force balance. Because tangent stiffness is positive throughout this model, force increases strictly with displacement, giving one real equilibrium displacement for each prescribed force. That uniqueness follows from the model's slope.

$$
W_{0\to b}=\int_0^b F(s)\,\mathrm ds=U(b)-U(0)
$$

| Symbol | Meaning and units |
| --- | --- |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/cfa1aa9ce37fea73c98f0d1b.svg) | Work supplied while slowly loading from displacement 0 to b, mJ. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/a77a353782459b753313d802.svg) | Final loading displacement, mm. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/b8208c8407bd0942fcaa88f9.svg) | Integration variable for displacement, mm; it varies from 0 to b. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/553badbaf2c0b915d0d4369a.svg) | Applied force at displacement s, N. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/eafdac3dd6a477b3670861c5.svg) | The integral accumulates work over small displacement increments; ds has units of mm. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/fdd3a5a8d8d6ca2f49a8ba46.svg) | Stored energies at the final and initial positions, mJ. |

For b = 2 mm, k = 2 N/mm, and α = 0.5 N/mm³, integration gives k b² / 2 + α b⁴ / 4 = 4 + 2 = 6 mJ. Initial energy is zero, so work equals final stored energy. The symbol s distinguishes the varying integration coordinate from the fixed endpoint b.

Integration adds the work of all the small loading increments. Loading from 0 to 2 mm stores 6 mJ, equal to the final energy minus the initial energy. Multiplying the final force of 8 N by the entire displacement would give 16 mJ. That calculation assumes 8 N was applied throughout, although the force actually rose from zero. The relevant work is the area under the complete force curve, giving a direct mechanical interpretation of the symbolic integral.

An initial guess and a model parameter play different roles. The guess specifies where a numerical search begins; changing it should still lead to the unique equilibrium in this example when the search converges. Changing a stiffness coefficient changes the element and shifts equilibrium. More complicated energy functions can have multiple equilibria. Their interpretation then involves the allowed domain and the behavior of energy near each solution. Reading the force curve before interpreting the returned position connects the solver to the physical picture.

## Why the smallest difference step is not always the best

A function that returns energy values is enough to estimate force numerically. Evaluate the function on both sides of the target position and divide the energy difference by their separation. This centered difference uses information symmetrically. With half-spacing h, the full separation is 2h; omitting that factor of two doubles the estimated force. For the quartic energy used here, SymPy can expand the complete difference between this estimate and the derivative.

$$
D_hU(x)=\frac{U(x+h)-U(x-h)}{2h},\qquad D_hU(x)-F(x)=\alpha xh^2
$$

| Symbol | Meaning and units |
| --- | --- |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/732aa542b12ff5c3ed36159d.svg) | Centered-difference estimate of force with half-spacing h, N. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/a83c7a267ed0d7a6190ac2db.svg) | Stored energies on either side of the center, mJ. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/8c42b0b36a7b3ec0bebfa150.svg) | x is central displacement and h a positive half-spacing, both mm; the points are 2h apart. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/d7f42ff2aa801298d0b0e10a.svg) | Applied force obtained from the symbolic derivative, N. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/7995b2daef1650484d2fa651.svg) | Quartic energy coefficient, N/mm³. |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/f5f3224583db57b9cfe323c8.svg) | The denominator factor 2 converts half-spacing to full spacing; superscript 2 denotes squaring. |

Substitute x+h and x−h into energy and expand. Subtraction cancels terms with even powers of h; division by 2h leaves kx + αx³ + αxh². The first two terms are F, leaving the exact-arithmetic truncation error. For α = 0.5 N/mm³, x = 1 mm, and h = 0.1 mm, it is 0.005 N and the difference estimate is 2.505 N. Floating-point evaluation adds rounding effects.

At 1 mm with a half-spacing of 0.1 mm, the exact-arithmetic estimate is 2.505 N, exceeding the derivative by 0.005 N. Halving the spacing to 0.05 mm reduces this error to 0.00125 N, a factor of four. The squared step in the error expression explains the phrase second-order accuracy with a directly calculable example. When the quartic coefficient is zero, the centered difference of the quadratic energy gives the exact derivative in exact arithmetic.

![At left, compare the tangent at x = 1 mm with a secant using half-spacing 0.2 mm. At right, evaluate 170 steps for the same model. Orange is the exact-arithmetic error αxh²; blue is absolute error from actual NumPy evaluation. Horizontal axes represent position and step size, respectively.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/2c2e3527960f342948be0a26.svg?v=2c2e3527960f)

Figure 3At left, compare the tangent at x = 1 mm with a secant using half-spacing 0.2 mm. At right, evaluate 170 steps for the same model. Orange is the exact-arithmetic error αxh²; blue is absolute error from actual NumPy evaluation. Horizontal axes represent position and step size, respectively.

Floating-point arithmetic adds a competing effect. Very close positions have very close energy values. Subtraction leaves a small difference, so rounding errors in the original values can become a substantial fraction of that difference. Dividing by a still smaller separation magnifies the effect. The error plot initially follows the predicted square-law decrease, then fluctuates and rises as the step becomes extremely small. Details depend on operation order and floating-point implementation; the competition between the two error mechanisms is the useful pattern.

A symbolic derivative supplies a clear reference in this example. The difference calculation shows what happens when only evaluations of the energy function are used. Studying both on a tractable problem provides a method for examining more complicated functions. When a derivative can be generated from the model, use that mathematical structure. When differences are needed, compare several step sizes and look for a stable region.

The vertical error axis uses newtons and reports the absolute difference from the derivative. Scaling up the forces can also scale up absolute error. Comparisons across models may therefore benefit from normalization by a clearly defined reference force. Dividing by the local force becomes problematic near zero force, so selecting a reference scale is part of defining the numerical question. Absolute error here connects directly to the worked value of 0.005 N.

## A complete program from derivation to figures

The program creates symbols with assumptions, constructs energy using exact fractions, and derives force, stiffness, and the centered-difference error. It then substitutes a common parameter set, records key values in a numerical summary, and generates model and error tables. The three figures show connected physical quantities, the actual expression tree, and competing numerical errors. Every plotted model value, tree node, and error point comes from the calculation.

### Complete example: from energy expression to numerical error

Generate model and error CSV tables, a numerical summary, and three figures. SymPy performs derivation and solving; NumPy evaluates arrays.

```
"""Derive a spring model symbolically, then evaluate it with NumPy."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import json
import numpy as np
import sympy as sp
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager


def expression_tree(ax, expression):
    """Draw the actual func/args structure; each leaf receives one position."""
    nodes, edges = [], []
    next_leaf = [0]

    def visit(expr, depth=0):
        index = len(nodes)
        nodes.append(None)
        children = [visit(child, depth + 1) for child in expr.args]
        if children:
            horizontal = np.mean([nodes[child][0] for child in children])
        else:
            horizontal = next_leaf[0]
            next_leaf[0] += 1
        label = expr.func.__name__ if children else str(expr)
        nodes[index] = (horizontal, -depth, label, bool(children))
        edges.extend((index, child) for child in children)
        return index

    visit(expression)
    for parent, child in edges:
        a, b = nodes[parent], nodes[child]
        ax.plot([a[0], b[0]], [a[1], b[1]], color='#b7c6cd', lw=1.7, zorder=0)
    for x, y, label, branch in nodes:
        ax.text(x, y, label, ha='center', va='center', fontsize=14,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=.48', facecolor='#eaf2f5' if branch else '#fbf1e9',
                          edgecolor='#28658c' if branch else '#b36837', lw=1.3))
    ax.set(xlim=(-.65, next_leaf[0] - .35), ylim=(-3.65, .65))
    ax.axis('off')
    return len(nodes)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--language', choices=['zh', 'en'], default='en')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tr = lambda zh, en: zh if args.language == 'zh' else en
    available = {f.name for f in font_manager.fontManager.ttflist}
    plt.rcParams.update({'font.family': [f for f in ['Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Noto Sans SC',
        'Microsoft YaHei', 'SimHei', 'DejaVu Sans'] if f in available],
        'font.size': 12, 'svg.fonttype': 'none', 'axes.spines.top': False,
        'axes.spines.right': False, 'grid.alpha': .16})

    def save(fig, name):
        fig.savefig(args.output / f'{name}-{args.language}.svg')
        fig.savefig(args.output / f'{name}-{args.language}.png', dpi=160)
        plt.close(fig)

    # Numerical values use mm, N, and N*mm (= mJ) consistently.
    x = sp.Symbol('x', real=True)
    k = sp.Symbol('k', positive=True)
    alpha = sp.Symbol('alpha', nonnegative=True)
    h = sp.Symbol('h', positive=True)
    U = sp.Rational(1, 2) * k * x**2 + sp.Rational(1, 4) * alpha * x**4
    F = sp.diff(U, x)
    K = sp.diff(F, x)
    reconstructed = sp.integrate(F, x)
    assert sp.simplify(reconstructed - U) == 0
    centered = (U.subs(x, x + h) - U.subs(x, x - h)) / (2 * h)
    truncation = sp.expand(centered - F)
    assert sp.simplify(truncation - alpha * x * h**2) == 0
    values = {k: sp.Integer(2), alpha: sp.Rational(1, 2)}
    exact_one = [expr.subs(values).subs(x, 1) for expr in (U, F, K)]
    work = sp.integrate(F.subs(values), (x, 0, 2))
    equilibrium = sp.nsolve(F.subs(values) - 3, x, 1, prec=40)
    equilibrium_residual = abs((F.subs(values) - 3).subs(x, equilibrium))
    u_num = sp.lambdify((x, k, alpha), U, modules='numpy')
    f_num = sp.lambdify((x, k, alpha), F, modules='numpy')
    stiffness_num = sp.lambdify((x, k, alpha), K, modules='numpy')
    grid = np.linspace(0, 2, 401)
    energy = u_num(grid, 2., .5)
    force = f_num(grid, 2., .5)
    stiffness = stiffness_num(grid, 2., .5)
    np.savetxt(args.output / 'model.csv', np.column_stack([grid, energy, force, stiffness]),
               delimiter=',', header='displacement_mm,energy_mJ,force_N,stiffness_N_per_mm', comments='')

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13.4, 5.2), layout='constrained')
    for a, color in zip([0., .5, 2.], ['#82939b', '#28658c', '#c26835']):
        for ax, fn in zip(axes, [u_num, f_num, stiffness_num]):
            output = np.broadcast_to(fn(grid, 2., a), grid.shape)
            ax.plot(grid, output, color=color, lw=2.3, label=f'α = {a:g} N/mm³')
    for ax, value, title, ylabel in zip(axes, [1.125, 2.5, 3.5],
        [tr('A  储存了多少能量', 'A  Stored energy'), tr('B  维持位移的外力', 'B  Holding force'),
         tr('C  当前有多难再拉长', 'C  Tangent stiffness')],
        [tr('储能 U / mJ', 'Energy U / mJ'), tr('外力 F / N', 'Applied force F / N'),
         tr('切线刚度 K / (N/mm)', 'Tangent stiffness K / (N/mm)')]):
        ax.scatter([1], [value], s=58, color='#28658c', edgecolor='white', zorder=5)
        ax.annotate(f'{value:g}', (1, value), xytext=(6, 10), textcoords='offset points', color='#28658c',
                    bbox=dict(facecolor='white', edgecolor='none', alpha=.85, pad=.5))
        ax.set(title=title, xlabel=tr('位移 x / mm', 'Displacement x / mm'), ylabel=ylabel, xlim=(0, 2))
        ax.set_xticks([0, .5, 1, 1.5, 2]); ax.grid(True)
    axes[0].legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=11)
    fig.suptitle(tr('同一个储能函数的三个读法；k = 2 N/mm',
                       'Three readings of one energy function; k = 2 N/mm'), fontsize=16)
    save(fig, 'mechanics')

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6.8), layout='constrained')
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 1, height_ratios=[4, 1])
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0]); node_count = expression_tree(ax, U)
    ax.set_title(tr('SymPy的2017年论文：表达式树架构',
                       'Expression-tree architecture in the 2017 SymPy paper'), fontsize=16, pad=14)
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1]); ax.axis('off')
    ax.text(.02, .73, '$U=' + sp.latex(U) + '$', fontsize=19, transform=ax.transAxes)
    ax.text(.55, .73, '$F=' + sp.latex(F) + '$', fontsize=19, transform=ax.transAxes)
    ax.text(.02, .05, tr('Add：相加     Mul：相乘     Pow：乘方；叶子保留符号和精确分数。',
        'Add: sum     Mul: product     Pow: power; leaves retain symbols and exact fractions.'),
        fontsize=12, transform=ax.transAxes)
    save(fig, 'history')

    steps = np.logspace(-14, -1, 170)
    differences = (u_num(1 + steps, 2., .5) - u_num(1 - steps, 2., .5)) / (2 * steps)
    errors = abs(differences - 2.5)
    exact_error = .5 * steps**2
    np.savetxt(args.output / 'difference-error.csv', np.column_stack([steps, differences, errors, exact_error]),
        delimiter=',', header='step_mm,centered_force_N,absolute_error_N,exact_arithmetic_error_N', comments='')
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12.5, 6), layout='constrained', gridspec_kw={'width_ratios': [1, 1.22]})
    local = np.linspace(.65, 1.35, 200); hh = .2
    secant = float((u_num(1 + hh, 2., .5) - u_num(1 - hh, 2., .5)) / (2 * hh))
    intercept = float((u_num(1 + hh, 2., .5) + u_num(1 - hh, 2., .5)) / 2)
    axes[0].plot(local, u_num(local, 2., .5), color='#28658c', lw=2.5, label=tr('能量曲线', 'Energy'))
    axes[0].plot(local, 1.125 + 2.5 * (local - 1), color='#2b8a74', ls='--', label=tr('中心切线', 'Center tangent'))
    axes[0].plot(local, intercept + secant * (local - 1), color='#c26835', ls=':', lw=2.4, label=tr('两点割线', 'Two-point secant'))
    axes[0].scatter([.8, 1.2], u_num(np.array([.8, 1.2]), 2., .5), color='#c26835', zorder=5)
    axes[0].set(title=tr('A  先看斜率的几何意义', 'A  Read slope geometrically'),
        xlabel=tr('位移 / mm', 'Displacement / mm'), ylabel=tr('储能 / mJ', 'Stored energy / mJ'))
    axes[0].legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=11); axes[0].grid(True)
    positive = errors > 0
    axes[1].loglog(steps[positive], errors[positive], color='#28658c', lw=1.2, marker='.', ms=3,
                  label=tr('NumPy浮点计算', 'NumPy floating-point calculation'))
    axes[1].loglog(steps, exact_error, color='#c26835', lw=2.2, ls='--',
                  label=tr('精确算术：αxh²', 'Exact arithmetic: αxh²'))
    axes[1].set(title=tr('B  步长与力的绝对误差', 'B  Step size and absolute force error'),
        xlabel=tr('半间距 h / mm', 'Half-spacing h / mm'), ylabel=tr('绝对误差 / N', 'Absolute error / N'),
        ylim=(1e-17, .1))
    axes[1].legend(loc='upper center', fontsize=11); axes[1].grid(True, which='major')
    fig.suptitle(tr('x = 1 mm，k = 2 N/mm，α = 0.5 N/mm³；左图 h = 0.2 mm',
                       'x = 1 mm, k = 2 N/mm, α = 0.5 N/mm³; left panel h = 0.2 mm'), fontsize=14)
    save(fig, 'difference')
    summary = {'sympy_version': sp.__version__, 'energy_expression': str(U), 'force_expression': str(F),
        'stiffness_expression': str(K), 'truncation_expression': str(truncation),
        'energy_at_1_mJ': float(exact_one[0]), 'force_at_1_N': float(exact_one[1]),
        'stiffness_at_1_N_per_mm': float(exact_one[2]), 'work_0_to_2_mJ': float(work),
        'equilibrium_3N_mm': float(equilibrium), 'equilibrium_residual_N': float(equilibrium_residual),
        'centered_h01_N': float(centered.subs(values).subs({x: 1, h: sp.Rational(1, 10)})),
        'exact_h01_error_N': .005, 'expression_tree_nodes': node_count,
        'sqrt_real_x_squared': str(sp.sqrt(x**2)), 'zero_float_errors': int((errors == 0).sum()),
        'minimum_positive_float_error_N': float(errors[positive].min()),
        'maximum_float_error_N': float(errors.max())}
    (args.output / 'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

Start inspecting the output with the three results at 1 mm, followed by the work from 0 to 2 mm. The field `equilibrium_3N_mm` records the inverse solution and `truncation_expression` records the exact difference identity. The error table retains each step, estimated force, absolute numerical error, and exact-arithmetic error, allowing a plotted point to be traced to its values. A logarithmic vertical axis accepts positive values; any exactly zero numerical errors are counted and omitted from that curve. The count was zero in the displayed run.

For a first modification, set the quartic coefficient to zero and check that force becomes linear and stiffness constant. Restore it, then consider adding a new energy contribution and examine how its derivative and units change. Altering one component at a time makes the relationship between formulas and figures easy to follow. Choosing an energy term for a particular material requires matching the physical response that the model is meant to describe.

## Explore energy, force, and calculation error together

Keep the default position of 1 mm and quartic coefficient of 0.5 N/mm³, and locate the energy of 1.125 mJ and force of 2.5 N. The upper panel shows the energy curve, the tangent at the current position, and the two evaluation points. The lower-left panel follows force at that position. The lower-right panel displays errors across step sizes and highlights the selected step. All views update together, separating a change in the physical model from a change in numerical resolution.

# 从公开接口获取可追溯的数据

Source: https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p25/
Language: zh-CN

从四个蛋白质数据库条目出发，把网址、嵌套 JSON、科学含义与可重复的数据表连接起来。

## 一张结构表，是怎样从数据库来到电脑里的

准备比较蛋白质或核酸结构时，我们常常先做一张表：每个结构叫什么名字，用哪种实验方法得到，包含多少个原子，结构的分辨率是多少。如果只有两条记录，打开网页抄写似乎很快；当记录增加到几十条，真正耗时的事情便出现了：有的数字藏在不同栏目里，有的条目没有同一种指标，有的字段更新后需要重新检查。Python 适合接手这一段重复劳动。数据库提供一种供程序访问的入口，称为应用程序接口，通常简称 API。程序按约定的地址提出请求，数据库返回结构清楚的数据，随后我们再根据科学问题挑选字段、检查含义、生成表格和图。

本章使用 RCSB Protein Data Bank 的公开接口，读取 1UBQ、4HHB、1BNA 和 1D3Z 四个条目。它们分别涉及泛素、血红蛋白、DNA 和溶液核磁共振得到的泛素结构。这样的选择有一个具体目的：前三个条目能在衍射分辨率这一列中比较，第四个条目则要求我们认真处理“这一指标不适用于当前实验方法”的情况。学习结束时，你会得到四份保留原始内容的 JSON 文件、一张字段含义明确的 CSV 表，以及能够解释这些数字的图。更重要的是，你能沿着表格中的任意一个数值，找回它来自哪个条目、哪一层字段、哪一份原始响应。

API 可以理解为图书馆的标准借阅窗口。网址说明要找哪本书，请求说明想执行什么操作，响应状态说明这次办理是否成功，而返回的内容才是交到你手上的材料。这个类比还包含一个容易忽略的细节：借阅成功并不意味着这本书恰好回答你的研究问题。程序仍要核对身份和内容。我们会把网络通信与科学解释分别做好，再将它们接起来，因此遇到新的数据库时，能够沿用相同的工作方法，而不必重新猜测每一步的职责。

## 从共享坐标到可以连接的数据记录

蛋白质数据库在 1971 年宣布建立。结构研究需要共享的核心成果之一，是原子在三维空间中的坐标；有了坐标，其他研究者才能查看分子形状、计算距离、比较结合位点，并将结构用于新的问题。随着档案积累，坐标之外的说明也变得越来越重要。同样叫“泛素”的分子，可以通过不同实验方法研究，可以在不同条件下测量，也可能有多份独立提交的结构。因此，科学数据的组织需要一个稳定的条目身份，以及与身份连接的实验方法、分子组成和文献等信息。本章的四字符编号就是条目入口，编号对应的是一条档案记录，而不是一种蛋白质在所有条件下的唯一形状。

这种组织方式解释了为什么网页、坐标文件和 API 可以互相配合。网页帮助人阅读，坐标文件保存空间结构，接口则帮助程序提取结构化信息。它们围绕同一条目连接，但承担的任务不同。本章访问的是 `core/entry` 入口，返回条目层面的说明；其中的原子数是一项档案元数据。若下一步要计算两个原子之间的距离，还需要下载并读取坐标文件。先明确当前层级，可以避免把“有一条结构记录”误解为“已经把分子坐标读进 Python”。

![共享结构档案的发展与条目实体实例层级。](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/6e451c3dc032223b2b658089.svg?v=6e451c3dc032)

图 1原创档案结构图：1971 年 PDB 建立、1977 年计算机档案论文，以及今天围绕条目连接的网页、接口和坐标。下方区分条目、实体与实例。

一个条目还可以继续分成聚合物实体和结构中的链。实体描述某一种聚合物分子，例如某条特定氨基酸序列；链描述结构中出现的实例。同一种实体可以在结构中出现多次。血红蛋白条目 4HHB 的 `polymer_entity_count` 为 2，表达的是两种聚合物实体，不能直接读成“两条链”。这种差异看似属于生物学，却会直接决定代码怎样命名列、怎样连接表。我们把结果列命名为 `polymer_entities`，就是要让数据对象的名字保留原字段的科学层级。

## 把一次请求拆成能够检查的步骤

访问 1UBQ 的完整地址为 `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/1UBQ`。前面的部分指定服务与资源类型，末尾的编号选择条目。使用 Requests 时，`session.get(...)` 发出 HTTP GET 请求，返回一个响应对象。这个对象同时保存状态、响应头和正文。`raise_for_status()` 检查 HTTP 错误状态，使不存在的地址或服务器错误在下载阶段明确暴露。随后调用 `response.json()`，把 JSON 文本解析成 Python 对象。两个动作检查的是不同事情：前者关注服务器怎样回应，后者关注正文能否按照 JSON 语法读懂。

JSON 中用花括号包围的对象通常转成 Python 字典，方括号中的有序集合转成列表，数字转成相应数值，`null` 转成 `None`。例如实验方法位于一个列表中，读取第一项的方法需要先取 `exptl`，再取列表中的第 0 项，最后取其中的 `method`。这条索引路径描述的是数据结构，不是一个可以随意省略的写法。列表保留多个项目的可能性，所以示例会收集全部方法并连接成文本，而不是默认每条记录永远只有一个方法。理解这层对应关系后，新的嵌套字段也可以按相同方式逐层检查。

网络等待也需要具体的设置。代码使用 `timeout=(10, 60)`，分别给连接阶段和读取阶段设置等待时限，单位是秒。这有助于在服务暂时不可达或响应迟迟没有到来时结束当前尝试。读取超时关注接收数据时的等待间隔，并不是承诺整个任务一定在 70 秒内完成。我们只有四个条目，按顺序访问并在请求间留出间隔即可。将来扩大到大量条目时，应先查看服务提供的查询和批量获取方式，复用已经下载的记录，再决定怎样组织请求，避免把相同内容反复传输。

一个 JSON 能正常解析，还不等于它适合进入结果表。示例的 `validate_record` 会检查返回的条目编号是否与请求一致，实验方法是否为非空文本列表，原子数是否为正整数。这些检查来自本章表格的用途：如果身份错了，后面的每一列都会归到错误对象名下；如果方法缺失，分辨率的解释就失去上下文；如果原子数不是合理的计数，绘图也没有清楚含义。检查应围绕将要使用的字段设计，同时保留完整原始响应，便于以后增加新的字段。

## 完整示例：先保留原始记录，再生成分析表

下面的程序可以直接运行。默认模式读取随示例提供的四份公开 JSON 快照，因而没有网络也能完成解析和绘图。需要获取数据库当前内容时，加入 `--refresh` 参数；程序通过 Requests 下载新的响应，并把它们写入本次输出目录。两种模式共用同一套字段检查和绘图逻辑。这样，课堂上看到的图有明确的输入版本，之后也能用新记录重新计算，而不会在刷新时悄悄改掉原来的教学数据。

### 读取、检查并比较四条 PDB 记录

默认读取随包保存的原始响应；加入 --refresh 后通过 Requests 获取当前记录并另存于输出目录。

```
"""Read four public PDB entry records, validate their identities, and plot metadata.

Default execution reads the bundled JSON snapshots.  --refresh retrieves current
records with Requests and places the new snapshots inside the output directory.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import json
import platform
import time

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager
import numpy as np
import requests

IDS = ("1UBQ", "4HHB", "1BNA", "1D3Z")
BASE_URL = "https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/"
HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent



def available_plot_fonts():
    """Choose installed fonts; keep a Latin fallback on every platform."""
    choices = ["Noto Sans CJK SC", "Noto Sans SC", "Microsoft YaHei", "SimHei", "DejaVu Sans"]
    installed = {font.name for font in font_manager.fontManager.ttflist}
    return [name for name in choices if name in installed]



def fetch_record(session, pdb_id, destination):
    """Download one identified entry. A failed request never replaces a cache."""
    response = session.get(BASE_URL + pdb_id, timeout=(10, 60))
    response.raise_for_status()
    value = response.json()
    validate_record(value, pdb_id)
    destination.write_bytes(response.content)
    return value


def validate_record(record, requested_id):
    if record.get("rcsb_id") != requested_id:
        raise ValueError("The response identifier differs from the requested entry")
    methods = record.get("exptl", [])
    if not methods or not all(isinstance(x.get("method"), str) for x in methods):
        raise ValueError("The entry has no readable experimental method")
    info = record.get("rcsb_entry_info", {})
    atom_count = info.get("deposited_atom_count")
    if not isinstance(atom_count, int) or atom_count <= 0:
        raise ValueError("The deposited atom count must be a positive integer")


def select_fields(record, raw):
    info = record["rcsb_entry_info"]
    resolutions = info.get("resolution_combined", [])
    return {
        "pdb_id": record["rcsb_id"],
        "title": record["struct"]["title"],
        "method": "; ".join(x["method"] for x in record["exptl"]),
        "deposited_atoms": info["deposited_atom_count"],
        "polymer_entities": info["polymer_entity_count"],
        "resolution_angstrom": float(resolutions[0]) if resolutions else None,
        "response_bytes": len(raw),
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
    }


def figures(rows, records, output, language):
    zh = language == "zh"
    plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": available_plot_fonts(),
        "font.size": 12, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
        "svg.fonttype": "none", "axes.unicode_minus": False, "figure.facecolor": "#faf9f5",
        "axes.facecolor": "#faf9f5", "text.color": "#172534", "axes.labelcolor": "#172534"})
    blue, orange, grey = "#205b8c", "#b4482e", "#6a7782"
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12.2, 7.5), layout="constrained")
    grid = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, width_ratios=[1.35, 1])
    ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[:, 0])
    positions = np.arange(len(rows))
    colours = [orange if "NMR" in r["method"] else blue for r in rows]
    ax.hlines(positions, 0, [r["deposited_atoms"] for r in rows], color=colours, lw=3)
    ax.scatter([r["deposited_atoms"] for r in rows], positions, c=colours, s=80, zorder=3)
    ax.set_yticks(positions, [r["pdb_id"] for r in rows]); ax.invert_yaxis()
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(r["deposited_atoms"] for r in rows) * 1.24)
    ax.set_xlabel("条目报告的存档原子数" if zh else "Deposited atom count reported by the entry")
    ax.set_title("A  同一字段，四个结构条目" if zh else "A  One field across four structure entries", loc="left", pad=22)
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        ax.text(r["deposited_atoms"] + 100, i, f'{r["deposited_atoms"]:,}', va="center", fontsize=12)
    ax.grid(axis="x", color="#dde1e3", lw=.6); ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    bx = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, 1])
    valid = [r for r in rows if r["resolution_angstrom"] is not None]
    bx.scatter([r["resolution_angstrom"] for r in valid], np.arange(len(valid)), color=blue, s=75)
    bx.set_yticks(np.arange(len(valid)), [r["pdb_id"] for r in valid]); bx.invert_yaxis()
    bx.set_xlabel("报告的分辨率 / Å" if zh else "Reported resolution / Å")
    bx.set_xlim(0, max(r["resolution_angstrom"] for r in valid) * 1.25)
    bx.set_title("B  有该字段的X射线条目" if zh else "B  X-ray entries with this field", loc="left")
    bx.grid(axis="x", color="#dde1e3", lw=.6)
    cx = fig.add_subplot(grid[1, 1]); cx.axis("off")
    txt = ("实验方法是解释数字的前提\n\n蓝：X-RAY DIFFRACTION\n橙：SOLUTION NMR\n\n1D3Z 的分辨率字段缺失，\n保留为 null；不填成 0 Å。" if zh else
           "Read the experimental method first\n\nBlue: X-RAY DIFFRACTION\nOrange: SOLUTION NMR\n\nThe resolution field for 1D3Z is absent.\nKeep null; do not substitute 0 Å.")
    cx.text(.02, .95, txt, va="top", linespacing=1.7, fontsize=12)
    fig.savefig(output / f"entry-comparison-{language}.svg", metadata={"Date": None}); plt.close(fig)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(14, 7.2), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios":[1.4,1,1.45],"height_ratios":[2.5,1]}, layout="constrained")
    for axis in axes.ravel(): axis.axis("off")
    info = records[0]["rcsb_entry_info"]
    source_fields = {"rcsb_id":records[0]["rcsb_id"],"rcsb_entry_info":{key:info[key] for key in ["deposited_atom_count","polymer_entity_count","resolution_combined"]}}
    axes[0,0].set_title("A  真实响应中的选定字段" if zh else "A  Selected fields in the actual response",loc="left",fontsize=13)
    axes[0,0].text(.02,.9,json.dumps(source_fields,indent=2),va="top",family="DejaVu Sans Mono",fontsize=13,linespacing=1.45,
                   bbox={"facecolor":"#edf2f4","edgecolor":"#cad5dc","pad":14})
    axes[0,1].set_title("B  从嵌套路径到结果列" if zh else "B  Nested paths become result columns",loc="left",fontsize=13)
    for y,key,name,value,color in [(.83,'deposited_atom_count','deposited_atoms',rows[0]['deposited_atoms'],blue),
                                   (.53,'polymer_entity_count','polymer_entities',rows[0]['polymer_entities'],'#277a78'),
                                   (.23,'resolution_combined[0]','resolution_angstrom',rows[0]['resolution_angstrom'],orange)]:
        axes[0,1].text(0,y,'rcsb_entry_info.\n'+key,va='top',fontsize=12.5,color=color,linespacing=1.4)
        axes[0,1].text(0,y-.17,'→ '+name+' = '+str(value),fontsize=12,color=color)
    axes[0,2].set_title("C  同一路径用于四条记录" if zh else "C  Apply the same path to all four records",loc="left",fontsize=13)
    labels=['编号','原子数','实体数','Å'] if zh else ['ID','Atoms','Entities','Å']
    table=axes[0,2].table(cellText=[[r['pdb_id'],r['deposited_atoms'],r['polymer_entities'],r['resolution_angstrom'] if r['resolution_angstrom'] is not None else 'null'] for r in rows],colLabels=labels,cellLoc='center',bbox=[0,.14,1,.72],colWidths=[.23,.27,.25,.25])
    table.auto_set_font_size(False);table.set_fontsize(13)
    for (r,c),cell in table.get_celld().items():
        cell.set_edgecolor('#cbd7dd');cell.set_facecolor('#e7eef3' if r==1 else '#ffffff')
        if r==0:cell.set_facecolor(['#172534',blue,'#277a78',orange][c]);cell.get_text().set_color('white')
        if r==4 and c==3:cell.set_facecolor('#f3e5df');cell.get_text().set_color(orange)
    nmr=next(record for record in records if record['rcsb_id']=='1D3Z')
    missing='resolution_combined' not in nmr['rcsb_entry_info']
    axes[1,0].text(.02,.9,'1D3Z · '+nmr['exptl'][0]['method'],color=orange,fontsize=14,va='top')
    axes[1,0].text(.02,.55,('rcsb_entry_info 中没有\nresolution_combined 字段' if zh else 'resolution_combined is absent\nfrom rcsb_entry_info') if missing else 'resolution_combined is present',fontsize=12,va='top',linespacing=1.5)
    axes[1,1].text(0,.9,'→ Python: None\n→ JSON: null\n→ CSV: '+('空单元格' if zh else 'empty cell'),fontsize=13,va='top',linespacing=1.6,color=orange)
    axes[1,2].text(0,.9,'1D3Z'+(' 保留身份与实验方法\n分辨率图不放置数值点\n缺失状态随记录保存' if zh else ' keeps its identity and method\nNo point on the resolution axis\nMissing state remains in the record'),fontsize=12,va='top',linespacing=1.7)
    fig.savefig(output / f"response-to-table-{language}.svg", metadata={"Date": None})
    fig.savefig(output / f"response-to-table-{language}.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--language", choices=["zh", "en"], default="zh")
    parser.add_argument("--refresh", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(); args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data_dir = HERE / "data"
    if args.refresh:
        data_dir = args.output / "refreshed-data"; data_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        with requests.Session() as session:
            session.headers["User-Agent"] = "ScientificPythonCourse/1.0"
            for pdb_id in IDS:
                fetch_record(session, pdb_id, data_dir / f"{pdb_id}.json")
                time.sleep(.2)
    rows = []; records = []
    for pdb_id in IDS:
        raw = (data_dir / f"{pdb_id}.json").read_bytes()
        record = json.loads(raw); validate_record(record, pdb_id)
        records.append(record)
        rows.append(select_fields(record, raw))
    with (args.output / "entries.csv").open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=list(rows[0])); writer.writeheader(); writer.writerows(rows)
    summary = {"source": "RCSB PDB core entry API", "entry_count": len(rows), "rows": rows,
               "resolution_present": sum(r["resolution_angstrom"] is not None for r in rows),
               "missing_resolution_ids": [r["pdb_id"] for r in rows if r["resolution_angstrom"] is None]}
    (args.output / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    figures(rows, records, args.output, args.language)
    print(json.dumps({"entry_count": len(rows), "resolution_present": summary["resolution_present"]}))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

代码可以沿着数据流来阅读。`fetch_record` 负责与服务器交流并保留响应，`validate_record` 负责检查本章依赖的字段，`select_fields` 将嵌套记录变成一行，`figures` 将多行数据转成图，最后的 `main` 把输入、参数和输出组织起来。函数之间传递的都是普通的路径、字典和列表；每个函数名字都对应一个能够单独说明的动作。与把所有语句堆在一个循环中相比，这种安排使你更容易判断某个问题发生在下载、解析还是解释阶段，也方便在下一章把结果接入 Excel。

下载完成后，程序先检查返回内容，再把原始字节写入文件。保存字节的好处是，响应中的字段顺序、空白和完整内容都能保留下来；如果先解析再重新写成 JSON，科学字段可能相同，文件字节却会改变。代码同时计算 SHA-256 摘要，它相当于这份文件的内容指纹。日后重新读取同一份文件，若摘要一致，就能确认比较的是同一串字节。摘要帮助核对版本，科学正确性仍由字段含义、实验方法和研究问题共同决定，两者在工作流程中各有用途。

运行时给 `--output` 一个希望保存结果的目录，给 `--language` 选择 `zh` 或 `en`。程序会生成 `entries.csv`、`summary.json` 和两张 SVG 科学图。CSV 适合继续用 pandas 或电子表格读取，摘要 JSON 还保留了输入文件的字节数和摘要，SVG 则便于放大、排版和检查文字。输出文件的角色不同，但它们都由同一组已检查的行记录产生，因此表格和图中的数字能够相互核对。

## 空值也有科学含义：怎样比较四条记录

示例快照中的原子数分别为 660、4779、566 和 602。这里使用的是数据库返回的 `deposited_atom_count`，所以图中写成“存档原子数”。这个指标帮助了解条目规模，涉及具体的存档模型、分子组成和记录规则；它与蛋白质序列长度并不是一回事。一个氨基酸含有多个原子，记录还可能包含水分子或其他组分。为保证比较口径一致，代码对每条记录都提取同一个字段，而不是对某些条目数氨基酸、对另一些条目数坐标行。

![原子数点图、三条衍射分辨率及核磁条目说明。](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/8e3cc8b4d324948dd086f752.svg?v=8e3cc8b4d324)

图 2四条公开记录的存档原子数与实验方法；分辨率面板保留 Å 单位，并明确标记 NMR 条目没有本例使用的衍射分辨率。

三个 X 射线衍射条目的分辨率依次为 1.80、1.74 和 1.90 Å，Å 是埃，1 Å 等于 0.1 nm。这个指标描述衍射数据能够分辨的空间尺度，在相应实验语境下，较小的数值对应更精细的空间信息。阅读时要同时看方法和结构用途：分辨率是一项重要描述，还需要结合模型检验指标和具体区域的实验支持来判断某个结构问题。图中把分辨率放在独立的面板内，横轴保留单位，并直接标出条目，读者便能看清比较的是哪一种量。

1D3Z 的方法是溶液核磁共振。它没有本例所用的衍射分辨率字段，因此表中保存 `None`，写 CSV 时留下空单元格，图上则说明当前记录没有该指标。如果把空值填成 0，排序时它会被排到最小值一端，产生“分辨率最好”的错误解释；如果把整行删除，又会丢掉一个真实有效的结构条目。这里需要保留记录身份，将缺失状态与实验方法一起展示。空值处理因此属于科学建模的一部分，不能只根据哪种写法方便绘图来决定。

本例比较选定四条记录的元数据，并通过它们说明接口、档案层级和实验方法的差异。研究某类蛋白质在数据库中的分辨率分布时，应先明确检索条件、重复结构处理、实验方法筛选以及样本范围，再收集相应条目。先写出问题对应的总体，才能判断当前数据表是否包含了足够的信息。这一步会直接影响后续代码中的筛选条件和分组方式。

## 沿着字段路径，查看同一个数值的三种表示

下面的交互把记录、字段路径和比较图放在同一个工作区。选择一个条目，右侧显示它的实验方法和选定字段；切换字段后，柱形长度和表格数值同步变化。你可以先选择“存档原子数”，观察 4HHB 的条目规模，再选择“分辨率”，看 1D3Z 怎样保留自己的位置并显示空值。图上的每条记录也可以直接选择，键盘使用原生下拉框即可完成相同操作。这里读取的是随课程保存的四份记录，页面切换不会向数据库发送请求。

### 记录与字段联动

最值得练习的动作，是从图上的一个值反向寻找原始字段。选中 1UBQ 与分辨率后，路径指向 `rcsb_entry_info.resolution_combined[0]`，数值为 1.8；选择聚合物实体数，则指向另一个字段，单位也变成计数。两个数都来自同一条目，却描述不同层面的属性。这样的反向检查能够发现许多表面上像“数据异常”的问题：字段选错、单位没写、把实体与实例混在一起，或把空值转成零。交互中的联动让这些关系直接可见，也为自己编写数据检查界面提供了一个完整例子。

## 让下一次分析仍然找得到这一次的输入

网络数据库会修订条目、补充字段和改进服务。重复运行一段网址相同的程序，并不自动保证收到的字节完全一样。一个可重复的分析目录因此需要同时保存原始响应和提取后的表格：前者记录当时实际收到什么，后者表达这次研究选用了什么。程序中的 JSON 快照、输入摘要和字段路径将这两件事接在一起。原始文件保持完整，分析脚本则可以不断改进，例如加入发布日期、分子名称或相关文献，而不必为了每个新问题重新下载全部输入。

![真实 JSON 的嵌套字段、提取路径与四记录表逐项对应；下方追踪 1D3Z 缺失分辨率在 Python、JSON、CSV 和图中的一致表达。](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/e27c45e00983a181c4c8353c.svg?v=e27c45e00983)

图 3真实 JSON 的嵌套字段、提取路径与四记录表逐项对应；下方追踪 1D3Z 缺失分辨率在 Python、JSON、CSV 和图中的一致表达。

图中的三列把这条追踪关系展开：左侧从真实原始响应中选出相关字段，中间写出嵌套路径及结果列名，右侧将同一路径用于四条记录。颜色沿着原子数、实体数和分辨率三个字段保持一致，因此可以直接追踪 1UBQ 的 1.8 怎样进入结果表。下方单独追踪 1D3Z：原始记录没有分辨率字段，Python 保存为 None，导出的 JSON 保存为 null，CSV 保留空单元格，比较图则保留方法说明。这些表示方式服务于不同文件格式，保存的是同一个科学状态。调整表格定义时，应同时更新路径和列名，使后来的读者能够区分直接读取、筛选取得和进一步计算的数值。

在实际研究中，还应把接口地址、获取时间、数据许可和使用的字段定义与结果一起保存。公开 PDB 档案数据采用 CC0，RCSB 页面同时说明部分整合的外部资源遵循各自的使用条款。本章使用的是四条核心结构记录，保留其公开身份和学术引用入口。对于另一个数据库，可以沿用相同的代码结构，但应先读它的接口和数据使用说明，再安排缓存、请求频率与引用方式。清楚记录输入身份，能够让合作者把精力放在科学问题上，而不用猜测一列数值是从哪里来的。

## 把这个小流程扩展成自己的数据入口

最自然的练习是再加入一个条目，并在运行前写下你预期检查的内容：编号是否匹配、实验方法是什么、分辨率字段是否适用、原子数是否为正整数。随后刷新新记录，查看原始 JSON，再读输出表和图，确认新增条目确实沿着同一套规则进入结果。若条目包含多种实验方法，保留方法列表提供的信息，重新思考比较图该怎样分组。这个练习把“改一个编号”推进成“验证一个数据对象”，也使你逐渐积累适合自己研究对象的检查规则。

当条目数量增加，可以把编号列表放进文本文件，先检查重复编号，再逐条读取缓存；需要更新的条目才访问网络。把失败记录单独列出，保留错误类型和编号，之后针对这些记录重试。对成功结果和失败结果分别保存明确的状态，比在异常发生后悄悄跳过更容易追踪。再往后，可以将提取函数交给测试程序，使用一个正常条目、一个缺少可选字段的条目和一个身份不符的条目，检查程序是否作出预期响应。[程序检查与复用](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p27/)会继续展开这一做法。

本章建立的入口可直接连接后面的科学计算：结构表可以交给 pandas 分组，坐标可以交给 Biopython 或 MDAnalysis 读取，结果可以写入 [Excel 报告](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p26/)。无论接入哪一个工具，都保留“条目身份—原始响应—字段定义—结果”的关系。这样，当一个图中的点引起兴趣时，研究者能够回到具体结构和实验条件继续追问，而不是停留在一张失去上下文的数字表上。

解压后按 README 运行；代码与本篇示例一致。

# Retrieving Traceable Data from Public APIs

Source: https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p25/en/
Language: en

Connect URLs, nested JSON, scientific meaning, and reproducible tables through four Protein Data Bank entries.

## How a structure table travels from a database to your computer

A comparison of protein or nucleic-acid structures often begins with a modest table: the name of each structure, its experimental method, the number of deposited atoms, and its resolution. Copying two records from a website is manageable. With dozens of records, the demanding work becomes keeping the columns consistent, noticing when a measurement does not apply, and revisiting records after they change. Python can perform the repeated retrieval and transformation. An application programming interface, or API, provides an agreed entrance for programs: a request identifies the desired resource, the service returns structured data, and the analysis selects and interprets the fields needed for a scientific question.

This chapter retrieves four entries from the RCSB Protein Data Bank: 1UBQ, 4HHB, 1BNA, and 1D3Z. They concern ubiquitin, haemoglobin, DNA, and a solution-NMR ubiquitin structure. The selection has a teaching purpose. Three records contain a diffraction-resolution value; the fourth asks us to handle a measurement that does not apply to its experimental method. The completed example produces four original JSON responses, a CSV table with clearly defined columns, and figures that explain the recorded values. You will also be able to trace a number in that table back to its entry, its nested field, and the particular response file used to generate it.

Think of an API as a library's standardized service desk. The address identifies the requested item, the request specifies an operation, the response status reports what happened, and the response body contains the material delivered. A successful transaction still leaves a scientific question: is this the right item, and does it contain what the analysis needs? We therefore check communication and content separately before connecting them. This separation gives each part of the program a clear job and makes the workflow transferable to another database.

## From shared coordinates to connected scientific records

The Protein Data Bank was announced in 1971. Atomic coordinates are among the central results that structural research needs to share: another researcher can inspect molecular shape, measure distances, compare binding sites, or investigate a new problem using those coordinates. As the archive grows, the accompanying descriptions become increasingly valuable. A molecule called ubiquitin can be studied by different experimental methods, under different conditions, and in multiple independent depositions. Organizing this information requires an entry identity connected to experimental methods, molecular composition, and publications. The four-character identifiers in this example locate archive entries; each identifier describes a particular record rather than the single universal shape of a protein.

This organization explains how a website, a coordinate file, and an API work together. The website supports human reading, a coordinate file carries the spatial model, and the API supports programmatic extraction of structured information. Our request uses the `core/entry` resource and returns entry-level descriptions. An atom count in that response is archive metadata. Calculating the distance between two atoms would require the coordinates themselves. Identifying the level of information needed is an early design decision: it determines which resource the program should request and which objects it should create.

![Development of the shared archive and entry/entity/instance levels.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/42e1da4e5926cf3194d793bf.svg?v=42e1da4e5926)

Figure 1Original archive diagram linking the 1971 PDB announcement and 1977 computer-based archive paper to current website, API, and coordinate resources. Entry, entity, and instance levels are distinguished below.

An entry can also be described through polymer entities and chain instances. An entity represents a particular polymer molecule, such as a particular amino-acid sequence, while a chain is an instance occurring in the structure. One entity can have several instances. The value of `polymer_entity_count` in 4HHB is 2: it counts two polymer entities, not two chains. This biological distinction has immediate consequences for programming. It determines column names and table joins. Calling the output column `polymer_entities` preserves the level of the original field and helps the next person interpret the number correctly.

## Separate a request into steps you can inspect

The complete address for 1UBQ is `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/1UBQ`. The first part identifies the service and resource type; the final identifier selects an entry. In Requests, `session.get(...)` sends an HTTP GET request and returns a response object containing the status, headers, and body. Calling `raise_for_status()` exposes HTTP error responses, such as an unavailable resource or a server error. Calling `response.json()` then interprets the body as JSON. These operations answer different questions: how did the server respond, and can its body be parsed using JSON syntax?

A JSON object enclosed in braces usually becomes a Python dictionary. An ordered array in square brackets becomes a list, numbers become numeric values, and `null` becomes `None`. The experimental method is nested inside a list: accessing a method involves selecting `exptl`, selecting an item from that list, and reading its `method` field. That indexing path describes the structure of the data. A list also allows more than one item, so the example collects every reported method rather than assuming that one method must always be present. Once this connection between JSON and Python is clear, unfamiliar nested fields can be inspected one layer at a time.

Network waiting needs an explicit setting. The example uses `timeout=(10, 60)`, giving the connection and read stages waiting limits in seconds. These settings allow a stalled request to end when a service cannot be reached or stops delivering data. The read timeout concerns waiting between received data, rather than guaranteeing that the entire task finishes within seventy seconds. With four entries, sequential requests and a short interval are sufficient. Before scaling to many entries, inspect the service's query and bulk-retrieval facilities, reuse downloaded records, and design requests around the actual data needed.

A valid JSON document still needs to match the analysis. The example's `validate_record` function checks that the returned entry identifier matches the request, that the experimental methods form a nonempty list of strings, and that the deposited atom count is a positive integer. Each check follows from the table's purpose. A wrong identifier assigns every value to the wrong object; a missing method removes the context required to interpret resolution; an invalid count makes the size comparison meaningless. Checks should cover the fields the analysis relies on, while the complete original response remains available for later additions.

## A complete example: preserve the response before making the table

The program below runs directly. Its default mode reads four public JSON snapshots included with the example, so parsing and plotting work offline. Adding `--refresh` retrieves current responses with Requests and saves them in the new output directory. Both modes use the same validation, extraction, and plotting functions. The figures shown in this chapter therefore have a definite input version, while a later run can use updated records without silently replacing the teaching inputs.

### Read, validate, and compare four PDB records

Read bundled original responses by default; add --refresh to retrieve current records with Requests into the output directory.

```
"""Read four public PDB entry records, validate their identities, and plot metadata.

Default execution reads the bundled JSON snapshots.  --refresh retrieves current
records with Requests and places the new snapshots inside the output directory.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import json
import platform
import time

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager
import numpy as np
import requests

IDS = ("1UBQ", "4HHB", "1BNA", "1D3Z")
BASE_URL = "https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/"
HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent



def available_plot_fonts():
    """Choose installed fonts; keep a Latin fallback on every platform."""
    choices = ["Noto Sans CJK SC", "Noto Sans SC", "Microsoft YaHei", "SimHei", "DejaVu Sans"]
    installed = {font.name for font in font_manager.fontManager.ttflist}
    return [name for name in choices if name in installed]



def fetch_record(session, pdb_id, destination):
    """Download one identified entry. A failed request never replaces a cache."""
    response = session.get(BASE_URL + pdb_id, timeout=(10, 60))
    response.raise_for_status()
    value = response.json()
    validate_record(value, pdb_id)
    destination.write_bytes(response.content)
    return value


def validate_record(record, requested_id):
    if record.get("rcsb_id") != requested_id:
        raise ValueError("The response identifier differs from the requested entry")
    methods = record.get("exptl", [])
    if not methods or not all(isinstance(x.get("method"), str) for x in methods):
        raise ValueError("The entry has no readable experimental method")
    info = record.get("rcsb_entry_info", {})
    atom_count = info.get("deposited_atom_count")
    if not isinstance(atom_count, int) or atom_count <= 0:
        raise ValueError("The deposited atom count must be a positive integer")


def select_fields(record, raw):
    info = record["rcsb_entry_info"]
    resolutions = info.get("resolution_combined", [])
    return {
        "pdb_id": record["rcsb_id"],
        "title": record["struct"]["title"],
        "method": "; ".join(x["method"] for x in record["exptl"]),
        "deposited_atoms": info["deposited_atom_count"],
        "polymer_entities": info["polymer_entity_count"],
        "resolution_angstrom": float(resolutions[0]) if resolutions else None,
        "response_bytes": len(raw),
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
    }


def figures(rows, records, output, language):
    zh = language == "zh"
    plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": available_plot_fonts(),
        "font.size": 12, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
        "svg.fonttype": "none", "axes.unicode_minus": False, "figure.facecolor": "#faf9f5",
        "axes.facecolor": "#faf9f5", "text.color": "#172534", "axes.labelcolor": "#172534"})
    blue, orange, grey = "#205b8c", "#b4482e", "#6a7782"
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12.2, 7.5), layout="constrained")
    grid = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, width_ratios=[1.35, 1])
    ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[:, 0])
    positions = np.arange(len(rows))
    colours = [orange if "NMR" in r["method"] else blue for r in rows]
    ax.hlines(positions, 0, [r["deposited_atoms"] for r in rows], color=colours, lw=3)
    ax.scatter([r["deposited_atoms"] for r in rows], positions, c=colours, s=80, zorder=3)
    ax.set_yticks(positions, [r["pdb_id"] for r in rows]); ax.invert_yaxis()
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(r["deposited_atoms"] for r in rows) * 1.24)
    ax.set_xlabel("条目报告的存档原子数" if zh else "Deposited atom count reported by the entry")
    ax.set_title("A  同一字段，四个结构条目" if zh else "A  One field across four structure entries", loc="left", pad=22)
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        ax.text(r["deposited_atoms"] + 100, i, f'{r["deposited_atoms"]:,}', va="center", fontsize=12)
    ax.grid(axis="x", color="#dde1e3", lw=.6); ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    bx = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, 1])
    valid = [r for r in rows if r["resolution_angstrom"] is not None]
    bx.scatter([r["resolution_angstrom"] for r in valid], np.arange(len(valid)), color=blue, s=75)
    bx.set_yticks(np.arange(len(valid)), [r["pdb_id"] for r in valid]); bx.invert_yaxis()
    bx.set_xlabel("报告的分辨率 / Å" if zh else "Reported resolution / Å")
    bx.set_xlim(0, max(r["resolution_angstrom"] for r in valid) * 1.25)
    bx.set_title("B  有该字段的X射线条目" if zh else "B  X-ray entries with this field", loc="left")
    bx.grid(axis="x", color="#dde1e3", lw=.6)
    cx = fig.add_subplot(grid[1, 1]); cx.axis("off")
    txt = ("实验方法是解释数字的前提\n\n蓝：X-RAY DIFFRACTION\n橙：SOLUTION NMR\n\n1D3Z 的分辨率字段缺失，\n保留为 null；不填成 0 Å。" if zh else
           "Read the experimental method first\n\nBlue: X-RAY DIFFRACTION\nOrange: SOLUTION NMR\n\nThe resolution field for 1D3Z is absent.\nKeep null; do not substitute 0 Å.")
    cx.text(.02, .95, txt, va="top", linespacing=1.7, fontsize=12)
    fig.savefig(output / f"entry-comparison-{language}.svg", metadata={"Date": None}); plt.close(fig)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(14, 7.2), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios":[1.4,1,1.45],"height_ratios":[2.5,1]}, layout="constrained")
    for axis in axes.ravel(): axis.axis("off")
    info = records[0]["rcsb_entry_info"]
    source_fields = {"rcsb_id":records[0]["rcsb_id"],"rcsb_entry_info":{key:info[key] for key in ["deposited_atom_count","polymer_entity_count","resolution_combined"]}}
    axes[0,0].set_title("A  真实响应中的选定字段" if zh else "A  Selected fields in the actual response",loc="left",fontsize=13)
    axes[0,0].text(.02,.9,json.dumps(source_fields,indent=2),va="top",family="DejaVu Sans Mono",fontsize=13,linespacing=1.45,
                   bbox={"facecolor":"#edf2f4","edgecolor":"#cad5dc","pad":14})
    axes[0,1].set_title("B  从嵌套路径到结果列" if zh else "B  Nested paths become result columns",loc="left",fontsize=13)
    for y,key,name,value,color in [(.83,'deposited_atom_count','deposited_atoms',rows[0]['deposited_atoms'],blue),
                                   (.53,'polymer_entity_count','polymer_entities',rows[0]['polymer_entities'],'#277a78'),
                                   (.23,'resolution_combined[0]','resolution_angstrom',rows[0]['resolution_angstrom'],orange)]:
        axes[0,1].text(0,y,'rcsb_entry_info.\n'+key,va='top',fontsize=12.5,color=color,linespacing=1.4)
        axes[0,1].text(0,y-.17,'→ '+name+' = '+str(value),fontsize=12,color=color)
    axes[0,2].set_title("C  同一路径用于四条记录" if zh else "C  Apply the same path to all four records",loc="left",fontsize=13)
    labels=['编号','原子数','实体数','Å'] if zh else ['ID','Atoms','Entities','Å']
    table=axes[0,2].table(cellText=[[r['pdb_id'],r['deposited_atoms'],r['polymer_entities'],r['resolution_angstrom'] if r['resolution_angstrom'] is not None else 'null'] for r in rows],colLabels=labels,cellLoc='center',bbox=[0,.14,1,.72],colWidths=[.23,.27,.25,.25])
    table.auto_set_font_size(False);table.set_fontsize(13)
    for (r,c),cell in table.get_celld().items():
        cell.set_edgecolor('#cbd7dd');cell.set_facecolor('#e7eef3' if r==1 else '#ffffff')
        if r==0:cell.set_facecolor(['#172534',blue,'#277a78',orange][c]);cell.get_text().set_color('white')
        if r==4 and c==3:cell.set_facecolor('#f3e5df');cell.get_text().set_color(orange)
    nmr=next(record for record in records if record['rcsb_id']=='1D3Z')
    missing='resolution_combined' not in nmr['rcsb_entry_info']
    axes[1,0].text(.02,.9,'1D3Z · '+nmr['exptl'][0]['method'],color=orange,fontsize=14,va='top')
    axes[1,0].text(.02,.55,('rcsb_entry_info 中没有\nresolution_combined 字段' if zh else 'resolution_combined is absent\nfrom rcsb_entry_info') if missing else 'resolution_combined is present',fontsize=12,va='top',linespacing=1.5)
    axes[1,1].text(0,.9,'→ Python: None\n→ JSON: null\n→ CSV: '+('空单元格' if zh else 'empty cell'),fontsize=13,va='top',linespacing=1.6,color=orange)
    axes[1,2].text(0,.9,'1D3Z'+(' 保留身份与实验方法\n分辨率图不放置数值点\n缺失状态随记录保存' if zh else ' keeps its identity and method\nNo point on the resolution axis\nMissing state remains in the record'),fontsize=12,va='top',linespacing=1.7)
    fig.savefig(output / f"response-to-table-{language}.svg", metadata={"Date": None})
    fig.savefig(output / f"response-to-table-{language}.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--language", choices=["zh", "en"], default="zh")
    parser.add_argument("--refresh", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(); args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data_dir = HERE / "data"
    if args.refresh:
        data_dir = args.output / "refreshed-data"; data_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        with requests.Session() as session:
            session.headers["User-Agent"] = "ScientificPythonCourse/1.0"
            for pdb_id in IDS:
                fetch_record(session, pdb_id, data_dir / f"{pdb_id}.json")
                time.sleep(.2)
    rows = []; records = []
    for pdb_id in IDS:
        raw = (data_dir / f"{pdb_id}.json").read_bytes()
        record = json.loads(raw); validate_record(record, pdb_id)
        records.append(record)
        rows.append(select_fields(record, raw))
    with (args.output / "entries.csv").open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=list(rows[0])); writer.writeheader(); writer.writerows(rows)
    summary = {"source": "RCSB PDB core entry API", "entry_count": len(rows), "rows": rows,
               "resolution_present": sum(r["resolution_angstrom"] is not None for r in rows),
               "missing_resolution_ids": [r["pdb_id"] for r in rows if r["resolution_angstrom"] is None]}
    (args.output / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    figures(rows, records, args.output, args.language)
    print(json.dumps({"entry_count": len(rows), "resolution_present": summary["resolution_present"]}))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Read the program by following the data. `fetch_record` communicates with the service and saves a response; `validate_record` checks the fields used here; `select_fields` transforms a nested record into one row; `figures` makes figures from the collected rows; and `main` organizes parameters, inputs, and outputs. Paths, dictionaries, and lists pass between these functions. Each function corresponds to an action that can be explained independently. This organization makes it easier to locate a problem in downloading, parsing, or interpretation and to connect the resulting table to the Excel workflow in the next chapter.

The download function validates the received record before writing its original bytes. Keeping those bytes preserves the full response, including field order and whitespace. Parsing a response and writing a newly formatted JSON file can preserve the scientific fields while changing its byte representation. The program also calculates a SHA-256 digest, a content fingerprint that can be recalculated when the file is read again. Matching digests identify matching byte sequences. Scientific correctness has a different role: it comes from the meanings of the fields, the experimental method, and the question being asked. Both file identity and scientific interpretation belong in a reproducible workflow.

Use `--output` to choose a result directory and `--language` to select `zh` or `en`. The program writes `entries.csv`, `summary.json`, and two SVG figures. The CSV can be read with pandas or a spreadsheet. The summary retains input byte counts and digests as well as extracted values. SVG graphics remain readable when enlarged and are convenient for publication layout. These files serve different purposes, but all derive from the same validated rows, allowing the table and figures to be checked against each other.

## A missing value can carry scientific meaning

The deposited atom counts in the example snapshots are 660, 4779, 566, and 602. These values come from `deposited_atom_count`, so the figure explicitly labels them as deposited atom counts. They describe the size of particular deposited records, whose contents depend on the model, molecular composition, and archive conventions. An atom count is different from an amino-acid sequence length: one amino acid contains several atoms, and a coordinate model may include water molecules or other components. The program extracts the same field from every record to maintain a consistent definition across the comparison.

![Atom-count plot, three diffraction resolutions, and the NMR missing-value state.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/60536867a1b403215f4663ef.svg?v=60536867a1b4)

Figure 2Deposited atom counts and experimental methods for four public records. The resolution panel retains ångström units and identifies the absent diffraction-resolution value for the NMR entry.

The three X-ray diffraction entries have resolution values of 1.80, 1.74, and 1.90 Å. An ångström is 0.1 nm. In the context of diffraction, resolution describes the spatial scale of information that the data can resolve, with smaller values corresponding to finer spatial information. The method and intended structural question still matter: model-validation measures and the experimental support for a specific region also contribute to an assessment. The resolution plot therefore has its own axis with units and directly identifies the entries being compared.

Entry 1D3Z was determined using solution NMR. It does not have the diffraction-resolution field used by this example. The program preserves that state as `None`, writes an empty CSV cell, and explains the absence in the figure. Filling the field with zero would place it at the smallest end of a resolution ranking and create a false interpretation. Deleting the entire row would discard a valid structure entry. Keeping the identity, experimental method, and missing-value state together provides the information needed to interpret the record. Missing-data handling is consequently part of the scientific model of the table.

The four entries were chosen to expose interface structure, archive levels, and method differences. They are a teaching collection, rather than a statistical sample of the archive. The plotted comparison answers a question about these four records. A question about the resolution distribution of a protein family would require explicit search criteria, handling of repeated structures, method selection, and a defined population of entries. Writing down that population before collecting data helps determine whether the resulting table contains the right information and which grouping or filtering operations are appropriate.

## Follow one value through its record, field, and plot

The interactive workspace connects entry selection, a nested field path, and a comparison plot. Select an entry to inspect its method and selected value. Change the field to update the bars and table together. Start with deposited atoms to inspect the scale of 4HHB, then choose resolution and observe how 1D3Z retains its identity while displaying an absent value. Records in the plot can also be selected directly; the native select controls provide the same interaction with a keyboard. This workspace reads the four bundled snapshots and sends no database request when a selection changes.

A useful exercise is to work backwards from a plotted value. With 1UBQ and resolution selected, the path is `rcsb_entry_info.resolution_combined[0]` and the value is 1.8. Selecting polymer entities changes the path and changes the quantity to a count. Both values belong to one entry, yet describe different properties. Following the path can reveal problems that initially look like unusual data: an incorrect field, an omitted unit, an entity confused with an instance, or a missing value converted to zero. The linked views make these relationships visible and provide a practical model for an inspection interface of your own.

## Keep the inputs available for the next analysis

Online databases revise entries, add fields, and improve services. Repeating a request to the same address does not guarantee an identical sequence of response bytes. A reproducible analysis directory therefore retains both the original responses and the extracted table. The responses record what was received; the table expresses what this analysis selected. Snapshot files, input digests, and field paths connect those two roles. With complete original records available, an extraction script can be improved to include release dates, molecular names, or publications without requesting the same input for every new question.

![Actual nested JSON fields, extraction paths, and the four-record table are connected explicitly. The lower row follows the absent 1D3Z resolution through Python, JSON, CSV, and the figure.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/ed8d3e4819046aa050391d62.svg?v=ed8d3e481904)

Figure 3Actual nested JSON fields, extraction paths, and the four-record table are connected explicitly. The lower row follows the absent 1D3Z resolution through Python, JSON, CSV, and the figure.

The figure expands that traceability across three columns. Selected fields from the actual response appear on the left, nested paths and output names in the middle, and the four-record table on the right. Consistent colors follow atom count, entity count, and resolution, so the value 1.8 for 1UBQ can be traced directly into the table. The lower row follows 1D3Z separately: its original resolution field is absent, Python retains None, exported JSON retains null, CSV has an empty cell, and the figure preserves the method context. These formats express the same scientific state. Updating paths and column names when a table definition changes helps another reader distinguish directly retrieved, selected, and calculated quantities.

A research workflow should also retain the endpoint, retrieval time, data terms, and field definitions alongside its results. Public PDB archive data are released under CC0; RCSB's policy separately identifies integrated external resources that follow their own terms. This example uses four core entry records and preserves their public identities and scientific citation links. For another database, the same program structure remains useful, while its interface documentation and data terms determine caching, request frequency, and attribution. Clearly identified inputs let collaborators investigate the scientific question without reconstructing the origin of an unexplained column.

## Develop this workflow into your own data entrance

Add one entry and write down the checks you expect before running the program: the returned identifier, experimental method, applicability of resolution, and a positive integer atom count. Retrieve the record, inspect its original JSON, and compare the resulting table and plot to those expectations. If the entry reports several methods, preserve that information and reconsider how the comparison should be grouped. This exercise turns a change of identifier into the validation of a data object and gradually builds checks appropriate to the molecules you study.

For a larger collection, place identifiers in a text file, check duplicates, and read available cached records before making network requests. Keep failed requests in a separate list with their identifiers and error types, then retry those records deliberately. Explicit success and failure states are easier to investigate than silently skipped rows. Extraction functions can subsequently be tested with a normal record, a record missing an optional field, and a record with the wrong identity. The chapter on [testable and reusable programs](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p27/en/) develops this approach.

This entrance connects naturally to later scientific work. pandas can group the structure table, Biopython or MDAnalysis can read coordinate data, and the results can become an [Excel report](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p26/en/). Preserve the connection between entry identity, original response, field definition, and result as the data move between tools. When an interesting point appears in a figure, that connection allows the investigation to return to a particular structure and its experimental context.

8. [1D3Z · Validation of Protein Structure from Anisotropic Carbonyl Chemical Shifts in a Dilute Liquid Crystalline Phase (1998)](https://doi.org/10.1021/ja9812610)

   Original study for this structure entry. [Inspect entry 1D3Z](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1D3Z).
