# Making Analysis Programs Testable and Reusable

Source: https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p27/en/
Language: en

Use hand-checkable geometry, explicit input definitions, and executed tests to make an area calculation reusable.

## How can the original calculation remain valid after an edit?

An analysis program often starts with one immediate task: read an image, select a region, and calculate its area. Later, it processes dozens of images with different pixel spacings and supplies values to a report. As the program becomes more useful, more behavior needs to remain consistent when it changes. Automated tests retain that behavior as repeatable conditions: a defined input should produce a particular result, and an input outside the function's definition should receive a clear response. Checks that once depended on memory, hand calculations, and temporary print statements can then remain with the program.

This chapter develops a complete example around two-dimensional region area. The function takes a Boolean mask and two pixel spacings and returns area in μm². We begin with a rectangle whose answer is calculable on paper, then check an empty region, changes of scale, transposition, invalid calibration, and incorrect dimensions. The pytest file contains thirteen executed checks. Three deliberately changed implementations provide teaching comparisons: one omits a scale factor, one counts the entire array, and one omits input validation. Their different behavior appears in a diagnostic matrix, making the purpose of each condition visible.

Think of preparing known-size objects to check a ruler. Before measuring an unfamiliar specimen, a reference block helps establish that the ruler's scale and reading agree. A program benefits from reference objects too. A complex cell's exact area may be difficult to know independently, while a rectangle four pixels wide and three pixels high is straightforward. Establishing the calculation with simple geometry before applying it to complex objects supports both scientific understanding and program maintenance.

## Define the inputs and outputs

Before writing tests, decide what the function means. The mask is a two-dimensional Boolean array: true pixels belong to the selected region and false pixels are background. `spacing` contains two lengths in row-column order, both in μm. They may differ because imaging and resampling can have unequal intervals along the two axes. The output is the total physical area of selected pixels in μm². The mask already expresses a region selection, so thresholding belongs upstream; the area function converts an explicitly selected region into a physical quantity.

$$
A=N s_y s_x
$$

| Symbol | Meaning and units |
| --- | --- |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/3207697e43e4f88223ad85c1.svg) | two-dimensional selected area, μm² |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/256531b7f0ddb14dd11a59a3.svg) | number of true pixels, dimensionless count |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/8f5fc51f77ebba17af28d557.svg) | row-direction pixel spacing, μm |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/d65997e80acc2ddac324815b.svg) | column-direction pixel spacing, μm |

One pixel is a rectangle with width s_x and height s_y. Multiplying those lengths gives its area; summing N selected pixels gives A. Twelve pixels with row spacing 0.2 μm and column spacing 0.3 μm give A=12×0.2×0.3=0.72 μm². Independent whole-object geometry gives width 1.2 μm and height 0.6 μm, whose product is also 0.72 μm².

The definition includes edge cases. An all-false mask describes an empty region whose area is zero. This differs from receiving an array that is not a two-dimensional image. A three-dimensional object requires three spacings and a volume definition, so the function reports a dimension error for a volume. A raw intensity array also differs from a Boolean mask: counting all its nonzero values could include many ordinary background pixels. Requiring Boolean membership asks the caller to make the region selection explicit before measurement. These checks address inputs that would otherwise change the scientific meaning.

Both spacings must be finite and strictly positive. Zero and negative values do not describe the pixel side lengths used here, and NaN or infinity cannot participate in an ordinary finite area calculation. The function raises `ValueError` for such values and `TypeError` for an incorrect mask type. The exception name and short message help the caller identify what to repair. In batch processing, an image identifier and error description can be recorded together, allowing calibration or array shape to be examined for that particular input.

### Scientific function: area from a region and calibration

The function explicitly defines types, dimensions, units, and invalid-calibration behavior.

```
"""A small scientific function with an explicit input and unit contract."""
import numpy as np


def mask_area(mask, spacing):
    """Return selected 2D area in um^2 for (row, column) spacing in um.

    A Boolean mask defines membership. Empty selections have area zero.
    Both physical spacings must be finite and strictly positive.
    """
    mask = np.asarray(mask)
    if mask.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError("mask must have exactly two spatial dimensions")
    if mask.dtype != np.bool_:
        raise TypeError("mask must contain Boolean membership values")
    scale = np.asarray(spacing, dtype=float)
    if scale.shape != (2,) or not np.all(np.isfinite(scale)) or np.any(scale <= 0):
        raise ValueError("spacing must contain two finite positive lengths")
    return float(np.count_nonzero(mask) * scale[0] * scale[1])
```

## Prepare an object with an independent answer

The test rectangle sits inside an eight-row, ten-column background. Rows 2 through 4 and columns 1 through 4 are true. Python slices exclude their stopping index, so `mask[2:5, 1:5]` selects three rows and four columns: twelve pixels. With row spacing 0.2 μm and column spacing 0.3 μm, the rectangle is 0.6 μm high and 1.2 μm wide. Its geometric area is 0.72 μm². This expected value comes from width times height, independently of how the function counts pixels internally.

![Independent expectations from explicit geometry: twelve selected pixels within an eighty-pixel grid, with unequal directional spacings.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/4f3aaa4542ec64eab53d51af.svg?v=4f3aaa4542ec)

Figure 1Independent expectations from explicit geometry: twelve selected pixels within an eighty-pixel grid, with unequal directional spacings.

Keeping background around the rectangle makes the test more informative. If every input pixel were true, counting selected pixels and counting all array elements would agree, allowing an incorrect implementation to pass. The present array has eighty pixels but only twelve selected ones. Those two operations therefore have clearly different results. A test input is useful because of the behaviors it distinguishes, rather than simply because it contains many values. A small, targeted input can locate a problem more directly than a complicated image whose answer is unknown.

A calculated result may appear as `0.7200000000000001` because of floating-point representation. pytest's `approx` compares floating-point results within a tolerance, expressing agreement with the geometric expectation at a specified numerical precision. Counts can be compared exactly; floating-point multiplication and longer numerical methods need an appropriate tolerance. A tolerance wide enough to accept values such as 2.4 or 4.8 would hide scale or counting errors. Its size should therefore follow the numerical calculation and scientific definition.

The tests explicitly set relative tolerance `rel=1e-12` and absolute tolerance `abs=1e-12`. The relative allowance scales with the expected value at one part in a trillion; the absolute allowance has a scale of 10 to the power −12 μm². The comparison uses the larger allowance. For an expectation of 0.72 μm², the relative term is 0.72 times 10 to the power −12, so the absolute allowance determines the threshold. This accommodates rounding from the few double-precision multiplications here while remaining far smaller than a missing-scale error. A later approximate solver or numerical integral would need a tolerance chosen for that algorithm's accuracy.

## Retain a check as a repeatable object

The history of testing frameworks has produced useful divisions of responsibility. Python's standard `unittest` was inspired by JUnit and separates input preparation, individual cases, collections of cases, and their execution. Its documentation also links Kent Beck's early paper on Smalltalk testing patterns. The organization fits scientific code: prepare a reusable geometric object, express distinct properties as individual cases, and let an execution tool run and report them together. pytest provides concise function and assertion syntax within this tradition, making automated checks accessible to small analysis projects.

![The same rectangle connects independent geometry, an actual pytest failure excerpt, and the passing correct-function suite. The executed report reveals how omitting column spacing changes 0.72 to 2.4.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/9b252a3754443b6dc16f3b7a.svg?v=9b252a375444)

Figure 2The same rectangle connects independent geometry, an actual pytest failure excerpt, and the passing correct-function suite. The executed report reveals how omitting column spacing changes 0.72 to 2.4.

Here, a fixture prepares the rectangle with background. Each test requesting it receives the same defined input. Functions whose names begin with `test_` state checks, and `assert` expresses the expected relationship. pytest discovers those functions, runs them, and identifies a failed assertion. A fixture avoids copying the array-construction code into several tests. The geometric object's definition remains in one place, making it easier to confirm that different checks refer to the intended input.

Parametrization lists several inputs for the same type of check. Zero spacing, negative spacing, nonfinite spacing, and an incorrect number of spacing values all violate the calibration definition. `pytest.mark.parametrize` runs one check function separately for each set of arguments. `pytest.raises(ValueError)` states that a call should reject the input explicitly. Raising the expected exception is the correct outcome in those cases. Successful testing therefore includes both a correct value for valid input and an appropriate response to invalid input.

### Checks of independent geometry, input boundaries, and invariants

Thirteen executed pytest checks use geometry and object definitions as expectations.

```
"""Expected values come from geometry and input definitions."""
import numpy as np
import pytest
from measurement import mask_area


@pytest.fixture
def rectangle():
    mask = np.zeros((8, 10), dtype=bool)
    mask[2:5, 1:5] = True
    return mask


def test_rectangle_geometry(rectangle):
    # Four columns × 0.3 um = 1.2 um; three rows × 0.2 um = 0.6 um.
    assert mask_area(rectangle, (.2, .3)) == pytest.approx(.72, rel=1e-12, abs=1e-12)


def test_empty_region():
    assert mask_area(np.zeros((4, 7), dtype=bool), (.2, .3)) == 0


def test_doubling_both_lengths_quadruples_area(rectangle):
    assert mask_area(rectangle, (.4, .6)) == pytest.approx(2.88, rel=1e-12, abs=1e-12)


def test_transpose_with_swapped_spacing(rectangle):
    assert mask_area(rectangle.T, (.3, .2)) == pytest.approx(.72, rel=1e-12, abs=1e-12)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("spacing", [(0, .3), (-.2, .3), (.2, float('nan')),
                                    (.2, float('inf')), (.2,), (.2, .3, .4)])
def test_reject_invalid_calibration(rectangle, spacing):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        mask_area(rectangle, spacing)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("mask", [np.ones(5,dtype=bool), np.ones((2,3,4),dtype=bool)])
def test_reject_wrong_dimension(mask):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        mask_area(mask, (.2, .3))


def test_reject_numeric_intensities():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        mask_area(np.array([[0, 120], [80, 255]]), (.2, .3))
```

## Add geometric relationships to individual examples

A known rectangle provides one numerical reference. Geometric relationships check behavior under transformations. Doubling both pixel spacings doubles each pixel's width and height, so area must become four times larger: 0.72 becomes 2.88 μm². An implementation using only one spacing responds to only one length change, exposing its missing spatial factor. Expressing this relationship in a test makes the physical definition directly visible to someone modifying the code.

Transposing the array exchanges rows and columns. Swapping the associated spacings at the same time describes the same region in a different axis order, so area remains 0.72 μm². This check becomes particularly helpful when direction-dependent properties are added later, because an axis mistake can still produce plausible numbers. An empty-region check confirms that background does not contribute area. Dimension and type checks distinguish a two-dimensional region from a volume or an unsegmented intensity image. Together, they turn the function's intended use into executable conditions.

Three questions guide the selection of tests: is there an independently calculable answer, is there a relationship that should survive an input change, and is there an incorrect input that would change the object's meaning? These provide numerical references, relational references, and input constraints. Other scientific functions offer similar opportunities. A line fit can use points on a known line; an integral can use a function with known area; a coordinate transformation can preserve distances under rigid translation. Connecting tests to the scientific meaning clarifies which changes deserve attention during later revisions.

## Inspect what a collection of tests detects

The following matrix comes from executing eight diagnostic conditions. Columns represent the correct implementation and three deliberate changes; rows represent inputs. PASS and FAIL indicate whether an implementation meets the expectation for that row. The unit-square case allows all four implementations to pass because it has no background, both spacings are one, and the input is valid. Introducing a rectangle with background and unequal, nonunit spacings reveals the missing-factor and whole-array errors. Invalid calibration and incorrect array types then distinguish the omitted-validation implementation.

![Diagnostic matrix from eight executed conditions. PASS means the row expectation is met, including numerical outputs for valid inputs and expected exceptions for invalid ones.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/63013fb524ca30125cb40a8b.svg?v=63013fb524ca)

Figure 3Diagnostic matrix from eight executed conditions. PASS means the row expectation is met, including numerical outputs for valid inputs and expected exceptions for invalid ones.

Interpret the matrix through inputs and expectations rather than counting green cells alone. The missing-factor implementation passes six conditions because it retains validation and happens to handle zero area and the unit square. The nonunit rectangle and doubled-spacing case reveal its geometric error. The implementation without validation calculates valid inputs correctly but continues accepting invalid spacings, a volume, and raw intensities. Different mistakes leave different patterns of failure, which the matrix brings together for inspection.

The interactive workspace lets you choose which conditions are active and observe which implementations that collection distinguishes. Begin with the unit square, add the rectangle, and then add negative calibration. Selecting a case or changing the implementation updates its input description, independent expectation, and observed result. The values come from actual Python execution of the implementations. Choosing among those recorded outcomes helps explain the composition of a test collection without turning a test count into a general reliability score.

To read an actual failure, first locate `test_missing_column_spacing`, then inspect `Obtained` and `Expected`. The observed value is 2.4000000000000004 and the expectation is 0.72±1.0e-12, with the same twelve-pixel rectangle as input. Returning to geometry, twelve times row spacing 0.2 gives exactly 2.4: column spacing 0.3 has been omitted. Restoring that factor gives 0.72, which can be checked with the independent suite. The file `failure_demo.py` retains this teaching failure and is invoked separately by the main program. Its expected exit status is one; the correct-function suite exits with zero.

### An explicitly selected teaching failure

The intentionally omitted column spacing produces the actual 2.4-versus-0.72 failure.

```
"""One intentional failure, selected explicitly for reading a failure report."""
import numpy as np
import pytest
from main import changed_area


def test_missing_column_spacing():
    mask = np.zeros((8, 10), dtype=bool)
    mask[2:5, 1:5] = True
    observed = changed_area(mask, (.2, .3), mode="one_scale")
    assert observed == pytest.approx(.72, rel=1e-12, abs=1e-12)
```

## Run the checks and generate the diagnostic results

The core example has three files, plus a teaching file for inspecting a failure. `measurement.py` holds the scientific function for other programs to import. `test_measurement.py` holds independent checks. `main.py` executes the checks and generates figures and the diagnostic matrix. All complete files are shown on this page and run together from one directory. The main program invokes pytest using the current Python interpreter, checks its return status, and saves the actual test output. After the correct-function suite succeeds, it separately executes the missing-scale example and checks that the intended discrepancy is reported.

Open a terminal in the example directory. The first command runs the complete program and creates figures and summaries; the second runs the thirteen tests of the correct function; the third explicitly selects the teaching failure. `--output` chooses the result directory and `--language` chooses figure language. Naming the test file keeps the two collections separate.

### Full run, correct-function checks, and the failure example

The third command displays the intentional teaching failure and exits with status one.

```
python main.py --output results --language en
python -m pytest test_measurement.py -q
python -m pytest failure_demo.py -q
```

### Execute tests and generate the diagnostic matrix

Save actual test output, compare three teaching mutations, and draw geometry, matrix, and structure figures.

```
"""Run scientific tests and compare deliberately changed implementations."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap
from measurement import mask_area

HERE=Path(__file__).resolve().parent



def available_plot_fonts():
    """Choose installed fonts; keep a Latin fallback on every platform."""
    choices = ["Noto Sans CJK SC", "Noto Sans SC", "Microsoft YaHei", "SimHei", "DejaVu Sans"]
    installed = {font.name for font in font_manager.fontManager.ttflist}
    return [name for name in choices if name in installed]



def changed_area(mask,spacing,mode):
    """Teaching mutations: each intentionally changes one scientific rule."""
    if mode=='correct':return mask_area(mask,spacing)
    if mode=='no_validation':return float(np.count_nonzero(mask)*spacing[0]*spacing[1])
    mask_area(mask,spacing)  # These two mutations retain the input checks.
    if mode=='one_scale':return float(np.count_nonzero(mask)*spacing[0])
    if mode=='whole_grid':return float(mask.size*spacing[0]*spacing[1])
    raise ValueError(mode)


def cases():
    rectangle=np.zeros((8,10),bool);rectangle[2:5,1:5]=True
    return [
        ('unit_square',np.ones((2,2),bool),(1.,1.),4.),
        ('rectangle',rectangle,(.2,.3),.72),
        ('empty',np.zeros((8,10),bool),(.2,.3),0.),
        ('doubled',rectangle,(.4,.6),2.88),
        ('negative',rectangle,(-.2,.3),'ValueError'),
        ('nonfinite',rectangle,(.2,float('nan')),'ValueError'),
        ('volume',np.ones((2,3,4),bool),(.2,.3),'ValueError'),
        ('intensity',np.array([[0,120],[80,255]]),(.2,.3),'TypeError')]


def main():
    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__);ap.add_argument('--output',type=Path,required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--language',choices=['zh','en'],default='en');args=ap.parse_args()
    out=args.output.resolve();out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);zh=args.language=='zh';tr=lambda a,b:a if zh else b
    environment=os.environ.copy();environment['PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE']='1'
    environment['PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD']='1'
    command=[sys.executable,'-m','pytest',str(HERE/'test_measurement.py'),'-q','--rootdir',str(HERE),'-p','no:cacheprovider']
    completed=subprocess.run(command,cwd=HERE,text=True,capture_output=True,env=environment)
    (out/'pytest-output.txt').write_text(completed.stdout+completed.stderr,encoding='utf8')
    if completed.returncode:raise RuntimeError('Scientific tests failed; see pytest-output.txt')
    negative=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','pytest','failure_demo.py','-q','--tb=short','-p','no:cacheprovider'],cwd=HERE,text=True,capture_output=True,env=environment)
    if negative.returncode!=1:raise RuntimeError('The deliberate missing-scale example must fail its assertion')
    (out/'failure-example.txt').write_text(negative.stdout+negative.stderr,encoding='utf8')
    modes=['correct','one_scale','whole_grid','no_validation'];records=[]
    for name,mask,spacing,expected in cases():
        for mode in modes:
            try:
                value=changed_area(mask,spacing,mode)
                observed=value if math.isfinite(value) else 'NaN'
            except (ValueError,TypeError) as error:observed=type(error).__name__
            passed=(observed==expected if isinstance(expected,str) else isinstance(observed,(int,float)) and math.isclose(observed,expected,rel_tol=1e-12,abs_tol=1e-12))
            records.append({'case':name,'mode':mode,'expected':expected,'observed':observed,'passed':bool(passed)})
    passes={m:sum(r['passed'] for r in records if r['mode']==m) for m in modes}
    passed_count=int(re.search(r'(\d+) passed',completed.stdout).group(1))
    summary={'pytest_exit_code':completed.returncode,'pytest_passed':passed_count,'deliberate_failure_exit':negative.returncode,'cases':8,'modes':4,'pass_counts':passes,
             'rectangle_area_um2':mask_area(cases()[1][1],(.2,.3)),'mutation_results':records}
    (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary,indent=2),encoding='utf8')
    inputs={name:{'shape':list(mask.shape),'dtype':str(mask.dtype),'mask':mask.tolist(),
                  'spacing':[v if math.isfinite(v) else 'NaN' for v in spacing]}
            for name,mask,spacing,expected in cases()}
    (out/'lab-data.json').write_text(json.dumps({'records':records,'modes':modes,'cases':[c[0] for c in cases()],'inputs':inputs}),encoding='utf8')
    plt.rcParams.update({'font.family':available_plot_fonts(),'font.size':12,'svg.fonttype':'none','figure.facecolor':'#faf9f5','axes.facecolor':'#faf9f5','axes.spines.top':False,'axes.spines.right':False})
    def save(fig,name):
        fig.savefig(out/f'{name}-{args.language}.svg',metadata={'Date':None});fig.savefig(out/f'{name}-{args.language}.png',dpi=150);plt.close(fig)
    mask=cases()[1][1];fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(9,5.3),layout='constrained')
    ax.imshow(mask,cmap=ListedColormap(['#f0f2f3','#205b8c']),extent=(0,3,1.6,0),interpolation='nearest')
    ax.vlines(np.arange(0,3.01,.3),0,1.6,color='white',lw=1.2)
    ax.hlines(np.arange(0,1.61,.2),0,3,color='white',lw=1.2)
    ax.set(xlabel=tr('水平位置 / μm','Horizontal position / μm'),ylabel=tr('垂直位置 / μm','Vertical position / μm'))
    ax.text(1.8,.65,tr('选中 4 列 × 3 行\n宽 1.2 μm，高 0.6 μm\n独立几何面积 = 0.72 μm²','4 columns × 3 rows selected\nWidth 1.2 μm, height 0.6 μm\nGeometric area = 0.72 μm²'),fontsize=12,linespacing=1.8)
    ax.set_title(tr('一个能在纸上独立算出答案的测试对象','A test object with an independently calculable answer'),loc='left')
    save(fig,'known-geometry')
    grid=np.array([[int(next(r['passed'] for r in records if r['case']==case[0] and r['mode']==m)) for m in modes] for case in cases()])
    fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(12.4,6.4),layout='constrained');ax.imshow(grid,cmap=ListedColormap(['#f1d7cb','#deebe6']),vmin=0,vmax=1,aspect='auto')
    names=tr(['单位方格','有背景的矩形','空区域','双向尺度加倍','负标定','非有限标定','误传三维数组','误传灰度数组'],['Unit square','Rectangle with background','Empty region','Both lengths doubled','Negative calibration','Nonfinite calibration','3D input','Intensity input'])
    ax.set_xticks(range(4),tr(['正确实现','漏乘一个尺度','误数整个网格','省略输入检查'],['Correct','One scale missing','Whole grid counted','No input validation']))
    ax.set_yticks(range(8),names)
    for y in range(8):
        for x in range(4):ax.text(x,y,'PASS' if grid[y,x] else 'FAIL',ha='center',va='center',color='#205b55' if grid[y,x] else '#9b3e21',fontsize=13)
    ax.set_title(tr('测试诊断矩阵：不同科学条件发现不同错误','Diagnostic test matrix: different conditions detect different errors'),loc='left',pad=18)
    save(fig,'test-matrix')
    fig=plt.figure(figsize=(13.2,7.3));gs=fig.add_gridspec(2,2,width_ratios=[1,1.6],height_ratios=[1.3,1],left=.06,right=.97,bottom=.15,top=.88,hspace=.23,wspace=.18)
    geom=fig.add_subplot(gs[0,0]);geom.imshow(mask,cmap=ListedColormap(['#edf1f3','#205b8c']),extent=(0,3,1.6,0),interpolation='nearest')
    geom.vlines(np.arange(0,3.01,.3),0,1.6,color='white',lw=1);geom.hlines(np.arange(0,1.61,.2),0,3,color='white',lw=1)
    geom.set(xlabel=tr('横坐标 / μm','Horizontal position / μm'),ylabel=tr('纵坐标 / μm','Vertical position / μm'))
    geom.set_title(tr('A  同一个 12 像素矩形','A  The same 12-pixel rectangle'),loc='left',fontsize=14)
    calculation=fig.add_subplot(gs[1,0]);calculation.axis('off')
    calculation.text(0,.97,tr('独立几何期望','Independent geometry'),fontsize=14,color='#205b8c',va='top')
    calculation.text(0,.73,'(4 × 0.3) × (3 × 0.2)\n= 0.72 μm²',fontsize=17,va='top',linespacing=1.6)
    calculation.text(0,.16,tr('漏乘列间隔：12 × 0.2 = 2.4\n恢复列间隔：2.4 × 0.3 = 0.72','Missing column spacing: 12 × 0.2 = 2.4\nRestore it: 2.4 × 0.3 = 0.72'),fontsize=12,va='top',linespacing=1.6)
    failure=fig.add_subplot(gs[0,1]);failure.axis('off');failure.set_title(tr('B  pytest 的实际失败片段','B  Actual pytest failure excerpt'),loc='left',fontsize=14,color='#9b3e21')
    excerpt=[line for line in negative.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith('E ') or 'failure_demo.py:' in line]
    # Keep actual diagnostic text; wrap long lines for display.
    visible=[]
    for line in excerpt[:7]:visible.extend(textwrap.wrap(line,width=64,replace_whitespace=False,drop_whitespace=False) or [''])
    failure.text(0,.94,'\n'.join(visible),va='top',family='DejaVu Sans Mono',fontsize=12,linespacing=1.45,
                 bbox={'facecolor':'#f5e8e1','edgecolor':'#d7b5a5','pad':12})
    success=fig.add_subplot(gs[1,1]);success.axis('off');success.set_title(tr('C  正确函数通过独立测试集','C  Correct function passes the independent suite'),loc='left',fontsize=14,color='#205b55')
    success.text(0,.85,'assert area == pytest.approx(\n    0.72, rel=1e-12, abs=1e-12\n)',va='top',family='DejaVu Sans Mono',fontsize=12.5,linespacing=1.5)
    actual_pass=next(line for line in completed.stdout.splitlines() if re.search(r'\d+ passed',line))
    success.text(0,.15,actual_pass,fontsize=14,color='#205b55',bbox={'facecolor':'#e1eee7','edgecolor':'none','pad':9})
    fig.suptitle(tr('把一次真实失败读回面积定义','Read an actual failure back into the area definition'),x=.06,ha='left',fontsize=18)
    fig.text(.06,.035,tr('测试传统：Python unittest 受 JUnit 启发；可重复输入、独立期望与执行报告保留在一起。','Testing tradition: Python unittest was inspired by JUnit; retain repeatable inputs, independent expectations, and execution reports.'),fontsize=12)
    save(fig,'test-structure')
    print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in summary.items() if k!='mutation_results'}))


if __name__=='__main__':main()
```

The example run passes thirteen tests, and the correct implementation passes all eight diagnostic conditions. The three teaching variants pass six, five, and four conditions respectively. These counts describe the explicitly listed inputs. `summary.json` also retains each case's expected value, observed value, and comparison result, allowing changes to the test objects to be inspected later. The figures and records derive from the same execution, so each matrix cell can be traced to a particular comparison.

Separating the main program from the scientific function has another practical benefit: an analysis script can import `mask_area` without automatically starting plotting or testing. The `if __name__ == '__main__'` block starts the program when this file is run directly. This organization suits small scientific projects: core calculations remain callable, checks remain repeatable, and the main script organizes presentation and file writing. Later performance changes can be checked against the same scientific definitions before their timings are compared.

## Let the tests develop with the research question

Moving from two-dimensional images to volumes calls for a volume function with three spacings and a stated volume unit, followed by tests using a rectangular solid, an empty volume, and scale transformations. The original area function continues to serve its original definition. When a scientific question changes, the interface, explanation, and tests should change together. A caller benefits from knowing whether the function measures area or volume, with the corresponding inputs made explicit.

During maintenance, a discovered error can become a small reproducible test input. If an axis-order change produces an incorrect result, retain the smallest array and spacings that reproduce that situation. Once corrected, preserve the expected behavior in a test so that future restructuring checks it automatically. The important objects are the triggering relationship and its intended meaning. A compact geometric array and calibration parameters can travel with the test as an independent example.

Useful checks make code easier to change. Array operations can be reorganized, functions separated, and execution accelerated while known geometry and input constraints confirm that the scientific meaning remains consistent. The next chapter compares the time and memory costs of different calculations, beginning with agreement of their results. Testing connects a research definition to its implementation and gives later optimization a stable reference.

# 找到耗时在哪里，再提高效率

Source: https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p28/
Language: zh-CN

用同一个邻近对计数问题，比较真实耗时、数组形状和内存，再判断局部提速能改变多少整体工作。

## 让一次科学计算更快，需要先看它在做什么

一个程序处理一百个颗粒位置时几乎立即结束，换成几千个位置后却要等待很久。这样的变化在显微颗粒追踪、分子结构分析和空间邻域计算中很常见：我们想知道哪些对象彼此接近，程序便需要比较许多位置。提高效率的第一步，是把科学问题、计算次数和数据形状连接起来；随后测量时间花在哪里，再选择合适的实现。这样得到的改进不仅能让当前例子更快，也能解释数据规模继续增加时会发生什么。

本章比较同一个任务的三种写法：Python 双循环、NumPy 完整广播，以及按行分块的 NumPy 计算。输入是明确生成的二维教学坐标，分布在边长 10 μm 的正方形内；任务是统计距离严格小于 1 μm 的无序点对。三种方法必须给出同一个整数，再比较耗时和内存。在保存的 800 点计时记录中，三种方法都得到 9106 对，单次中位时间分别约为 130.47、8.90 和 5.47 ms，最后一个结果使用 64 行分块。图中还保留七次实际计时，便于看清这些代表值来自怎样的重复测量。

速度与内存需要一起考虑。完整广播把大量标量操作交给 NumPy，但会创建随点数平方增长的中间数组；分块则一次处理一部分点对，随后复用工作空间。它们仍然比较同一批点对，只是组织计算的方式不同。把这个例子讲清楚后，读者可以更有依据地选择广播、分块或进一步采用空间索引，而不必把“循环少”当作判断程序好坏的唯一标准。

## 先固定计数规则，才能比较不同写法

每个点由两个坐标表示，分别对应水平和竖直方向，单位都是 μm。两个点的坐标差给出一段直角三角形的两条直角边，距离平方由两条边长的平方相加得到。我们只需判断距离是否小于某个半径，因此可以直接比较距离平方与半径平方，省去每一对点的开平方。半径为正时，这两种比较具有相同顺序关系；输入和阈值都应使用同一长度单位。

$$
d_{ij}^2=(x_i-x_j)^2+(y_i-y_j)^2,\qquad d_{ij}^2<r^2
$$

| 符号 | 含义与单位 |
| --- | --- |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/4ce29d83e8648088fa2af7b9.svg) | 点 i 与点 j 的欧氏距离，μm |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/5e1d0f9befd63fa0c25bf752.svg) | 两个点的水平、竖直坐标，μm |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/3a4ef1c1b261a53f9c45d0c9.svg) | 正的邻域半径，μm |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/1f848077b31e64f57fc97f4b.svg) | 点的编号，无量纲；只计 j 大于 i 的点对 |

坐标差是直角三角形的两条直角边，勾股关系给出距离平方。正距离与正半径的大小顺序在平方后保持不变，所以不必逐对开平方。点(0,0)与(1,0)的距离平方为1 μm²，半径1.1 μm的平方为1.21 μm²，因此该对符合严格小于条件；点(1,0)与(0,1)的距离平方为2 μm²，则不符合。

“无序点对”表示点 i 与点 j 只计数一次，交换次序仍是同一对；一个点与自己也不参与统计。双循环用 `j` 从 `i+1` 开始实现这条规则。完整距离矩阵则关于对角线对称，因此保留主对角线上方的三角区域即可。分块时，局部行号要转换成全局点号，再用列号大于行号筛选。三种写法的数组形状不同，计数对象的身份必须一致。

独立检查使用四个可以手算的位置：(0,0)、(1,0)、(0,1)、(3,3)，单位为 μm，半径取 1.1 μm。前面三个点中，原点到另外两个点的距离都为 1 μm，而后两个点之间的距离约为 1.414 μm；远处的点与它们也不满足条件，因此答案是 2 对。程序先验证三种方法都得到 2，再处理较大的生成坐标。这个小算例沿用上一章的原则：在比较运行表现之前，先建立与实现方式无关的科学参照。

## 区分定位耗时与测量速度

性能分析器回答“时间主要花在哪些函数里”。示例中的 `analyze_frame` 先计算坐标中心，再统计近邻点对，最后计算平均径向距离。`cProfile` 记录这些函数的调用和时间，`pstats` 按累计时间整理结果。累计时间包含函数调用的其他函数，自身时间则只计算该函数内部的工作。阅读报告时，先看科学流程中哪个步骤占据主要部分，再决定深入哪一段代码。若大部分时间在读取大量小文件，优化一个很快的数组加法就不会明显改变等待时间。

比较几段实现的实际速度时，示例改用 `timeit.repeat`。输入坐标在计时前生成，三个方法都使用相同数组、半径和计数定义；每个配置分别执行七次，每次记录一次调用的耗时。性能分析会带来额外记录开销，因此不把开启分析器时的时间直接用作基准计时。这个区分与实验测量类似：一种仪器帮助定位过程中的环节，另一种测量安排用于比较统一条件下的结果。

![相同坐标与计数定义下的实际时间：左侧比较不同点数的中位数，右侧显示800点时七次独立计时。](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/0806220025aff3b22fe947c1.svg?v=0806220025af)

图 1相同坐标与计数定义下的实际时间：左侧比较不同点数的中位数，右侧显示800点时七次独立计时。

计时结果会受系统调度、缓存和当前资源使用影响，所以保留整组记录比只报最快一次更容易理解。这里用中位数描述典型单次时间，同时保存最小值和七次原始时间。中位数位于排序后的中间位置，少量较慢的运行对它影响较小；最小值则帮助观察外部干扰较少时的执行水平。图中用对数时间轴同时展示毫秒量级的差异，并在右侧直接画出每一次计时。它描述这份记录中的运行表现，读者重新执行程序时会获得自己环境中的新记录。

任务规模也应进入比较。点数从 100 增加到 800 时，需要考察的无序点对增长得更快，因为每个点都要与其他许多点比较。对不同规模重复同一测量，能够看出某种写法何时开始受内存分配或工作块大小影响。一个在小数组上很简洁的做法，扩大后可能产生很大的临时数据；反过来，分块在小任务中引入的循环开销，也可能抵消它节省内存带来的好处。

## 广播把循环移到哪里，产生了什么数组

坐标数组的形状是 `(N, 2)`。表达式 `points[:, None, :]` 在中间增加一个长度为 1 的轴，得到 `(N, 1, 2)`；`points[None, :, :]` 得到 `(1, N, 2)`。相减时，NumPy 根据广播规则对齐两个点编号轴，结果形状变成 `(N, N, 2)`。前两个轴表示点对，最后一个轴保存水平和竖直坐标差。这个形状与科学对象一一对应，也直接告诉我们需要保存多少个浮点数。

`np.einsum('ijk,ijk->ij', delta, delta)` 将同一坐标差与自身相乘，并沿最后一个坐标轴求和。这里 i、j 表示两个点的编号，k 表示坐标方向；结果只保留 i 和 j，因此形成 `(N, N)` 的距离平方矩阵。也可以用逐元素平方后求和表达同样的数学关系，不过那样可能额外产生一个平方数组。理解每个轴代表什么，比背住一个简短函数名更有用：看到输出形状时，就能判断是否沿正确的方向求和。

广播常常提高这类计算的速度，因为许多重复操作进入 NumPy 的底层数组循环，减少了 Python 逐个元素解释语句的开销。它并没有让两两比较的工作量消失。坐标差数组仍然需要容纳点对的信息，之后还要形成距离和布尔筛选。因此，评价广播写法时应同时问两个问题：底层执行是否减少了解释开销，中间数组是否适合当前数据规模。前一个问题对应计时，后一个问题对应下一节的内存分析。

## 分块：在保留计算定义的同时控制工作空间

完整广播同时保存坐标差和距离平方。两个方向的坐标差需要两个浮点数，每对点的距离平方再需要一个；本例使用 64 位浮点数，每个占 8 字节。因此这两个命名数组合计每对点占 24 字节，随 N 的平方增长。这个计算描述特定数组的存储量；程序还会创建布尔筛选、索引和其他对象，所以实际追踪到的峰值会更高。把公式估计与实际测量并排放置，可以看清数组形状解释了哪一部分内存。

$$
M_{\mathrm{full}}=24N^2\ \mathrm{bytes},\qquad M_{\mathrm{block}}=24BN\ \mathrm{bytes}
$$

| 符号 | 含义与单位 |
| --- | --- |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/38162b15af75aabe566b89b0.svg) | 坐标差和距离平方这两个命名浮点数组的合计存储量，字节 |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/256531b7f0ddb14dd11a59a3.svg) | 点数，无量纲计数 |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/7533ad047439b7d799dd7afe.svg) | 当前完整块的行数，假设不大于 N，无量纲计数 |

每对点保存两个坐标差和一个距离平方，共3个float64数，每个8字节，因此系数为3×8=24。N=800时，完整数组占24×800×800=15360000字节，除以1048576约为14.648 MiB；B=64时占1228800字节，约1.172 MiB。末块不足B行时按实际行数计算。布尔数组、索引与运行时分配另外计入追踪峰值。

![两个命名浮点数组的形状预测与独立tracemalloc峰值测量。MiB等于1048576字节；峰值还包含其他可追踪分配。](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/5a39844b1ce29f33f31487a9.svg?v=5a39844b1ce2)

图 2两个命名浮点数组的形状预测与独立tracemalloc峰值测量。MiB等于1048576字节；峰值还包含其他可追踪分配。

分块把第一个点编号轴切成 B 行一组。当前块与全部 N 个点比较，得到 `(B, N, 2)` 的坐标差和 `(B, N)` 的距离平方；完成计数后释放这两个工作数组，再处理下一组。只要 B 小于 N，命名浮点数组的大小就随 B×N 增长，而不是一次保存 N×N。对于 N=800、B=64，两个数组合计 1228800 字节，完整广播则为 15360000 字节。每一块仍用全局编号去掉重复点对，因此最终计数保持 9106。

示例用 `tracemalloc` 另外执行一次计算，记录其能够追踪的峰值分配，并把结果标为“tracemalloc 峰值”。这与整个进程占用的物理内存有不同定义。内存追踪和速度计时分开进行，避免追踪开销混入七次基准记录。图中不同块大小对应不同的工作数组规模；块过小会增加循环次数，块过大则增加临时内存。选择块大小时，结合实际计时和内存预算寻找合适范围，比假定某个固定数字总是最快更实用。

## Amdahl 的问题：局部快十倍，整体会怎样

1967 年，Gene Amdahl 讨论大规模计算能力时，将程序中能够加速和保持不变的部分放在一起考虑。这个思路至今仍适合日常科研程序。一次完整分析除了邻居计数，还可能包含读取、清洗、拟合和写图；即使把其中一个函数大幅提速，其他部分仍然需要原先的时间。先测量各部分所占比例，才能估计哪项修改最值得做。

把原始总时间设为一个整体，其中比例 p 的工作获得 s 倍局部加速，其余部分时间保持不变。加速后的总时间由未改变部分与缩短后的目标部分相加得到，再用原时间除以新时间，就得到整体加速倍数。这个模型用于固定工作量，并假定修改没有改变其他环节的成本。下面的数值时间预算是明确的教学算例，与前面的实际计时记录分别标识。

$$
S=\frac{1}{(1-p)+p/s}
$$

| 符号 | 含义与单位 |
| --- | --- |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/4d93e1f4798eafa4154488df.svg) | 完整任务原时间除以新时间得到的整体加速倍数，无量纲 |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/48c7b594e8628a17b991d4e6.svg) | 原时间中目标部分所占比例，0到1，无量纲 |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/b8208c8407bd0942fcaa88f9.svg) | 目标部分获得的局部加速倍数，本例不小于1，无量纲 |

把原总时间归一化为1，未改变部分仍需1−p，目标部分从p缩短到p/s，两者相加是新总时间。原时间1除以新时间即为S。p=0.8、s=10时，新时间比例为0.2+0.08=0.28，S≈3.571。对应100 s的教学流程，其中80 s缩短到8 s，另外20 s保持不变，得到28 s。模型采用固定工作量，其他部分成本保持不变。

![Amdahl时间分解的原创图：局部加速比例改变整体收益。右侧100 s到28 s为教学时间预算，与实际基准计时分别标识。](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/0ee927988b26069d88df74a6.svg?v=0ee927988b26)

图 3Amdahl时间分解的原创图：局部加速比例改变整体收益。右侧100 s到28 s为教学时间预算，与实际基准计时分别标识。

例如原流程用时 100 s，其中 80 s 属于目标计算，20 s 属于其他工作。目标计算加快十倍后变成 8 s，总时间为 28 s，整体加速约为 3.57 倍。继续让这 8 s 更短，仍会留下那 20 s。这个结果解释了为什么优化需要反复回到完整流程观察：当主要计算已经足够快，读取或输出可能成为下一项值得处理的工作。历史上的计算机体系结构问题，在一份 Python 分析脚本中仍然具有同样清楚的时间关系。

## 完整程序：保留计时记录、内存结果与数值检查

下面的程序生成固定随机种子的教学坐标，执行独立四点检查，再对 100、200、400 和 800 个点比较双循环、完整广播以及四种分块大小。每种配置都先检查计数一致，再保存七次时间和独立测量的峰值内存。科学任务的输入、计算和测量安排都在同一文件中，运行后得到 `benchmark.json`、`profile.txt`、`summary.json` 和三组科学图。计时文件保留每一次记录，便于进一步画分布或检查异常运行。

### 比较一致计算的耗时、内存与整体时间预算

默认进行七次重复计时，独立追踪内存；可用明确的已有记录生成另一种语言的图。

```
"""Compare equal neighbor-pair calculations using measured time and memory.

Coordinates are generated teaching data in a 10 um square. Timing samples are
local measurements; memory formulas describe named buffers rather than RSS.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import cProfile
import io
import json
import platform
import pstats
import timeit
import tracemalloc
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager



def available_plot_fonts():
    """Choose installed fonts; keep a Latin fallback on every platform."""
    choices = ["Noto Sans CJK SC", "Noto Sans SC", "Microsoft YaHei", "SimHei", "DejaVu Sans"]
    installed = {font.name for font in font_manager.fontManager.ttflist}
    return [name for name in choices if name in installed]



def pair_count_loop(points, radius):
    count=0;limit=radius*radius
    for i in range(len(points)):
        for j in range(i+1,len(points)):
            dx=points[i,0]-points[j,0];dy=points[i,1]-points[j,1]
            if dx*dx+dy*dy < limit:count+=1
    return count


def pair_count_full(points,radius):
    delta=points[:,None,:]-points[None,:,:]
    squared=np.einsum('ijk,ijk->ij',delta,delta)
    return int(np.count_nonzero(np.triu(squared < radius*radius,k=1)))


def pair_count_blocked(points,radius,block=64):
    count=0;n=len(points);columns=np.arange(n)[None,:]
    for start in range(0,n,block):
        stop=min(start+block,n)
        delta=points[start:stop,None,:]-points[None,:,:]
        squared=np.einsum('ijk,ijk->ij',delta,delta)
        rows=np.arange(start,stop)[:,None]
        count+=int(np.count_nonzero((squared < radius*radius)&(columns>rows)))
        del delta,squared
    return count


def measured_peak(function):
    tracemalloc.start()
    result=function()
    _,peak=tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()
    tracemalloc.stop()
    return result,int(peak)


def analyze_frame(points,radius):
    """A small scientific workload for function-level profiling."""
    center=points.mean(axis=0)
    centered=points-center
    pairs=pair_count_loop(centered,radius)
    radial=np.sqrt(np.einsum('ij,ij->i',centered,centered))
    return {'center':center.tolist(),'pairs':pairs,'mean_radius_um':float(radial.mean())}


def main():
    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__);ap.add_argument('--output',type=Path,required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--language',choices=['zh','en'],default='en')
    ap.add_argument('--timing-input',type=Path,help='Reuse an explicitly saved benchmark for an alternative-language figure')
    args=ap.parse_args();out=args.output;out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);zh=args.language=='zh';tr=lambda a,b:a if zh else b
    sizes=[100,200,400,800];blocks=[16,32,64,128];radius=1.0
    points=np.random.default_rng(2819).uniform(0,10,size=(max(sizes),2))
    hand=np.array([[0.,0.],[1.,0.],[0.,1.],[3.,3.]])
    assert pair_count_loop(hand,1.1)==pair_count_full(hand,1.1)==pair_count_blocked(hand,1.1,2)==2
    if args.timing_input:
        benchmark=json.loads(args.timing_input.read_text(encoding='utf8'))
        assert benchmark['seed']==2819 and benchmark['sizes']==sizes
        records=benchmark['records']
    else:
        records=[]
        for n in sizes:
            x=points[:n];reference=pair_count_loop(x,radius)
            methods=[('loop',0,lambda x=x:pair_count_loop(x,radius)),('full',n,lambda x=x:pair_count_full(x,radius))]
            methods += [('blocked',b,lambda x=x,b=b:pair_count_blocked(x,radius,b)) for b in blocks]
            for method,block,fn in methods:
                assert fn()==reference
                samples=timeit.repeat(fn,number=1,repeat=7)
                result,peak=measured_peak(fn)
                assert result==reference
                records.append({'n':n,'method':method,'block':block,'pairs':result,'seconds':samples,
                                'median_seconds':float(np.median(samples)),'minimum_seconds':min(samples),
                                'traced_peak_bytes':peak,'named_float_buffers_bytes':0 if method=='loop' else 24*n*min(block,n)})
        benchmark={'seed':2819,'sizes':sizes,'radius_um':radius,'python':platform.python_version(),
                   'numpy':np.__version__,'timing_definition':'seven independent timeit runs, one call per run',
                   'memory_definition':'separate tracemalloc peak; named buffers are float64 delta and squared distances',
                   'records':records}
    # Every run still independently checks the saved reference computations.
    for n in sizes:
        expected=next(r['pairs'] for r in records if r['n']==n)
        assert pair_count_full(points[:n],radius)==pair_count_blocked(points[:n],radius,64)==expected
    (out/'benchmark.json').write_text(json.dumps(benchmark,indent=2),encoding='utf8')
    profile=cProfile.Profile();profile_result=profile.runcall(analyze_frame,points[:400],radius)
    assert profile_result['pairs']==next(r['pairs'] for r in records if r['n']==400)
    stream=io.StringIO();pstats.Stats(profile,stream=stream).strip_dirs().sort_stats('cumulative').print_stats(8)
    (out/'profile.txt').write_text(stream.getvalue(),encoding='utf8')
    largest=[r for r in records if r['n']==800]
    summary={'hand_checked_pairs':2,'sizes':sizes,'pair_counts':{str(n):next(r['pairs'] for r in records if r['n']==n) for n in sizes},
             'all_methods_agree':True,'repeats':7,'largest_full_named_buffers_bytes':24*800*800,
             'largest_block64_named_buffers_bytes':24*800*64,'amdahl_p08_s10':1/(.2+.8/10)}
    (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary,indent=2),encoding='utf8')
    (out/'lab-data.json').write_text(json.dumps({'points':points.tolist(),'radius':radius,'records':records}),encoding='utf8')
    plt.rcParams.update({'font.family':available_plot_fonts(),'font.size':12,'svg.fonttype':'none','figure.facecolor':'#faf9f5','axes.facecolor':'#faf9f5','axes.spines.top':False,'axes.spines.right':False})
    colors={'loop':'#b4482e','full':'#205b8c','blocked':'#2b7c73'}
    def save(fig,name):
        fig.savefig(out/f'{name}-{args.language}.svg',metadata={'Date':None});fig.savefig(out/f'{name}-{args.language}.png',dpi=150);plt.close(fig)
    fig,axs=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12.4,5.3),layout='constrained',gridspec_kw={'width_ratios':[1.1,1]})
    for method in ['loop','full','blocked']:
        selected=[r for r in records if r['method']==method and (method!='blocked' or r['block']==64)]
        label=tr({'loop':'Python 双循环','full':'完整广播','blocked':'64 行分块'}[method],{'loop':'Python loops','full':'Full broadcast','blocked':'64-row blocks'}[method])
        axs[0].plot([r['n'] for r in selected],[r['median_seconds']*1000 for r in selected],'-o',color=colors[method],label=label)
        r=next(r for r in selected if r['n']==800);i=['loop','full','blocked'].index(method)
        axs[1].scatter(np.full(7,i)+np.linspace(-.1,.1,7),np.array(r['seconds'])*1000,color=colors[method],s=35)
        axs[1].hlines(r['median_seconds']*1000,i-.24,i+.24,color=colors[method],lw=3)
    axs[0].set(xscale='log',yscale='log',xlabel=tr('点数 N','Point count N'),ylabel=tr('单次中位时间 / ms','Median time per call / ms'))
    axs[0].set_xticks(sizes,[str(n) for n in sizes]);axs[0].xaxis.set_minor_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.NullFormatter())
    axs[0].legend(frameon=False,fontsize=11);axs[0].set_title(tr('A  相同输入与计数定义','A  Equal inputs and counting definitions'),loc='left')
    axs[1].set_yscale('log');axs[1].set_xticks(range(3),tr(['双循环','完整广播','64 行分块'],['Loops','Full','Block 64']))
    axs[1].set_ylabel(tr('单次时间 / ms（7 次）','Time per call / ms (7 runs)'));axs[1].set_title(tr('B  N = 800 的实际重复测量','B  Actual repeated timings at N = 800'),loc='left')
    for ax in axs:ax.grid(axis='y',alpha=.2)
    save(fig,'measured-timings')
    fig,axs=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12.4,5.2),layout='constrained');nn=np.array(sizes)
    axs[0].plot(nn,24*nn**2/2**20,'-o',color=colors['full'],label=tr('完整浮点数组','Full floating-point buffers'))
    axs[0].plot(nn,24*nn*64/2**20,'-o',color=colors['blocked'],label=tr('64 行浮点分块','64-row floating-point buffers'))
    axs[0].set(xlabel=tr('点数 N','Point count N'),ylabel=tr('命名浮点数组大小 / MiB','Named floating-point buffers / MiB'));axs[0].legend(frameon=False,fontsize=10)
    rows=[r for r in largest if r['method']=='full' or (r['method']=='blocked' and r['block'] in [16,64,128])]
    x=np.arange(len(rows));axs[1].bar(x-.17,[r['named_float_buffers_bytes']/2**20 for r in rows],width=.34,color='#a5bfce',label=tr('两个命名数组','Two named arrays'))
    axs[1].bar(x+.17,[r['traced_peak_bytes']/2**20 for r in rows],width=.34,color='#205b8c',label=tr('tracemalloc 峰值','tracemalloc peak'))
    axs[1].set_xticks(x,[('Full' if r['method']=='full' else f"B={r['block']}") for r in rows]);axs[1].set_ylabel(tr('追踪/计算内存 / MiB','Traced/calculated memory / MiB'));axs[1].legend(frameon=False,fontsize=10)
    axs[0].set_title(tr('A  保存形状决定增长规律','A  Stored shapes determine growth'),loc='left');axs[1].set_title(tr('B  N = 800：数组与实际峰值','B  N = 800: arrays and measured peaks'),loc='left')
    save(fig,'memory-growth')
    fig,axs=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12.4,5.2),layout='constrained');accelerations=np.linspace(1,50,250)
    for p,color in [(.5,'#205b8c'),(.8,'#b4482e'),(.95,'#2b7c73')]:
        axs[0].plot(accelerations,1/((1-p)+p/accelerations),color=color,label=f'p = {p}')
    axs[0].set(xlabel=tr('目标部分的加速倍数 s','Speedup s of the selected part'),ylabel=tr('整体加速倍数 S','Overall speedup S'));axs[0].legend(frameon=False)
    axs[0].set_title(tr('A  Amdahl（1967）的时间分解思想','A  Amdahl (1967): decompose elapsed time'),loc='left',fontsize=13)
    axs[1].barh([1,0],[20,20],color='#9db5c3',label=tr('保持不变的部分','Unchanged work'))
    axs[1].barh([1,0],[80,8],left=[20,20],color='#b4482e',label=tr('加速的部分','Accelerated work'))
    axs[1].set_yticks([1,0],tr(['原流程','局部加速 10 倍'],['Original','Local 10× speedup']))
    axs[1].set_xlabel(tr('教学时间预算 / s','Illustrative time budget / s'));axs[1].legend(frameon=False,loc='lower right',fontsize=10)
    axs[1].text(29,0,'100 / 28 ≈ 3.57',va='center',fontsize=13);axs[1].set_title(tr('B  80% 工作加速后的整体变化','B  Accelerating 80% of the original work'),loc='left',fontsize=13)
    save(fig,'amdahl-budget')
    print(json.dumps(summary))


if __name__=='__main__':main()
```

默认运行会进行新的计时。`--timing-input` 可以读取明确指定的一份既有计时记录，以便为同一批测量生成另一种语言的图；这个模式仍会重新核对计数结果。页面中的中英图使用同一份基准记录，因此比较关系一致。Python 与 NumPy 版本同方法、数组规模、单位和测量定义一起保存，为后来比较不同运行记录提供一致的依据。

查看输出时，先确认四点例子的答案为 2，三个方法在各个规模下计数相同，再读时间与内存。800 点的计数为 9106，完整广播的两个命名浮点数组为 15360000 字节，64 行分块对应 1228800 字节。将这些可以由定义和形状核对的量与实际运行时间一起保存，能区分算法语义、内存规模和机器上的执行表现。三者互相联系，但各自回答不同问题。

## 在点对矩阵中看见分块，再选择下一步改进

交互把点数、块大小、当前处理块和实际计时记录放在同一工作区。改变点数后，二维位置图、点对计数和方法比较同步更新；改变块大小后，矩阵中当前处理的行带、命名数组大小与对应的计时分布一起变化。矩阵的横轴和纵轴都是点编号，主对角线上方对应只计一次的无序点对。移动当前块可以观察一个完整矩阵怎样被逐段覆盖，而科学计数定义始终保持不变。

### 把点对工作分成可见的行带

[Figure: 二维坐标与当前块的点](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p28/#P28-points)

[Figure: 点对上三角矩阵与工作行带](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p28/#P28-matrix)

[Figure: 同点数下六种配置的七次实际计时](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p28/#P28-timing)

可以先在 800 点时比较 16、64 和 128 行分块，查看内存随工作块改变，计时却未必按同一比例变化。再切到 100 点，观察完整广播和分块之间的差距。这些结果提醒我们用目标任务规模来评估实现。若数据继续增大，两两枚举本身可能成为主要成本，此时可以研究网格划分、邻居表或树结构，让计算集中到可能接近的点；那属于改变搜索策略，需要重新设计适用条件与独立检查。

实际项目中的改进顺序可以沿着本章的证据展开：明确计算对象，保存能独立核对的测试，测量完整流程，选择占时较多的部分，再比较保持结果一致的实现。运行时间和内存都记录下来，后续换数据或改环境时继续沿用同样定义。这样，效率改进成为科学程序可解释的一部分，而不是一组脱离输入规模的速度数字。

# Finding and Improving Performance Bottlenecks

Source: https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p28/en/
Language: en

Use one neighbor-pair problem to connect measured time, array shapes, memory, and the effect of a local improvement on the whole task.

## Understand the work before making it faster

A program that finishes almost immediately for a hundred particle positions may require a noticeable wait for thousands. This change is common in microscopy tracking, structural analysis, and spatial-neighborhood calculations: identifying nearby objects requires many position comparisons. Improving performance begins by connecting the scientific question to the number of operations and the shapes of the data. Measure where time is spent, then choose an implementation suited to that work. The resulting improvement can explain both the present example and what happens when the dataset grows.

This chapter compares three implementations of one task: Python nested loops, full NumPy broadcasting, and a NumPy calculation processed in row blocks. The input is explicitly generated two-dimensional teaching data in a square of side 10 μm. The task counts unordered pairs separated by strictly less than 1 μm. All methods must return the same integer before their time and memory use are compared. In the saved record for 800 points, all methods find 9106 pairs. Median single-call times are approximately 130.47, 8.90, and 5.47 ms, with the last result using 64-row blocks. Seven actual timings remain visible alongside their representative values.

Time and memory should be considered together. Full broadcasting passes many scalar operations to NumPy but creates intermediate arrays that grow with the square of the point count. Blocking processes a subset of pairs at a time and reuses working space. These methods compare the same pairs with different organization. Understanding that relationship supports an informed choice among broadcasting, blocking, and later spatial-index methods, rather than treating fewer visible loops as the sole criterion for an implementation.

## Fix the counting definition before comparing implementations

Each point has horizontal and vertical coordinates in μm. Differences between two points form the perpendicular sides of a right triangle, so squared distance is the sum of their squares. Because the task asks whether distance is below a positive radius, comparing squared distance to squared radius preserves the ordering and avoids a square-root operation for every pair. Coordinates and radius must use the same length unit.

$$
d_{ij}^2=(x_i-x_j)^2+(y_i-y_j)^2,\qquad d_{ij}^2<r^2
$$

| Symbol | Meaning and units |
| --- | --- |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/4ce29d83e8648088fa2af7b9.svg) | Euclidean distance between points i and j, μm |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/5e1d0f9befd63fa0c25bf752.svg) | horizontal and vertical coordinates of both points, μm |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/3a4ef1c1b261a53f9c45d0c9.svg) | positive neighborhood radius, μm |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/1f848077b31e64f57fc97f4b.svg) | dimensionless point indices; only pairs with j greater than i are counted |

Coordinate differences form the perpendicular sides of a right triangle. Squaring preserves the ordering of nonnegative distances and a positive radius, avoiding a square root for every pair. Points (0,0) and (1,0) have squared distance 1 μm², less than 1.1²=1.21 μm². Points (1,0) and (0,1) have squared distance 2 μm² and do not qualify.

An unordered pair is counted once: exchanging point i and point j leaves the same pair. A point is not paired with itself. Nested loops implement this by beginning j at i+1. A full distance matrix is symmetric about its diagonal, so selecting the upper triangle above that diagonal implements the same rule. With blocks, local row numbers must be translated back into global point indices before retaining columns greater than rows. Array shapes differ, while the identity of the counted objects stays fixed.

An independent check uses four positions that can be inspected by hand: (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), and (3,3), all in μm, with radius 1.1 μm. The origin is one micrometre from each of the next two points. Those two points are approximately 1.414 μm apart, and the distant point creates no qualifying pair. The answer is therefore two. The program verifies that all implementations return two before processing larger generated datasets. As in the preceding chapter, an implementation-independent scientific reference precedes the performance comparison.

## Distinguish locating expensive work from timing implementations

A profiler answers which functions account for elapsed work. The example's `analyze_frame` calculates a coordinate center, counts neighboring pairs, and calculates mean radial distance. `cProfile` records calls and timing, while `pstats` organizes the results by cumulative time. Cumulative time includes called functions; self time describes work inside the function itself. Read the report in terms of scientific operations before investigating individual lines. If most time is spent reading many small files, improving an already quick array addition will have little effect on the overall wait.

For implementation benchmarks, the example uses `timeit.repeat`. Coordinates are generated before timing, and each method receives the same array, radius, and counting definition. Every configuration runs seven times, recording one call per repetition. Profiling adds recording overhead, so profiled timings are kept separate from the benchmark. The distinction resembles using one measurement arrangement to locate stages in a process and another to compare outcomes under matched conditions.

![Measured timings with equal coordinates and counting definitions: medians across point counts and seven individual calls at 800 points.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/8573f4176c6b7d1e27cffefb.svg?v=8573f4176c6b)

Figure 1Measured timings with equal coordinates and counting definitions: medians across point counts and seven individual calls at 800 points.

Scheduling, cache state, and current resource use can affect timings. Retaining the full collection makes a representative value easier to interpret. We report the median while also saving the minimum and all seven measurements. The median occupies the middle of the sorted values and is less affected by a few slow runs. The minimum provides a view of execution with less external interruption. A logarithmic time axis displays the range of durations clearly, while the second panel shows every repetition. The graph describes this saved record; rerunning the program produces a new record for the current environment.

Include workload size in the comparison. Increasing the point count from 100 to 800 increases the number of unordered pairs much more rapidly because every point is compared with many others. Repeating the same measurement across sizes reveals when allocation or block size begins to affect the result. A concise small-array expression may create substantial temporary data at larger sizes. Conversely, loop overhead introduced by blocking may outweigh its memory benefit on a small task.

## Follow broadcasting through the array shapes

The coordinate array has shape `(N, 2)`. `points[:, None, :]` adds a length-one middle axis, producing `(N, 1, 2)`; `points[None, :, :]` produces `(1, N, 2)`. Subtraction broadcasts across the two point-index axes and returns `(N, N, 2)`. Its first two axes identify a pair and its last axis contains horizontal and vertical differences. The shape corresponds directly to the scientific object and immediately tells us how many floating-point values must be stored.

`np.einsum('ijk,ijk->ij', delta, delta)` multiplies each coordinate difference by itself and sums over the last coordinate axis. Here i and j identify points and k identifies coordinate direction. Retaining i and j gives an `(N, N)` squared-distance matrix. Elementwise squaring followed by summation expresses the same mathematics, although it can create an additional temporary squared array. Understanding the axes makes it possible to inspect a result's shape and determine whether reduction occurred over the intended dimension.

Broadcasting often improves this calculation because repeated operations move into NumPy's lower-level array loops, reducing the overhead of interpreting Python statements for each element. Pairwise work still exists. The difference array stores information for point pairs, followed by distance and Boolean-selection arrays. Two questions therefore belong in an assessment: does lower-level execution reduce interpreter overhead, and do intermediate arrays fit the intended scale? Timing addresses the first, while memory analysis addresses the second.

## Control working space with blocks

Full broadcasting retains coordinate differences and squared distances. Each pair needs two floating-point differences and one squared distance. With eight bytes per float64 value, the two named arrays use twenty-four bytes per pair and grow quadratically with N. This calculation describes particular arrays. Boolean selections, indices, and other objects add to the measured peak. Placing a storage formula next to an actual memory measurement shows which part of the allocation is explained by array shapes.

$$
M_{\mathrm{full}}=24N^2\ \mathrm{bytes},\qquad M_{\mathrm{block}}=24BN\ \mathrm{bytes}
$$

| Symbol | Meaning and units |
| --- | --- |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/38162b15af75aabe566b89b0.svg) | combined storage of the named difference and squared-distance floating-point arrays, bytes |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/256531b7f0ddb14dd11a59a3.svg) | number of points, dimensionless count |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/7533ad047439b7d799dd7afe.svg) | row count of a full working block, no larger than N, dimensionless count |

A pair stores two coordinate differences and one squared distance: three float64 values at eight bytes each, giving 24 bytes. N=800 uses 15360000 bytes, approximately 14.648 MiB after division by 1048576. B=64 uses 1228800 bytes, approximately 1.172 MiB. A partial final block uses its actual row count. Boolean arrays, indices, and runtime allocations contribute separately to the traced peak.

![Shape-based storage for the two named floating-point arrays and independent tracemalloc peaks. One MiB is 1048576 bytes; peaks also include other traced allocations.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/ebd9dd256f20ba6db476e799.svg?v=ebd9dd256f20)

Figure 2Shape-based storage for the two named floating-point arrays and independent tracemalloc peaks. One MiB is 1048576 bytes; peaks also include other traced allocations.

Blocking divides the first point-index axis into groups of B rows. Comparing one group with all N points creates differences of shape `(B, N, 2)` and squared distances of shape `(B, N)`. After counting qualifying pairs, the program releases those arrays and processes the next block. When B is smaller than N, named floating-point storage grows with B times N rather than allocating N times N at once. For N=800 and B=64, those arrays total 1228800 bytes, compared with 15360000 bytes for the full calculation. Global indices still remove duplicate pairs, so the final count remains 9106.

The example separately runs each calculation under `tracemalloc`, labeling its result as a traced peak allocation. This quantity has a different definition from a process's total resident memory. Memory tracking runs separately from the seven timing repetitions so its overhead does not enter the benchmark. Different block sizes produce different working-array sizes. Small blocks require more loop iterations, while large blocks create more temporary storage. Combining measurements with a memory budget helps identify a useful range for the intended workload.

## Amdahl's question: what does a local tenfold improvement change?

In 1967, Gene Amdahl discussed large-scale computing capabilities by considering accelerated and unchanged portions of a program together. The reasoning remains useful for scientific scripts. An analysis can include reading, cleaning, fitting, and plotting in addition to neighbor counting. Improving one function leaves other work to be completed. Measuring their relative contributions helps identify which change will have the largest effect on the complete task.

Let a fraction p of the original runtime be work that becomes s times faster. The remaining fraction keeps its original duration. Adding the unchanged time to the shortened target time gives the new total; dividing the old total by that value gives overall speedup. This model describes a fixed workload and assumes the modification does not alter the cost of other stages. The following time budget is an explicitly illustrative calculation, identified separately from the actual benchmark measurements.

$$
S=\frac{1}{(1-p)+p/s}
$$

| Symbol | Meaning and units |
| --- | --- |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/4d93e1f4798eafa4154488df.svg) | overall speedup, original total time divided by new total time, dimensionless |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/48c7b594e8628a17b991d4e6.svg) | fraction of original runtime spent in the target part, between zero and one |
| ![Formula](https://ml-biomat.com/static/agent-math/b8208c8407bd0942fcaa88f9.svg) | speedup of the target part, at least one here, dimensionless |

Normalize original total time to one. Unchanged work still needs 1−p, and target work falls from p to p/s. Their sum is the new total, so dividing one by it gives S. With p=0.8 and s=10, the new fraction is 0.2+0.08=0.28 and S≈3.571. An illustrative 100-second task becomes 20+8=28 seconds. Workload and the cost of other stages remain fixed.

![Original illustration of Amdahl time decomposition. The 100-to-28-second budget is a teaching calculation, identified separately from measured benchmark timings.](https://ml-biomat.com/static/tutorials/python-scientific/figures/642fc54d086a81c979b98f6c.svg?v=642fc54d086a)

Figure 3Original illustration of Amdahl time decomposition. The 100-to-28-second budget is a teaching calculation, identified separately from measured benchmark timings.

For example, a hundred-second workflow might contain eighty seconds of target computation and twenty seconds of other work. Making the target ten times faster reduces it to eight seconds, giving a twenty-eight-second total and an overall speedup of approximately 3.57. Improving that eight-second portion further still leaves the twenty-second remainder. Performance work therefore returns repeatedly to the complete workflow: once one calculation is fast enough, reading or output may become the next useful target. The historical architectural question retains the same clear time relationship inside a Python analysis.

## Keep timing records, memory measurements, and numerical checks

The complete program generates teaching coordinates with a fixed random seed, performs the independent four-point check, and compares nested loops, full broadcasting, and four block sizes at 100, 200, 400, and 800 points. Each configuration first checks count agreement, then saves seven timings and a separately measured memory peak. Inputs, scientific calculations, and measurement arrangements are visible in one file. Outputs include `benchmark.json`, `profile.txt`, `summary.json`, and three scientific figures. The benchmark retains individual repetitions for later distribution plots or inspection of unusual runs.

### Compare equal computations using timing, memory, and an overall time budget

Run seven timing repetitions and independent memory tracking; an explicitly supplied prior record can generate another-language figures.

```
"""Compare equal neighbor-pair calculations using measured time and memory.

Coordinates are generated teaching data in a 10 um square. Timing samples are
local measurements; memory formulas describe named buffers rather than RSS.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import cProfile
import io
import json
import platform
import pstats
import timeit
import tracemalloc
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager



def available_plot_fonts():
    """Choose installed fonts; keep a Latin fallback on every platform."""
    choices = ["Noto Sans CJK SC", "Noto Sans SC", "Microsoft YaHei", "SimHei", "DejaVu Sans"]
    installed = {font.name for font in font_manager.fontManager.ttflist}
    return [name for name in choices if name in installed]



def pair_count_loop(points, radius):
    count=0;limit=radius*radius
    for i in range(len(points)):
        for j in range(i+1,len(points)):
            dx=points[i,0]-points[j,0];dy=points[i,1]-points[j,1]
            if dx*dx+dy*dy < limit:count+=1
    return count


def pair_count_full(points,radius):
    delta=points[:,None,:]-points[None,:,:]
    squared=np.einsum('ijk,ijk->ij',delta,delta)
    return int(np.count_nonzero(np.triu(squared < radius*radius,k=1)))


def pair_count_blocked(points,radius,block=64):
    count=0;n=len(points);columns=np.arange(n)[None,:]
    for start in range(0,n,block):
        stop=min(start+block,n)
        delta=points[start:stop,None,:]-points[None,:,:]
        squared=np.einsum('ijk,ijk->ij',delta,delta)
        rows=np.arange(start,stop)[:,None]
        count+=int(np.count_nonzero((squared < radius*radius)&(columns>rows)))
        del delta,squared
    return count


def measured_peak(function):
    tracemalloc.start()
    result=function()
    _,peak=tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()
    tracemalloc.stop()
    return result,int(peak)


def analyze_frame(points,radius):
    """A small scientific workload for function-level profiling."""
    center=points.mean(axis=0)
    centered=points-center
    pairs=pair_count_loop(centered,radius)
    radial=np.sqrt(np.einsum('ij,ij->i',centered,centered))
    return {'center':center.tolist(),'pairs':pairs,'mean_radius_um':float(radial.mean())}


def main():
    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__);ap.add_argument('--output',type=Path,required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--language',choices=['zh','en'],default='en')
    ap.add_argument('--timing-input',type=Path,help='Reuse an explicitly saved benchmark for an alternative-language figure')
    args=ap.parse_args();out=args.output;out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);zh=args.language=='zh';tr=lambda a,b:a if zh else b
    sizes=[100,200,400,800];blocks=[16,32,64,128];radius=1.0
    points=np.random.default_rng(2819).uniform(0,10,size=(max(sizes),2))
    hand=np.array([[0.,0.],[1.,0.],[0.,1.],[3.,3.]])
    assert pair_count_loop(hand,1.1)==pair_count_full(hand,1.1)==pair_count_blocked(hand,1.1,2)==2
    if args.timing_input:
        benchmark=json.loads(args.timing_input.read_text(encoding='utf8'))
        assert benchmark['seed']==2819 and benchmark['sizes']==sizes
        records=benchmark['records']
    else:
        records=[]
        for n in sizes:
            x=points[:n];reference=pair_count_loop(x,radius)
            methods=[('loop',0,lambda x=x:pair_count_loop(x,radius)),('full',n,lambda x=x:pair_count_full(x,radius))]
            methods += [('blocked',b,lambda x=x,b=b:pair_count_blocked(x,radius,b)) for b in blocks]
            for method,block,fn in methods:
                assert fn()==reference
                samples=timeit.repeat(fn,number=1,repeat=7)
                result,peak=measured_peak(fn)
                assert result==reference
                records.append({'n':n,'method':method,'block':block,'pairs':result,'seconds':samples,
                                'median_seconds':float(np.median(samples)),'minimum_seconds':min(samples),
                                'traced_peak_bytes':peak,'named_float_buffers_bytes':0 if method=='loop' else 24*n*min(block,n)})
        benchmark={'seed':2819,'sizes':sizes,'radius_um':radius,'python':platform.python_version(),
                   'numpy':np.__version__,'timing_definition':'seven independent timeit runs, one call per run',
                   'memory_definition':'separate tracemalloc peak; named buffers are float64 delta and squared distances',
                   'records':records}
    # Every run still independently checks the saved reference computations.
    for n in sizes:
        expected=next(r['pairs'] for r in records if r['n']==n)
        assert pair_count_full(points[:n],radius)==pair_count_blocked(points[:n],radius,64)==expected
    (out/'benchmark.json').write_text(json.dumps(benchmark,indent=2),encoding='utf8')
    profile=cProfile.Profile();profile_result=profile.runcall(analyze_frame,points[:400],radius)
    assert profile_result['pairs']==next(r['pairs'] for r in records if r['n']==400)
    stream=io.StringIO();pstats.Stats(profile,stream=stream).strip_dirs().sort_stats('cumulative').print_stats(8)
    (out/'profile.txt').write_text(stream.getvalue(),encoding='utf8')
    largest=[r for r in records if r['n']==800]
    summary={'hand_checked_pairs':2,'sizes':sizes,'pair_counts':{str(n):next(r['pairs'] for r in records if r['n']==n) for n in sizes},
             'all_methods_agree':True,'repeats':7,'largest_full_named_buffers_bytes':24*800*800,
             'largest_block64_named_buffers_bytes':24*800*64,'amdahl_p08_s10':1/(.2+.8/10)}
    (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary,indent=2),encoding='utf8')
    (out/'lab-data.json').write_text(json.dumps({'points':points.tolist(),'radius':radius,'records':records}),encoding='utf8')
    plt.rcParams.update({'font.family':available_plot_fonts(),'font.size':12,'svg.fonttype':'none','figure.facecolor':'#faf9f5','axes.facecolor':'#faf9f5','axes.spines.top':False,'axes.spines.right':False})
    colors={'loop':'#b4482e','full':'#205b8c','blocked':'#2b7c73'}
    def save(fig,name):
        fig.savefig(out/f'{name}-{args.language}.svg',metadata={'Date':None});fig.savefig(out/f'{name}-{args.language}.png',dpi=150);plt.close(fig)
    fig,axs=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12.4,5.3),layout='constrained',gridspec_kw={'width_ratios':[1.1,1]})
    for method in ['loop','full','blocked']:
        selected=[r for r in records if r['method']==method and (method!='blocked' or r['block']==64)]
        label=tr({'loop':'Python 双循环','full':'完整广播','blocked':'64 行分块'}[method],{'loop':'Python loops','full':'Full broadcast','blocked':'64-row blocks'}[method])
        axs[0].plot([r['n'] for r in selected],[r['median_seconds']*1000 for r in selected],'-o',color=colors[method],label=label)
        r=next(r for r in selected if r['n']==800);i=['loop','full','blocked'].index(method)
        axs[1].scatter(np.full(7,i)+np.linspace(-.1,.1,7),np.array(r['seconds'])*1000,color=colors[method],s=35)
        axs[1].hlines(r['median_seconds']*1000,i-.24,i+.24,color=colors[method],lw=3)
    axs[0].set(xscale='log',yscale='log',xlabel=tr('点数 N','Point count N'),ylabel=tr('单次中位时间 / ms','Median time per call / ms'))
    axs[0].set_xticks(sizes,[str(n) for n in sizes]);axs[0].xaxis.set_minor_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.NullFormatter())
    axs[0].legend(frameon=False,fontsize=11);axs[0].set_title(tr('A  相同输入与计数定义','A  Equal inputs and counting definitions'),loc='left')
    axs[1].set_yscale('log');axs[1].set_xticks(range(3),tr(['双循环','完整广播','64 行分块'],['Loops','Full','Block 64']))
    axs[1].set_ylabel(tr('单次时间 / ms（7 次）','Time per call / ms (7 runs)'));axs[1].set_title(tr('B  N = 800 的实际重复测量','B  Actual repeated timings at N = 800'),loc='left')
    for ax in axs:ax.grid(axis='y',alpha=.2)
    save(fig,'measured-timings')
    fig,axs=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12.4,5.2),layout='constrained');nn=np.array(sizes)
    axs[0].plot(nn,24*nn**2/2**20,'-o',color=colors['full'],label=tr('完整浮点数组','Full floating-point buffers'))
    axs[0].plot(nn,24*nn*64/2**20,'-o',color=colors['blocked'],label=tr('64 行浮点分块','64-row floating-point buffers'))
    axs[0].set(xlabel=tr('点数 N','Point count N'),ylabel=tr('命名浮点数组大小 / MiB','Named floating-point buffers / MiB'));axs[0].legend(frameon=False,fontsize=10)
    rows=[r for r in largest if r['method']=='full' or (r['method']=='blocked' and r['block'] in [16,64,128])]
    x=np.arange(len(rows));axs[1].bar(x-.17,[r['named_float_buffers_bytes']/2**20 for r in rows],width=.34,color='#a5bfce',label=tr('两个命名数组','Two named arrays'))
    axs[1].bar(x+.17,[r['traced_peak_bytes']/2**20 for r in rows],width=.34,color='#205b8c',label=tr('tracemalloc 峰值','tracemalloc peak'))
    axs[1].set_xticks(x,[('Full' if r['method']=='full' else f"B={r['block']}") for r in rows]);axs[1].set_ylabel(tr('追踪/计算内存 / MiB','Traced/calculated memory / MiB'));axs[1].legend(frameon=False,fontsize=10)
    axs[0].set_title(tr('A  保存形状决定增长规律','A  Stored shapes determine growth'),loc='left');axs[1].set_title(tr('B  N = 800：数组与实际峰值','B  N = 800: arrays and measured peaks'),loc='left')
    save(fig,'memory-growth')
    fig,axs=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12.4,5.2),layout='constrained');accelerations=np.linspace(1,50,250)
    for p,color in [(.5,'#205b8c'),(.8,'#b4482e'),(.95,'#2b7c73')]:
        axs[0].plot(accelerations,1/((1-p)+p/accelerations),color=color,label=f'p = {p}')
    axs[0].set(xlabel=tr('目标部分的加速倍数 s','Speedup s of the selected part'),ylabel=tr('整体加速倍数 S','Overall speedup S'));axs[0].legend(frameon=False)
    axs[0].set_title(tr('A  Amdahl（1967）的时间分解思想','A  Amdahl (1967): decompose elapsed time'),loc='left',fontsize=13)
    axs[1].barh([1,0],[20,20],color='#9db5c3',label=tr('保持不变的部分','Unchanged work'))
    axs[1].barh([1,0],[80,8],left=[20,20],color='#b4482e',label=tr('加速的部分','Accelerated work'))
    axs[1].set_yticks([1,0],tr(['原流程','局部加速 10 倍'],['Original','Local 10× speedup']))
    axs[1].set_xlabel(tr('教学时间预算 / s','Illustrative time budget / s'));axs[1].legend(frameon=False,loc='lower right',fontsize=10)
    axs[1].text(29,0,'100 / 28 ≈ 3.57',va='center',fontsize=13);axs[1].set_title(tr('B  80% 工作加速后的整体变化','B  Accelerating 80% of the original work'),loc='left',fontsize=13)
    save(fig,'amdahl-budget')
    print(json.dumps(summary))


if __name__=='__main__':main()
```

The default run performs a new benchmark. `--timing-input` accepts an explicitly identified previous record when another-language figure is needed for the same measurements; that mode still rechecks pair counts. The Chinese and English figures on this page use one benchmark record, preserving the comparison across languages. Python and NumPy versions accompany method names, input sizes, units, and measurement definitions so that later results can be compared on a consistent basis.

Inspect the outputs in order: confirm the four-point answer of two, confirm agreement across methods for each size, then read time and memory. The 800-point count is 9106. The full method's two named floating-point arrays occupy 15360000 bytes, while 64-row blocks use 1228800 bytes. Retaining quantities derivable from definitions and shapes alongside timings separates algorithmic meaning, storage scale, and observed execution behavior. Each contributes a different part of the performance explanation.

## See the blocks inside the pair matrix

The interactive workspace connects point count, block size, the current block, and measured timing records. Changing the number of points updates positions, pair count, and method comparisons. Changing block size updates the highlighted matrix rows, named-buffer size, and corresponding timing distribution. Both matrix axes are point indices; the upper triangle represents unordered pairs counted once. Move the current block to inspect how a matrix is covered progressively while the counting definition stays fixed.

### Divide pairwise work into visible row blocks

[Figure: Coordinates and points in the current row block](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p28/en/#P28-points)

[Figure: Upper-triangular pair matrix and working row band](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p28/en/#P28-matrix)

[Figure: Seven actual timings for six configurations at the selected point count](https://ml-biomat.com/tutorials/python-scientific/p28/en/#P28-timing)

At 800 points, compare blocks of 16, 64, and 128 rows. Storage changes with block size, while timings need not follow the same proportion. Switch to 100 points and examine the difference between full broadcasting and blocking. The intended workload size belongs in an implementation decision. If data grow much further, enumerating all pairs may itself become the main cost. Grid partitions, neighbor lists, or tree structures can concentrate work on potentially nearby points; changing the search strategy calls for new applicability conditions and independent checks.

A practical improvement follows the evidence developed here: define the objects being counted, preserve independent tests, measure the full workflow, select an expensive component, and compare implementations that retain the same result. Record both time and memory, then reuse the definitions when inputs or computing environments change. Performance becomes an explainable property of a scientific program, connected to its actual workload.
